title: Jonathan Taylor is active for the Colts on Sunday
summary: Running back Jonathan Taylor may not be a member of the Colts at this time next week, but he will be in their lineup in Jacksonville on Sunday.
full_text: Running back Jonathan Taylor may not be a member of the Colts at this time next week, but he will be in their lineup in Jacksonville on Sunday. Taylor is active for the Colts as they try to improve on their 2-5 record in a divisional matchup with the Jaguars. The last few days have seen several reports that the Colts have stepped up talks with other clubs about trading Taylor and that gave rise to speculation that they might hold him out of the lineup in order to avoid an injury that would close the door on that possibility. Arizona took that step with wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. before dealing him to the Texans last month. The Colts are taking the other route and any potential trade will likely require Taylor to come through Sunday's game unscathed. The Colts aren't holding wide receiver Josh Downs either. Downs requested a trade this week as he plays out the final year of his current contract as part of a Colts team that has already traded away guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner.
author: Josh Alper

author: Josh Alper

title: Mike Macdonald hasn't committed to Jadarian Price playing on Monday
summary: When the Seahawks' final injury report, issued on Saturday, had both running back Zach Charbonnet and running back Jadarian Price free from any designation for Monday night's game against the Bears, it created the impression that both will play.
full_text: When the Seahawks' final injury report, issued on Saturday, had both running back Zach Charbonnet and running back Jadarian Price free from any designation for Monday night's game against the Bears, it created the impression that both will play . Not so fast. Charbonnet, who has been activated from the physically unable to perform list, is good to go — unless he's a healthy scratch, for some reason. Price remains on injured reserve, due to the chest injury he suffered in Week 3. "We have a plan for Zach and with JD," coach Mike Macdonald told reporters on Saturday, "if we were to make a move, that would happen on Monday to my knowledge. We’ll see if that’s what we do. We have some things going on roster wise that we’re working through right now, but we have a plan for Zach.” Asked later about Price not yet being activated from IR, Macdonald said, "We’re going to let the transaction speak for itself on that one.” The vague comments from Macdonald have prompted some to speculate that the Seahawks are trying to trade for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. The more likely explanation is that Macdonald knows that activating Price will require cutting a player currently on the team. It most likely puts one of the running backs at risk. Beyond Charbonnet, the Seahawks have Emanuel Wilson (who rushed for 100 yards in the Week 7 win over the Chiefs), George Holani, Velus Jones Jr., and Robert Henry Jr. on the active roster. Henry was inactive last week. Jones had nine offensive snaps and nine special-teams plays. One of those two would likely get the short straw if/when the Seahawks activate Price on Monday. With Charbonnet and Price healthy, the Seahawks suddenly have plenty of quality options. They'll likely be careful with Charbonnet, who tore an ACL in January. Price had 52 yards rushing in each of the first two games of the season, before suffering his injury at Washington. Regardless, Price remains on IR and doesn't have to be restored to the roster for at least two more weeks. They possibly will decide to let it ride for now, with Wilson, Charbonnet, Holani, Jones, and Henry as the running backs on the 53-man roster.
author: Mike Florio

title: Eagles reportedly won't trade Saquon Barkley
summary: At a time when some believe the Eagles are in a soft tank, their subtle effort to secure better round-by-round draft position in 2027 won't include getting an extra draft pick or two for running back Saquon Barkley.
full_text: At a time when some believe the Eagles are in a soft tank, their subtle effort to secure better round-by-round draft position in 2027 won't include getting an extra draft pick or two for running back Saquon Barkley. NFL Network reports that the Eagles won’t trade Barkley before the November 10 deadline. It's clear, unequivocal. The Eagles aren't playing the " no plans " game, like the Raiders are with Maxx Crosby. The Eagles, based on the report, are moving forward with Barkley. Of course, the emergence of the report nine days before the deadline could be an indication that the Eagles have realized there's no offer forthcoming that would get them to accept taking a $26 million dead-money charge for Barkley in 2027. The Eagles have already traded a veteran player, when Cam Jurgens was shipped to the Ravens in the aftermath of Lane Johnson's surprise retirement. That doesn't mean that the Eagles will have a Colts-style fire sale — especially as to any contracts that, if traded, would pour jet fuel on the cap situation next year. Given the cap consequences, it would make much more sense to trade Barkley after June 1 of 2027. Like they did when trading receiver A.J. Brown after June 1 of 2026. That move followed months of reports and claims and assertions that they wouldn't be trading Brown. So, yes, it will make plenty of sense to pay attention to any and all chatter that may emerge in the offseason, leading up to a potential June 1 move if the Eagles believe that 2027 could shape up to be another soft-tank season, too.
author: Mike Florio

title: The new allegations against Josh Jacobs could create a credibility issue
summary: Friday's release of police records in the Josh Jacobs case brought to light allegations made by three other women against the Packers running back.
full_text: Friday's release of police records in the Josh Jacobs case brought to light allegations made by three other women against the Packers running back. It also creates a problem for Jacobs, based on the things he may have said to the league. Although there has been no indication that the league has summoned Jacobs to Manhattan for a formal interview in advance of the potential imposition of discipline (that's often the final step in the investigation), it's possible — if not likely — that the NFL has had conversations with Jacobs before and/or during his six-game stint on paid leave. One obvious question to ask Jacobs is whether the incident for which he pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery charges was a one-time thing, or whether it has happened before. If the question was asked, and if Jacobs said there are no other incidents, the emergence of new allegations will impact his credibility in the eyes of the league. Even if the NFL's effort to explore the new allegations goes nowhere (the league has no subpoena power to compel cooperation by the others who spoke to the authorities in Wisconsin), the mere existence of three additional claims will make the league view anything Jacobs has told them more skeptically. Regardless of how it plays out, the evidence of the other claims against Jacobs reshuffles the deck, both for the league and for the Packers. The fact that they've been linked to trade talks for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor suggests that the team is already considering whether to move on from Jacobs. If they do, he could have a hard time finding a landing spot, given the new allegations. So, yes, it's a real problem for Jacobs. Even though his lawyers have issued a statement downplaying the development , it complicates his standing with the league, with the Packers, and possibly with any other team that could eventually be considering whether to offer him a roster spot, if/when he's no longer a member of the Green Bay organization.
author: Mike Florio

title: Colts will take calculated risk, if Jonathan Taylor plays today
summary: The NFL's injury report places no obligation on teams to disclose that a player will be a healthy scratch.
full_text: The NFL's injury report places no obligation on teams to disclose that a player will be a healthy scratch. The world finds out if a player who is able to play otherwise won't be playing roughly 90 minutes before kickoff, when the team supplies its list of inactive players. For the Colts, there's a decision to be made later this morning. Will running back Jonathan Taylor play at Jacksonville, as they continue to engage in talks aimed at trading him? (The Giants are definitely making a play to get him, and others presumably are, too.) By all indications, Taylor will play. But if the phone rings before 11:30 a.m. ET and the Colts get an offer they choose not to refuse, the plan could quickly change. (And since the Giants don't have a game this weekend, they can focus their efforts exclusively on trying to get it done, even if it takes a call from coach John Harbaugh to owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon.) Three weeks ago, the Cardinals knew on Friday that they'd be trading receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. after Sunday's game. Harrison didn't play. It's possible that one of the teams interested in Taylor will put the right terms on the table in order to persuade the Colts to put Taylor in bubble wrap for Sunday pending a post-game announcement that Taylor will be changing teams. Without a deal in place imminently, the Colts will be taking a calculated risk if Taylor is active. If he gets injured, the trade market will evaporate. Like it did on Friday for the Commanders and defensive tackle Daron Payne. There were trade talks regarding Payne, until he suffered a season-ending foot injury in practice. So even though the trade deadline doesn't arrive until November 10, there are various other deadlines that could drive a trade decision. For the Colts, the most immediate deadline arrives very soon, when they have to decide whether to let Taylor play and risk an injury that would necessarily close the door on a potential trade.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Raiders have "no plans" to trade Maxx Crosby (again)
summary: The Raiders traded defensive end Maxx Crosby in March.
full_text: The Raiders traded defensive end Maxx Crosby in March. They won't be trading him in November. Unless they do. The official word from Adam Schefter of ESPN is that the Raiders have " no plans " to trade Crosby. We've heard that message plenty of times over the years from teams that had "no intent" or "no intention" or "no plan" to trade a player. Until they traded him. It happened this week. The Titans had no plans to trade defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, until they did. They reportedly decided to start listening to the inquiries they were receiving on Tuesday. Two days later, Simmons was in Chicago. The simple reality is that teams that want Crosby will keep calling the Raiders. If the Raiders lose the next two games before the deadline and fall to 3-6, maybe they'll decide to do what they already decided to do in March. The trade of Crosby to the Ravens for a pair of first-round picks fell apart after the Ravens decided they weren't comfortable with the condition of his surgically-repaired knee. Still, it shows that the Raiders have already crossed the mental bridge required to pull the pin on a trade. If they did it in March, why wouldn't they do it now — if they get an offer they like? The problem is that whatever they get now will be compared to what they could have gotten in March. If it's less than two first-round picks, it could be a challenge to sell the move to the fan base. Or maybe not. After four straight losses, reality has set in for the once 3-0 Raiders. They still have plenty of holes on the roster. Trading Crosby would give them the ability to add young, cheap players. And it would free up cash and cap space to pay other veterans. Even if it's less than two ones, it's more than keeping Crosby through the never-ending rebuild. In trading Simmons, the Titans added two first-round picks and avoided the bulk of his $105 million extension. The Titans need players, and the Simmons trade will become five or six. The Raiders could do something similar with Crosby, because they need players, too. For now, they have "no plans." We now wait to see whether, over the next nine days, their plans change. And what, you say, of the notion that Crosby doesn't want to go? Absent a no-trade clause, he won't have much of a choice. And if/when he lands with a contender, it's hard to imagine that he'd have many complaints.
author: Mike Florio

title: Breece Hall is not expected to play against Raiders
summary: The Jets are set to play without running back Breece Hall again this Sunday.
full_text: ' The Jets are set to play without running back Breece Hall again this Sunday. Hall has missed the last four games with a quad injury and Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that he is expected to be inactive against the Raiders. Hall has been practicing on a limited basis for the last two weeks and he's been listed as questionable, but it appears the wait for his return will continue. Braelon Allen has been the Jets' lead back in Hall's absence. He has 72 carries for 357 yards and a touchdown during his time in the starting lineup. The Jets are also likely to be without linebacker David Bailey. The first-round pick is listed as doubtful due to a groin injury.
author: Josh Alper

title: Thank you for 25 years (get ready for 25 more)
summary: From November 1, 2001, to November 1, 2026. And beyond.
full_text: ' It was November 1, 2001. I woke up. I wrote a few blurbs about what was going on in the NFL. I pressed the button. And off we went. It is November 1, 2026. And here we are. We wouldn't be here if you weren't reading the stuff we write. It's that simple. Those of you who were around back then had plenty of other options for your time and attention. You've got even more options now. But enough of you have kept coming back (and enough of you have found us in the past 25 years) to keep the lights on, and then some. After five years of dogpaddling (I quit for a day or so in 2002 because I thought it would never really turn into anything), Sprint came along with a sponsorship deal that made it clear that, sooner or later, PFT would stop being a hobby and start being a full-time job. I remember not wanting it to become a job, because I didn't want it to ever feel like a job. Even now, it usually doesn't. Even when it does, it's better than every other job I ever had, by a long shot. None of it happens if you aren't out there, reading the stuff we write, watching PFT Live /#PFTPM or the various clips we attach to the articles, and/or listening to the podcasts. It all changed in 2009 when NBC came along, in every way possible. It's been great for us and, given that NBC keeps extending our contract, presumably good for NBC. Still, it relies on you. If/when you ever decide you don't care about what we have to say, it's done. I'll keep trying to give you a reason to keep coming back. For now, we'll keep rolling. It should be a busy day, with some excellent games in the afternoon windows. And the very small token of my appreciation for the folks who have been here the longest — and for everyone else — is the fully re-written Quarterback of the Future . The introduction explains how it came to be the first time around, and its direct connection to getting this operation started in the first place. Basically, without QBF there never would have been PFT. Chapter One is live. I'll post Chapter Two later today. And one per day, or maybe more often than that, until it's all up. Far more importantly, we'll keep posting the stuff you mainly come here to read, dozens per day and, on some days like today, more than 100. So thank you. We hope you choose to stick around for the next 25 years, and beyond.
author: Mike Florio

title: Ben Johnson: Jeffery Simmons will play a lot, maybe not a full workload Monday night
summary: In seven games with the Titans this season, Jeffery Simmons was on the field for 87 percent of defensive snaps and 21 percent of special teams snaps.
full_text: In seven games with the Titans this season, Jeffery Simmons was on the field for 87 percent of defensive snaps and 21 percent of special teams snaps. Few defensive tackles in the NFL get that kind of playing time. And now that he's on the Bears, Simmons probably won't get that kind of playing time on Monday night against the Seahawks. But Bears coach Ben Johnson says Simmons might come close. Asked if Simmons will play as much on Monday night as he played each week with the Titans, Johnson said it might not be quite that much. "He might not be quite that high Week 1 for us, but he certainly has shown the ability to carry a load," Johnson said. Johnson added that he has no doubt Simmons will pick up defensive coordinator Dennis Allen's system quickly. "He's played a lot of football, he's been in a few different defensive schemes, and I think DA is going to be able to find a spot to do what he does best," Johnson said. "We don't want him thinking out there, and that's what you're conscious of coming into a new team, but he's a smart guy and we've been encouraged by what we've seen so far." Ultimately, Johnson thinks Simmons will fit in perfectly. "I just told him I want him to be himself, be his productive self," Johnson said. "He's gonna help us win."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Josh Allen going for his 102nd win counting playoffs, more than Tom Brady's first 9 seasons
summary: If Allen and the Bills win today, he'll surpass Brady for sole possession of the third-most wins in a quarterback's first nine seasons.
full_text: By his ninth season in the NFL, Tom Brady had won three Super Bowls and had an undefeated regular season, so it's surprising that any quarterback could win more games than Brady did in his first nine years in the league. Brady won 101 starts, including both the regular season and the postseason, in his first nine seasons. Bills quarterback Josh Allen also has 101 wins counting the playoffs, so if the Bills beat the Ravens today, Allen will have 102 wins, one more than Brady's total in his first nine seasons. That's still not the record, however. Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes won 112 games in his first nine seasons, and former Seahawks quarterback Russell Wilson won 107 games in his first nine seasons. So Allen needs to win today and six more times before the Bills' postseason is over to surpass Wilson for second place, and he needs to win today and 11 more times before the Bills' postseason is over to surpass Mahomes for the most wins ever in a quarterback's first nine seasons. Allen has won 93 regular-season games and eight postseason games in his career. Brady won 87 regular-season games and 14 postseason games in his first nine seasons. It's worth noting that Brady didn't start at all in his rookie season, and only started one game in his ninth season, suffering a season-ending knee injury in Week 1. Allen started 11 games as a rookie, winning five, and has only missed one game since becoming the Bills' starter. Allen is racking up an impressive career résumé, even as he still hasn't done is what Brady did more than anyone else in NFL history: Get to, and win, a Super Bowl.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Bill Belichick and UNC nearly upset No. 1 Miami
summary: Earlier this month, Bill Belichick and North Carolina got a signature win over previously-unbeaten Pitt.
full_text: ' Earlier this month, Bill Belichick and North Carolina got a signature win over previously-unbeaten Pitt. On Saturday night, Belichick and company nearly pulled off a far bigger victory. The Tar Heels kept it very close against No. 1 Miami, ultimately losing the game 38-35. North Carolina recovered two onside kicks in an effort to secure possession with less than two minutes to play, after cutting the margin to three points. The first one was wiped out by an offside penalty. The second was nullified by an illegal block. UNC led the back-and-forth game in the fourth quarter, 28-24. A pair of touchdowns (the second of which was fueled by a UNC turnover) put Miami up by 10, forcing the Tar Heels to score seven and then to attempt to execute a successful onside kick. After starting 4-2, North Carolina is now 4-4. In his second season in college football, Belichick has a record of 8-12.
author: Mike Florio

title: Joe Burrow is one four-TD, no-INT game away from elite club
summary: The 2026 Bengals have won two, lost two, and then won two.
full_text: The 2026 Bengals have won two, lost two, and then won two. In their last two, quarterback Joe Burrow has been stellar. In both the 31-24 Week 5 win over the Dolphins and the 35-13 Week 6 win over the Ravens, Burrow threw four touchdown passes and no interceptions. If he does that again on Sunday against the Titans, Burrow will expand the membership of an elite club by 50 percent. Per NBC Sports research, another four-TD, no-pick game from Burrow would make him only the third quarterback in NFL history to do it for three straight games. Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford accomplished it in 2025. Then-Packers quarterback Aaron Rodgers was the first to ever do it, in 2016. The Bengals have beaten the Titans four of five times, including a victory over Tennessee in the 2021 postseason. A win would vault the Bengals into second place in the AFC North, in front of the loser of the Browns-Steelers game. Unless they tie. In that case, the Browns and Steelers would each be 5-2-1, and the Bengals (with a win on Sunday) would be 5-2.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cowboys have a franchise-record 14 straight games with 20 or more points allowed
summary: The Dallas Cowboys have applied to themselves the nickname of "greatest offense there is."
full_text: ' The Dallas Cowboys have applied to themselves the nickname of "greatest offense there is." While that may be debatable, the team has produced another trend that can't be denied. Via NBC Sports research, the Cowboys have allowed 20 or more points in 14 straight games. It's the longest active streak in the league, and it's the longest streak in franchise history. Although on the surface the Cowboys have drawn a favorable opponent on Sunday in the 2-5 Cardinals. But, in recent years, the Cardinals have been a spur in the Dallas saddle. Arizona is 8-1 against the Cowboys, dating back to 2008. The Cardinals also have won four in a row against Dallas — and four in a row at AT&T Stadium. In 2025, Arizona's third and final win of the year came in Week 9 at Dallas, when the Cardinals beat the Cowboys, 27-17, on a Monday night.
author: Mike Florio

title: With 88 yards on Sunday, Derrick Henry will jump to No. 7 all-time in rushing yards
summary: Ravens running back Derrick Henry, who turns 33 in early January, continues to get it done at a high level.
full_text: Ravens running back Derrick Henry, who turns 33 in early January, continues to get it done at a high level. A solid performance on Sunday at Buffalo will put him ahead of a pair of Hall of Famers on the all-time rushing list. Henry enters the Week 8 game with 13,597 career rushing yards. With only 66 yards, he'll pass Jerome Bettis for No. 8 on the career list. With 88, Henry will leapfrog LaDainian Tomlinson. If, along the way, Henry scores a rushing touchdown, he'll join Hall of Famers Marshall Faulk and Marcus Allen as the only players with 40 or more rushing touchdowns with multiple teams. Faulk did it with the Colts and the Rams. Allen did it with the Raiders and the Chiefs. Henry has previously gotten there with the Titans. The overriding question for Henry is how high he can go on the career rushing list. The current record holder, Hall of Famer Emmitt Smith, believes Henry can catch and beat Smith's all-time record of 18,355 yards. Henry needs 4,758 yards to match Smith. To get there, Henry probably will have to finish 2026 strong and keep it going for four more years. By then, it's possible that Henry will be playing for a third team. It would be fitting if the Cowboys — who weren't interested when Henry became a free agent — would be the team with which Henry breaks Smith's record.
author: Mike Florio

title: As Eagles prepare for Sunday night, questions of effort from Monday night linger
summary: As the Eagles plunged to their fifth straight loss, questions emerged regarding effort, or lack thereof.
full_text: As the Eagles plunged to their fifth straight loss, questions emerged regarding effort, or lack thereof. Or, more fundamentally, whether the defensive line was even bothering to get into their stances . To no surprise, then, effort was a theme of the week, specifically when reporters had a midweek chance to pose questions to coach Nick Sirianni. Asked whether there was an issue with effort on Monday night against the Cowboys, and how the coaching staff gauges whether effort is an issue, Sirianni said this: "We grade every play based off of what they did, we grade every play based off of their assignment alignment and we grade every play off of effort. That's not only in games, but that's also at every practice, because if we were just grading it in games and not emphasizing it on every play in every practice, then we wouldn't be doing our job. "I did not see an effort issue on Monday night. Obviously, it was other things, which I'm sure you guys will ask me about. There were other things, but effort in no way, shape [or] form was an issue there. "The plays -- now, do you bat 100% on effort? No, you don't play a perfect football game. The plays, anytime there is an effort stand out in a positive way, we show it to the team and show what the standard is. Anytime there's one that we feel like there was a loaf, we point that out and show that to the team. But I didn't think that we had -- I didn't look at the tape and say, 'Hey, this was an effort issue, and this is why this play happened or that play happened.' That's how I graded the film." He later was asked whether players get grades on a weekly basis regarding topics like assignment, alignment, and effort. "That would be crazy not to tell them what they've done and what they haven't done," Sirianni said. "We go over that with them. We watch the game with them, and everything is discussed with these guys. I guess I'm a little confused by the question. If we want them to get better, we've got to go over all the mistakes and everything with it." The reporters eventually attempted to address the confusion by explaining to Sirianni the perception that effort was an issue. So what does Sirianni think about the questions in that regard? "I think in that situation, everyone's going to look to find answers in a five-game losing streak," Sirianni said. "Just because the result -- If we win that game, do they still question the effort? I don't know. I can't -- I'm not them. My job is to look at the daily process of it and the daily work and what objectively happened in that game and not react based off of the outcome. I get it. I would understand [that] everyone's looking for answers. I don't give you a lot of answers up here. I get that. I understand that. I do respect the job that you guys have to do, but I'm always going to probably keep it tight to the vest. "But again, it's not about the outcome. . . . We're outcome-aware -- but it is about the process that goes [into] it, what happens Monday through Saturday. What happens Monday through Saturday is usually what happens in the game in my experience. That's why you need great week of preparation, but I'm not letting the outcome dictate how I grade the film. I'm grading the film objectively based off of what I see on a weekly basis." What everyone sees is a team in a tailspin, with the most recent Super Bowl win fading deep into the rear-view mirror. They get their next chance to turn things around on Sunday night, when they face the 1-4-1 Commanders.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jets put DT T'Vondre Sweat on IR
summary: The Jets ruled defensive tackle T'Vondre Sweat out for Week 8 on Friday and they ruled him out for at least three more games on Saturday.
full_text: ' The Jets ruled defensive tackle T'Vondre Sweat out for Week 8 on Friday and they ruled him out for at least three more games on Saturday. Sweat has been placed on injured reserve due to the knee injury he suffered in last Sunday's loss to the Dolphins. He had 17 tackles and two tackles for loss while starting six of the team's first seven games. The Jets filled his roster spot by signing defensive tackle Payton Page off of their practice squad. He appeared in four games for the Jets last season. The Jets also announced that they have elevated offensive lineman Brian Banks and linebacker Quinton Bell from the practice squad. Bell's elevation indicates David Bailey will be inactive after being listed as doubtful with a groin injury.
author: Josh Alper

title: Seahawks RBs Zach Charbonnet, Jadarian Price will return Monday night
summary: The Seahawks will have veteran running back Zach Charbonnet and rookie running back Jadarian Price in the same game for the first time on Monday.
full_text: The Seahawks will have veteran running back Zach Charbonnet and rookie running back Jadarian Price in the same game for the first time on Monday. Neither Charbonnet nor Price has an injury designation for the game against the Bears. Charbonnet is returning from a torn ACL in his left knee that ended his season on his fifth carry in the divisional round of the 2025 playoffs. He underwent surgery on Feb. 20. The Seahawks opened his 21-day return-to-practice window on Oct. 1. Charbonnet ran for 730 yards and 12 touchdowns on 184 carries in the 2025 regular season, while sharing carries with Kenneth Walker. Price missed the past four games on injured reserve with a chest injury. He has 32 touches for 140 yards. The Seahawks will have to make a move for Price to return to the active roster from IR. The team ruled out offensive tackle Charles Cross (ankle), running back Velus Jones (hamstring) and wide receiver Rashid Shaheed (knee). Linebacker Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) is doubtful. Linebacker Patrick O'Connell (toe), defensive tackle Brandon Pili (back) and quarterback Drew Lock (right elbow) are questionable. Lock was limited in all three practices this week.
author: Charean Williams

title: Deion Sanders and Colorado survive in overtime for first Big 12 win of the season
summary: It was harder than it should have been, but Colorado and coach Deion Sanders finally have their first Big 12 win of the season, beating Kansas State 27-24 in overtime to snap a five-game losing streak.
full_text: ' It was harder than it should have been, but Colorado and coach Deion Sanders finally have their first Big 12 win of the season, beating Kansas State 27-24 in overtime to snap a five-game losing streak. Colorado led for most of the game, and had a 21-14 lead and the ball late in the fourth quarter, but couldn't gain the game-clinching first down, punted, and then nearly choked the game away when Kansas State marched down the field and scored with two seconds remaining in the fourth quarter. With the score 21-20, Kansas State initially lined up to go for two and the win, but then decided to kick the extra point and force overtime. Kansas State scored a field goal on the opening possession and Colorado responded with a touchdown to win it. "Our kids, they've never stopped believing," Sanders said after the game. "I'm just so darn proud of these young men right now." Colorado hasn't given Sanders a lot to be proud of this season, and is now in a last-place tie with Kansas State at 1-4 in the conference. But in what has been a very rough season, Coach Prime finally has a conference win.

title: Josh Jacobs could be on thin ice in Green Bay
summary: Throughout his off-field incident that resulted in a no-contest plea to misdemeanor battery, the Packers have remained steadfast in their support of running back Josh Jacobs.
full_text: Throughout his off-field incident that resulted in a no-contest plea to misdemeanor battery, the Packers have remained steadfast in their support of running back Josh Jacobs. That could now be changing. The persistent presence of the Packers as one of the teams that have expressed some degree of interest in trading for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor suggests that they've at least pondered the possibility of swapping out Jacobs for Taylor. Recent developments don't help Jacobs's cause. Beyond the handcuff celebration that Jacobs tried to say wasn’t a handcuff celebration (but that video of the full celebration suggests was a handcuff celebration ), Friday's release of police records indicating that at least three other women have accused Jacobs of domestic violence could shake the team's apparent resolve to keep him. Throw in the fact that Jacobs is averaging 2.3 yards per carry in his two games back from a six-game stint on paid leave — including 1.9 yards per carry against the worst run defense in the league entering Thursday night's game — and it's possible that the Packers will realize that Jacobs is no longer good enough to justify a stubborn circling of the wagons. Cutting Jacobs would raise the issue of termination pay as to the balance of his $10.2 million salary, and it would short-circuit the team's ability to seek partial repayment of signing-bonus money if/when (when) he's eventually suspended under the Personal Conduct Policy. For now, we won't delve into the full extent of the niceties of Article 30 of the CBA; at a minimum, the Packers would have some potential arguments aimed at cutting off his right to any termination pay. Even if the Packers ultimately are on the hook for termination pay, it's a sunk cost. The question is whether they want to keep him on the team, in light of recent developments. Again, they've been linked in multiple reports from ESPNFL to a trade for Jonathan Taylor. That alone is substantial evidence that they're considering a future without Jacobs that could begin sooner rather than later.
author: Mike Florio

title: NFL "will review" the new allegations against Josh Jacobs
summary: Jacobs could be facing a lengthy suspension.
full_text: The NFL was already reviewing the case of Packers running back Josh Jacobs following a no-contest plea to misdemeanor battery arising from an incident that happened in May 2026. The league is now investigating additional allegations that have recently come to light. "We will review these allegations as part of the investigation which has remained open," the NFL said Saturday in a statement. Police records released on Friday revealed that three other women made allegations of violence against Jacobs, after the first incident came to light. The league likely will need to identify the individuals and then attempt to persuade them to cooperate. It significantly raises the potential discipline that may eventually be imposed on Jacobs. He'll get credit for the six games he missed on paid leave, with a requirement to forfeit the salary he received. With the Personal Conduct Policy creating a baseline suspension of six games without pay for each incident of domestic violence, along with enhanced penalties for repeat offenses, Jacobs could be facing a lengthy suspension. More immediately, the question remains whether the Packers will move on from Jacobs. The team had no comment on Saturday morning, in response to the news that three other women have made allegations against Jacobs. Through it all, the video of the May 2026 incident remains hidden from public view. The NFL wants to see it before finalizing his punishment for the incident that sparked a no-contest plea.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: John Harbaugh called Amy Adams Strunk directly in an effort to land Jeffery Simmons
summary: Harbaugh's unconventional move failed to prevent Bears from doing deal with Titans.
full_text: The trade that sent defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Titans to the Bears has an interesting — and unusual — postscript. Jonathan Jones of The Athletic reports that Giants coach John Harbaugh directly called Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk in an effort to get Simmons to New York. The call reportedly came after Giants G.M. Joe Schoen had contacted Titans G.M. Mike Borgonzi about Simmons, only to be told that the Titans weren't trading him. As Jones notes, another G.M. who learned about the effort said it "violates a code" among football's decision-makers. One source in a key football position with one of the NFL's teams dubbed the effort "shameful." Despite Borgonzi's claim from Thursday that the Titans weren't looking to trade Simmons until the Bears called on Wednesday night, Jones reports that the Titans' "braintrust" had a meeting on Tuesday during which they decided to start listening to offers for Simmons. It's unclear whether Harbaugh made the call to Adams before or after Bears G.M. Ryan Poles offered a package that included a pair of first-round picks. We're told the Giants were willing to offer more than what the Bears ultimately sent to the Titans. (Of course, that's easy to say at this point.) The entire situation underscores the value of pre-existing relationships when it comes to getting deals done. It was a point we discussed on Friday's PFT Live . In 2021, the trade that sent quarterback Matthew Stafford from the Lions to the Rams had a distinct "inside job" feel to it, given that Lions G.M. Brad Holmes had recently been hired from the Rams. Other teams that would have been interested in attempting to acquire Stafford were surprised to learn that he had been quietly and quickly dealt to the Rams, who were able to tuck quarterback Jared Goff into the deal — and to discreetly attach extra compensation to get the Lions to take on a contract that, after only two seasons, the Rams had come to regret. The outcome prompted former Commanders G.M. Martin Mayhew to call every team in the league the following offseason to inquire as to whether their starting quarterback may be available in trade. The ultimate question, when trades like this happen, is whether the relationship angle results in the team that gives up a key player getting as much as it could. If the Giants would have indeed offered more, shouldn't the Titans have fully explored that avenue? Ultimately, the longstanding relationship between Poles and Borgonzi may have superseded the effort to get as much as possible for Simmons.
author: Mike Florio

title: Of eight use of helmet infractions in Week 7, only Cam Skattebo was flagged
summary: The fine imposed on Giants running back Cam Skattebo for illegal use of the helmet was not a rarity.
full_text: The fine imposed on Giants running back Cam Skattebo for illegal use of the helmet was not a rarity. The flag thrown in real time for it was. Of eight fines levied by the NFL for use-of-helmet violations in Week 7, only Skattebo's came with a flag. The league fined Skattebo $7,073. The seven players fined but not flagged were: Bears cornerback Clark Phillips ($11,550); Broncos safety Brandon Jones ($23,882); Broncos Alex Singleton ($47,662); Lions safety Brian Branch ($23,882); Colts cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt ($7,791); Steelers receiver Brandon Smith ($4,916); and 49ers running back Jordan James ($6,194). The fines increase as the violations repeat. For Singleton, who was fined $23,882 for illegal use of the helmet, it was the second straight week he was fined. The officials, for whatever reason, don't often call penalties for illegal use of the helmet. That's what made the penalty called on Skattebo so unusual. The fact that the hit flattened Texans safety M.J. Stewart likely was a factor in the decision to penalize Skattebo. Still, the fact that only one of eight instances resulted in a foul being called underscores the fact that, when it comes to the rule against lowering the helmet and initiating forcible contact against an opponent, it's something that costs players money far more routinely than it costs their teams field position.

title: Jonathan Taylor mock trades: How Giants, Broncos, Seahawks could target Colts star RB
summary: The Colts need to replenish their draft assets, and dealing their three-time Pro Bowl running back could produce a significant return
full_text:
After a loss to the previously winless Titans dropped the Colts to 2-4 on the young season, Indianapolis fired GM Chris Ballard . It was the first firing by Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon, and it might not be the last. Shane Steichen has zero postseason trips in four seasons as the Colts' coach, and while he's still leading the way for now, there's no doubt his seat is and has been warm. How much warmer it became after Ballard's firing is unclear, but it's clear Irsay-Gordon expects better than what the Colts are producing.
It's also clear that the Colts aren't close to getting to the level Irsay-Gordon expects. Daniel Jones has been a turnover machine, and the defense is below average, with issues rushing the passer and defending the run. The Colts are 28th in yards per play allowed and 26th in net yards per attempt allowed.
Sometimes it has to get worse before it gets better, and that may be the case for the Colts. Indianapolis is already down a 2027 first-round pick, traded to the Jets at the 2025 trade deadline, but the Colts could be sellers -- and maybe major sellers -- this year.
The biggest name would be star running back Jonathan Taylor . He had 20 touchdowns and nearly 2,000 yards from scrimmage last year, and he's on his way to another big season, but the Colts are stuck going nowhere once again. He's 27 and has played in just one playoff game -- as a rookie in 2020. In fact, Taylor headlined Jordan Dajani's list of five players we want to see moved by the Nov. 10 deadline.
Taylor would have plenty of suitors if made available, and the situation isn't too dissimilar from what the Panthers were going through with Christian McCaffrey in 2022. McCaffrey is a more versatile player than Taylor in the passing game and was younger than Taylor is now when that deal happened, but he had also been injured. In the deal with the 49ers in 2022, Carolina received second-, third-, fourth- and fifth-round picks.
With that in mind, here are five teams who could come calling about Taylor and what a mock trade might look like:
Giants receive: RB Jonathan Taylor Colts receive: RB Cam Skattebo , 2027 second-round pick, 2028 fourth-round pick
The Giants used a four-running-back committee Sunday against the Saints and then released Najee Harris (who didn't exactly love the rotation). In between, John Harbaugh explained his rationale, saying he "would love" to have a " Derrick Henry circumstance or a 'Saquon Barkley circumstance." Whether he meant to or not, it was surely a bummer for Giants fans to hear Harbaugh mention his running back from last year and a former Giants running back in the same sentence. Regardless, Taylor could be that type of workhorse. The Colts getting two high draft picks over the next two years, plus Skattebo, who showed promise as a rookie but didn't have a single touch Sunday, on a cost-effective deal, would be a solid start. The Giants are leading a historically bad NFC East, and even if it doesn't finish that way, having Taylor next to Jaxson Dart next year would be an enticing prospect.
One thing to note, though, is that Harbaugh comes from one of the most patient, draft-and-develop franchises in Baltimore. This would be a significant departure from that.
Bengals receive: RB Jonathan Taylor, 2027 fourth-round pick Colts receive: RB Chase Brown , 2027 second-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pick
This would be similar to the package the Panthers got for McCaffrey, but instead of a third-round pick, the Colts would get Brown. At 26, he's younger and has less wear and tear than Taylor. He's also an accomplished player and productive pass catcher who has handled a bell-cow workload before. A change of scenery could do him good, as he has struggled to get going early this season. For the Bengals , this would be a second major win-now move in just over six months; they sent the No. 10 pick to the Giants in April for Dexter Lawrence . The Bengals have tried to work in more under-center looks, but are among the worst teams using it. Taylor could change that single-handedly. Cincinnati also has an extra third-round pick, which helps make giving up so many picks easier to swallow.
Broncos receive: RB Jonathan Taylor, 2027 fifth-round pick Colts receive: RB J.K. Dobbins , 2027 second-round pick, 2027 fourth-round pick
The Broncos traded a first-round pick for an upgrade at wide receiver in Jaylen Waddle this offseason (though it hasn't really worked out yet). Would they make another big deal for an upgrade at running back in Taylor? The Broncos have struggled to muster much on the ground, exacerbating quarterback Bo Nix's struggles. Dobbins is on a two-year deal, though there's an out after this year should the Colts choose to use it.
Seahawks receive: RB Jonathan Taylor Colts receive: RB Jadarian Price , 2027 second-round pick
It'd be rare to see a team move on from a first-round pick so quickly, but the Seahawks are in a rare position as the first team to lose a Super Bowl MVP in over two decades. Seattle very much misses Kenneth Walker III and is struggling to find much of anything on the ground without him. Price is on IR, and Emanuel Wilson and George Holani have had devastating fumbles. Offensive coordinator Brian Fleury has been with the 49ers since 2019, so he knows the value of a great top running back. Indianapolis would get a good young running back and ample future picks.
Vikings receive: RB Jonathan Taylor Colts receive: RB Jordan Mason , 2027 second-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pick
The 5-0 Vikings have shown signs of an improved run game this year, and Mason is on his way back from a thumb injury that had him on IR, but Taylor would be a game-changer, and combining him with a mobile quarterback in Kyler Murray would be a treat for Kevin O'Connell. Mason, meanwhile, is a good player on his own accord. Plus, the Vikings have draft capital to spare, with an extra third, two extra fifths and two extra sixths.

title: NFL Week 8 picks and score predictions: Browns end 38-year drought, Bills survive Baltimore
summary: Week 8 brings Halloween scares for several contenders, including the Bills, Vikings, Chiefs and Seahawks
full_text:
In honor of Halloween weekend, the NFL is giving us a horrifying Sunday night game this week: the Eagles (2-5) at the Commanders (1-4-1).
Roger Goodell, if you're reading, there's still time to flex this game out. I say move it to 2 a.m. and put it on Telemundo, because at this point the only thing that might make the game better is listening to it in Spanish.
Anyway, since Halloween is coming up on Saturday, this seems like the perfect time to hand out costume ideas, so that's exactly what we're going to do before we get to the picks this week.
If you're a Commanders fan, you could go as a clock since your team doesn't understand time management. If you're an Eagles fan, you could go as a couch since that's where the team will be sitting once the playoffs start. If you're a Titans fan, you could go as a bench, since that's where Cam Ward should probably be at this point. And if you're a Chargers fan, you could go as nothing since that's what your team has done this season.
Will I pick any of these teams to win in Week 8? Let's get to the picks and find out.
Actually, before we get to the Week 8 picks, here's a quick reminder that you can check out the weekly picks from every CBSSports.com NFL expert by clicking here . Also, as you probably know by now -- because I point it out every week -- I'm in charge of the NFL newsletter here at CBSSports.com. If you want to subscribe, all you have to do is click here and enter your email address .
Through the first seven weeks, the Bills look like one of the best teams in the AFC, but my biggest issue with them is that they have one major flaw and it's their entire defense. Having a major flaw isn't necessarily a bad thing. My major flaw is that I watch "Hot Tub Time Machine" whenever it's on TV. To fix that flaw, I could either stop watching TV or I could destroy all the TVs in my house. Either one of those would work. Unfortunately for the Bills, there's no easy fix for their problem.
Heading into Week 8, the Bills are surrendering 28.5 points per game, which is the third-most in the NFL. Only the Cardinals and Commanders are worse. When you're mentioned in the same conversation as those two teams, that's definitely a red flag.
One reason the Bills are giving up so many points is that they can't stop the pass. Through their first six games, the Bills are surrendering an average of 285.8 yards per game, which is the second-highest number in the NFL.
Since I've started things off here by ripping the Bills' defense, you might be thinking that I'm about to pick the Bills to lose, but there are two reasons why I'm hesitant to do that. For one, Josh Allen exists. For the Bills, it doesn't matter how bad their defense plays because Allen always manages to save the day.
The Bills defense has given up at least 30 points in four different games this season, but thanks to Allen, the Bills have gone 4-0 in those games. To put that in perspective, the other 31 teams are a combined 8-47 this year when they surrender at least 30 points.
The other reason I'm hesitant to pick against the Bills is that I have no idea whether Lamar Jackson will play. Jackson injured his ankle in Week 4 and hasn't played since. The Ravens have been saying he's "Day-to-day" for the past three weeks and all I have to say is that someone needs to explain to them how a calendar works. You can't be "day-to-day" for THREE WEEKS.
Although Jackson didn't play in Week 7, he returned to practice last week, suggesting there's at least a chance he could play in this game. If anyone can take advantage of the Bills' defense, it's definitely Jackson. For that reason, I'm going to make two picks here, one for if Lamar plays and one for if he doesn't. Actually, you know what, I really don't even need to make two picks because I'm taking the Bills either way.
PICK (Lamar plays): Bills 34-31 over Ravens PICK (No Lamar): Bills 34-24 over Ravens
The Vikings have done it. They're officially the final undefeated team left in the NFL. This is the greatest accomplishment by any Viking since Erik the Red and Leif Erikson roamed the planet.  Despite having no offense, the Vikings have somehow run the table through the first seven weeks.
So how bad is their offense? Glad you asked.
The Vikings are winning because of their defense, and if I were defensive coordinator Brian Flores, I would ask the organization to triple my salary and then double it again on top of that. One reason the Vikings' defense has been so good this year is that Flores has come up with a brilliant new strategy called, "We're going to blitz you on every play and see what happens." I won seven straight Super Bowls in Madden while using that strategy in college and it seems to be working out well for the Vikings.
In their win over the Colts , they blitzed at an 85.2% rate. THEY BLITZED ON ALMOST EVERY PLAY. And this was not a one-time thing: For the entire season, the Vikings have a blitz rate above 70%.
First, let me say that I love this strategy, but over the past three weeks, the Vikings have beaten Malik Willis , Tyler Shough and Daniel Jones . That's the NFL equivalent of winning a hamburger-eating contest against three vegans. What I need to know is if the Vikings defensive strategy is sustainable.
The Vikings have played the third-easiest strength of schedule through the first seven weeks, but things are going to get a lot more difficult starting this week. As a matter of fact, from Week 8 through Week 11, the Vikings have the most difficult strength of schedule in the NFL (.731) with games against the Lions , Bills, Packers and 49ers .
It's one thing to blitz Daniel Jones into oblivion, but that might not work against Jared Goff , Josh Allen, Jordan Love or Brock Purdy . I'm not sure what Flores will end up doing against the Lions, but I feel like he's going to have a special surprise in store for them. The Vikings swept the Lions last year, and a big reason was that Flores' defense held Detroit to 34 total points in the two games combined.
Flores has been the defensive coordinator in Minnesota since 2023, so he knows this Lions offense inside and out. If defense wins championships, then there's no way I can pick against the Vikings in this game.
PICK: Vikings 19-16 over Lions
The Browns have already beaten the Steelers once this season, and if they win this game, that would give them their first season sweep of Pittsburgh since 1988. That's right, it has somehow been 38 years since the Browns have swept the Steelers. The NFL should have flexed this game to Sunday night and asked everyone at the stadium to dress up like their favorite character from 1988. I would have definitely been John McClane from Die Hard, or maybe AC Slater. You know what? I'm not sure and we don't have time to talk about this.
This game is not an easy one to pick and that's mostly because both teams still feel like a mystery to me. I do love a good mystery -- That's why I read all 200 "Encyclopedia Brown" books as a kid -- but I can't quite figure out either team.
On Cleveland's end, the Browns are 5-2, but I still have no idea how good they are. The Browns seem to be flying by the seat of their pants every week. Their last three wins have all come on a field goal in the final 10 seconds, which I'm only pointing out, because they are the FIRST TEAM in NFL history to have three straight wins come by a field goal in the final 10 seconds.
Also, all five of their wins have come by four points or less. There have only been three other teams in NFL history to pick up their first five wins in games they won by four points or less and none of those teams made the playoffs. That being said, the Browns do have a great defense, Deshaun Watson has been absolutely clutch this year, and their rookie receivers have been impressive.
Maybe we should have seen all of this coming. Oh wait, I DID! Back in June, I predicted Cleveland's entire season and had them finishing 10-7. HERE'S THE VIDEO PROOF.
I actually had every AFC North team…

title: Saquon Barkley trade rumors: Eagles send a clear message about RB's future in Philadelphia
summary: The NFL's trade deadline is coming up on Nov. 10 with teams poking around on the former first-rounder
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles are staunch on keeping Saquon Barkley at this month's NFL trade deadline and prefer not moving on from one of their franchise players whose usage has dwindled amid a 2-5 start, NFL Network reports .
The 29-year-old running back has two years and $35 million remaining on his contract and sources close to the team have reportedly indicated general manager Howie Roseman has made it apparent to possible suitors that Barkley is off the market ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.
There's interest from others in a potential Barkley acquisition , but Philadelphia reportedly plans to move forward in 2027 with its current offensive nucleus and try again if this season continues to go awry.
At last season's deadline, the Eagles were buyers after acquiring edge rusher Jaelan Phillips from the Miami Dolphins for a 2026 third-round pick and landed cornerbacks Jaire Alexander and Michael Carter II. That continued a trend of Philadelphia fishing for talent under Roseman midway through the season to gear up for a potential stretch run.
Currently third in the NFC East with Jalen Hurts out for the season, the Eagles could be sellers this time around, with hopes of a postseason appearance diminishing. Barkley played only nine snaps in last week's game against the Dallas Cowboys with a back injury and has 244 yards rushing and a touchdown on 43 attempts this fall.
After averaging 312 carries and 1,572 yards rushing per season over his first two years with the Eagles, Barkley's statistical projections in 2026 fall well short of expectations during the first campaign in which he'll likely miss the playoffs with the franchise. He's expected to play in Sunday's game against the Washington Commanders despite a nagging back situation.
With four other ball carriers on injured reserve, the Eagles take the field with Barkley, Jaydon Blue and Elijah Mitchell available in the backfield. Barkley did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday and was reportedly limited during Friday's walk-through.
"I would hope so; I believe I'll be able to," Barkley said Friday about his weekend availability. "There's one day I'm not going to be playing football. Whenever that is, I don't want to look back and be like, 'I could have given it a chance and I didn't.' It's kind of what I live by. I'm going to try my best to just keep recovering, being smart, but I like playing football, so if I have an opportunity to play, I'm going to try my best to play."

title: It wouldn't shock me if ... NFL Week 8: Colts reduce Jonathan Taylor's reps, Lamar Jackson shows no rust
summary: A Vikings' tight end breaks out? The first place Atlanta Falcons?
full_text:
There's nothing quite like Halloween. Remember when you used to go trick-or-treating? I remember dressing up as a Power Ranger, Ghostface, or some skeleton, eagerly walking up to the front doors of all the houses in the neighborhood, and wondering what kind of candy my brother and I were about to get.
Would it be a KitKat bar, Reese's, M&M's? Maybe they'd even be king-sized!
That feeling of stepping up to those front doors, not knowing what was in store for us, is a bit like how we approach each week in the NFL . We have no clue what's going to happen when that door opens. You could receive your favorite candy in the world or — in NFL terms — see your favorite team pull out a win. Or, you could be handed an apple by that crunchy neighbor who reminds you to brush your teeth — the equivalent of your first-round pick in fantasy suffering a season-ending injury.
It's that unknown that makes the NFL a must-watch experience every week, and we do our best here to help give you some clues as to what may be coming around the bend to avoid a jump-scare. For instance, last week we said we wouldn't be shocked if J.J. McCarthy impressed in his first start with the Giants , and that's exactly what happened. We also highlighted the possibility of Kenneth Walker III having a muted return to Seattle.
We'll look to take the momentum of nailing those two predictions into Week 8, where we'll call our shots on some storylines and/or individual performances that we wouldn't be shocked to see happen.
The Colts have started to clean house ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. On Tuesday, the club shipped out star left guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and pass rusher DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers for draft compensation. Those are two heavy-hitters being shown the door amid the organization's 2-5 start to the year and impending rebuild, but they won't be the last to be dealt.
Jonathan Taylor is another name that has been spinning in the rumor mill as he'd fetch a pretty penny for Indianapolis and no longer fits its timeline as it looks to tear down the roster to the studs. The 27-year-old is still among the best running backs in the NFL and has rushed for 587 yards and eight touchdowns through seven games in 2026.
With a Taylor trade looming, I wouldn't be surprised if Indy starts managing the asset and holds him back a bit more as the deadline draws near. If Taylor gets hurt while he takes on his typical workload of 20-plus touches per game, the Colts, who do not have a first-round pick in 2027, lose one of their biggest chips in helping springboard their rebuild and filling the cupboard back up with draft picks. It makes a lot of sense to effectively put Taylor in bubble wrap until a trade is made.
Indy won't outright bench Taylor, but I think it'll start giving backup running back Seth McGowan more work. We already started to see this last week as Taylor played a season-low 67.2% of the offensive snaps. His 18 carries were also his second-lowest of the season. Meanwhile, McGowan's 32.8% offensive snap rate in Week 7 was his highest of the year, as were his 11 carries.
I expect that only to grow as these rumors around Taylor heat up.
Gambling angle to note : Jonathan Taylor's O/U rushing yards total is set at 63.5 (-109 to the Under).
Lamar Jackson is set to make his return to the field on Sunday against the Bills after missing the previous three games with an ankle injury. Given the injury and the time away, there's an argument to be made that Jackson could be a little rusty as he works his way back, particularly in what is billed as a high-stakes AFC matchup. However, I think this goes the other way. I can see Lamar Jackson showing little to no rust in his return and possibly even leading the Ravens to a road win in Buffalo.
Jackson wasn't just looking like an MVP candidate through his first four games of the season before dealing with the injury; the two-time NFL MVP was arguably playing the best football of his career. Jackson seemed right at home in new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's offense, as his yards per attempt (10.1), air yards per attempt (10.9), and 70.8% completion rate are all on pace to be career highs. Meanwhile, his 119.6 passer rating is on pace to tie his career-high, which came back during his MVP runner-up season in 2024.
Jackson nearly played last week, so I don't think he's as cold as the absence would suggest. On top of that, he has a pretty soft landing spot in his return as the Bills' defense has been one of the worst units in the league entering Week 8. So far, Buffalo's 386.8 total yards allowed is the second-highest in the NFL, while its 28.5 points per game allowed are the third-highest.
Look for Jackson to have a thunderous return in Week 8.
Gambling angle to note : Lamar Jackson's O/U passing touchdown total is 1.5 (-112 to the Over). Jackson's O/U passing yards total is 237.5 (-113 to the Over).
A lot will be made about the Lions ' high-flying offense squaring off against Minnesota's top-ranked defense, and rightfully so. That'll be what gets people in the door to watch this NFC North game, but I believe it'll be the other two sides of the ball that determine the game.
Specifically, I see this as a golden opportunity for the Vikings offense to break out against what is a poor Lions defense. Coming into Week 8, Detroit has the worst total defense (391.0 total yards allowed) and passing defense (291.8 passing yards allowed) in the NFL. As he looks to exploit that, Kyler Murray should be looking at one target in particular: T.J. Hockenson .
The Lions are at the bottom of the league in covering tight ends. Despite playing six games (when accounting for the bye vs. some teams who have played seven contests), Detroit has still given up the most receptions (56) and receiving yards (602) to tight ends this season. For the purposes of this prediction, it's noteworthy that they're also giving up a league-high 10 receiving touchdowns to tight ends.
The Lions are allowing touchdowns on 72% of opponents' red zone trips in 2026, which is the fifth-highest in the league. Hockenson leads the Vikings in red zone targets (6) this season, and he's tallied two touchdowns in the process. I wouldn't be shocked if he finds paydirt twice in this advantageous matchup.
Gambling angle to note : T.J. Hockenson is +230 to score one anytime touchdown and +2000 to score 2+ touchdowns (via DraftKings Sportsbook).
Washington was on the bye in Week 7, so Sunday's primetime matchup against the Eagles will be their first full game since wideout Terry McLaurin suffered his season-ending injury. McLaurin was the No. 1 weapon in the Commanders offense, so they'll need players in that receiver room to step up and adopt the 5.4 targets per game he was seeing this season.
While some will point to that target share shifting toward Stefon Diggs , I believe it could go to rookie Antonio Williams . The third-round pick out of Clemson has already flashed at points this season, but he hasn't seen a ton of opportunity, averaging about four targets per game. During that Week 6 loss to the 49ers, when McLaurin went down, Williams led the receiver room with 34 routes run. Thirty-one of those routes run were in the second, third and fourth quarters when McLaurin was already out of the game.
That suggests Williams could be the beneficiary of McLaurin's absence, and having a bye week to prepare for an added workload only emboldens the idea of a breakout for the young pass catcher. title: Commanders vs. Eagles: Struggling NFC East squads face off on 'Sunday Night Football'
summary: Here's what you need to know to catch the game
full_text:
Two NFC East teams desperate to get their seasons on track meet under the bright lights of "Sunday Night Football" when the 1-4-1 Washington Commanders host the 2-4 Philadelphia Eagles .
The Eagles won the first meeting between these rivals, 24-22, back in Week 1, but that Eagles team is far different from this one. The most notable difference is that there will be no Jalen Hurts . The star quarterback is out for the rest of the season with blood clots, just the tip of the iceberg for a team decimated by injuries. Saquon Barkley has missed time with a hamstring issue and looked far from 100% in his Week 7 return. He will play despite having hamstring and back ailments. Wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) and linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) are all out as well.
The Commanders, meanwhile, are in dire straits, and coach Dan Quinn could really use a win coming out of the bye. Jayden Daniels has played well since returning from his elbow dislocation, but he will be without Terry McLaurin , who suffered a season-ending torn patellar tendon in Week. Daniels has not won a start in over a year; this could be as good a chance as any.
Date: Sunday, Nov. 1 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location : Northwest Stadium (Landover, MD) TV: NBC | Stream: fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Commanders -6 ( via DraftKings )
Stoppable force (Eagles offense) vs. movable object (Commanders defense): This season, the Eagles are 29th in points per game and 32nd in yards per play. The Commanders, meanwhile, are 31st in points per game allowed and 22nd in yards per play allowed. This should be a decent chance for Tanner McKee and the Eagles offense to build off of a Week 7 performance against the Cowboys in which they showed some progress. Plus, the Commanders are without standout interior defenders Daron Payne (who suffered a season-ending injury Friday) and Javon Kinlaw . On the other hand, this is an opportunity for Washington's blitz-happy defense to take advantage of an undermanned, underperforming offense.
Jayden Daniels looks to get back in win column: Wins aren't a quarterback stat, but Jayden Daniels certainly would love to pick up a victory; he hasn't had one as a starter since Week 5, 2025. Since then, he has missed 10 games and gone 0-7-1 as a starter. Still, it's hard not to be impressed by how well Daniels has played in the past two weeks. He threw for 199 yards and ran for 103 yards and two scores in a 27-27 tie against the Giants that included a comical error at the end, and then he had his second. career 300-yard passing game against the 49ers in Washington's last game. With no McLaurin, expect a heavy dose of Stefon Diggs , Chig Okonkwo and Antonio Williams .
Primetime scares: The game is happening one day after Halloween, but primetime has been spooky time for Washington. The team has lost six straight primetime games. Only the Colts (seven straight) have a longer active losing streak.
The Eagles' offensive struggles are to be expected. The defensive struggles last week against the Cowboys were surprising, and the unit simply has too much talent to perform like that. It also performed very well in Week 1 against Washington, and I anticipate a return to closer to that form. Washington badly needs a win: at home, off a bye, as a favorite, with Dan Quinn on the hot seat. But I don't think it'll happen. Pick: Eagles 20, Commanders 17

title: Steelers vs. Browns: Rivals battle in Week 8 with first place in AFC North on the line
summary: Plus, where to watch, what to know and a preview from an NFL expert
full_text:
One of the NFL's greatest rivalries is alive and well. On Sunday, the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns will duel with first place in the AFC North on the line.
Both teams enter Sunday's game with 5-2 records. The Browns, by virtue of their Week 4 win over Pittsburgh, are technically the division leader. Cleveland responded to a loss to the Jets in Week 5 with wins over Baltimore and Tennessee.
Pittsburgh has won three straight since losing to Cleveland. Last Sunday, the Steelers became the first team to win a game in Paris after recording a 16-10 win over the Saints .
Here's how you can follow the action, along with a breakdown and a prediction.
Last time we met: The Browns' 27-24 win over Pittsburgh in Week 4 was their fifth consecutive win over the Steelers in Cleveland. The Browns led 21-7 before withstanding Pittsburgh's comeback attempt. The Steelers' comeback was spearheaded by Aaron Rodgers , who threw two fourth-quarter touchdown passes.
The Steelers tied the score with 1:42 left, but four completions by Deshaun Watson on Cleveland's ensuing drive set up Andre Szmyt's game-winning 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds remaining.
Rodgers threw for 299 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions in a losing effort. Jaylen Warren ran for 93 yards on 17 carries, and DK Metcalf led Pittsburgh's receivers with 115 yards on five catches.
Cleveland's offense ran through rookie receivers Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion , who combined to catch nine passes for 153 yards.
Steelers are finding their groove on both sides of the ball: Pittsburgh's three-game winning streak is largely the byproduct of better play from the offensive line and a defense that is continuously improving.
Pittsburgh's offensive line surrendered five sacks of Rodgers back in Week 4. Rodgers has been sacked nine times in the three games since. While that's still not great, it is a sign of the unit's continuous improvement.
The line has also helped revive the Steelers' rushing attack, which has improved further with Rico Dowdle's return. The duo specifically made their presence felt during Pittsburgh's game-winning drive in overtime in Tampa Bay back in Week 6.
Defensively, the Steelers have made marked improvements since the loss in Cleveland, which was the Steelers' first game after Joey Porter Jr . was traded to Dallas. The unit is currently fifth in the NFL in points allowed, fourth in touchdown passes allowed, sixth in average yards per carry allowed, seventh in third-down efficiency and eighth in red zone efficiency.
Linebacker Payton Wilson has been one of the Steelers' defensive standouts during the winning streak. He made a key interception during last week's win over the Saints.
While Cleveland's defense has been solid all year, its offense has at times left something to be desired. They are coming off their best performance in recent moments, however.
Against the Titans , the Browns piled up 491 yards while receiving excellent balance. They threw for 308 yards and ran for 183. Cleveland did turn the ball over twice after not doing so a week earlier in a 13-10 win over the Ravens .
Really, the big question in Cleveland is whether or not Watson can beat an elite defense. He'll try to show that he can on Sunday.
The Steelers have two distinct advantages. They have the better quarterback and a running game that should be able to take advantage of a Browns defense that is 22nd in the NFL in average yards-per-carry allowed. If Dowdle and Warren get going, that should help open things up for Rodgers and the passing game. Score: Steelers 20, Browns 16

title: NFL Week 8 last-minute best bets: Jaguars beat up on Colts, Chargers remain winless after battle with Rams
summary: Need some last-minute advice on how to bet the Week 8 slate? Allow us to be of assistance
full_text:
There's arguably nothing scarier than settling down on Sunday morning, getting ready for the new slate to unfold, and having no clue what to wager on. This week in particular can leave some folks on their heels in the betting sphere. After all, when you're out all night trick-or-treating on Saturday night, who has the time to comb through all the latest news, injury updates, and anything else that could swing a game? Well, fortunately for you, you've come to the right place.
We've fended off the urge to hunt for M&M's, Reese's, and other candy while dressed like our favorite comic-book hero and kept our eyes on the real prize: cashing our Week 8 bets. Below, you can find a pick for every matchup on the docket for Week 8, as well as five best bets. So, crack open some of your trick-or-treating haul from Halloween and let's bet!
Note : New Orleans, New York ( Giants ), San Francisco, and Houston are on the bye in Week 8.
The Colts are already selling off parts amid a 2-5 start to the year, which includes a three-game losing skid entering Week 8. It's hard to see a scenario where things change for the better this weekend, as they'll head to Jacksonville to face a 4-2 Jaguars team that'll be fresh off its bye week. Coming into this slate, the Colts have a claim to be one of the worst offenses in the NFL .
Their 4.5 yards-per-play average is tied for the worst in the league with the Eagles , and a large part of those issues lies at quarterback. Daniel Jones has yet to rekindle the version of himself from the first half of last year and has thrown an interception in all but one game so far in 2026. Jones ranks 31st out of 33 eligible quarterbacks in passer rating this season, while his EPA per dropback ranks 30th. Among quarterbacks with at least 100 pass attempts this year, Jones is tied for the second-highest turnover-worth-per-throw rate.
He now faces a Jaguars pass defense that is just outside the top-10 in the league with an 87.7 passer rating allowed. They're also tied for the third-most interceptions (7) in the league. Conversely, you have Trevor Lawrence playing like an MVP candidate and should face little resistance from a Colts defense that has just two interceptions on the year.
Projected score : Jaguars 33, Colts 20 The pick : Jaguars -10
The Bengals showed us their potential during their 35-point second-half outburst in the win over Baltimore. If anything close to that version of the Bengals is on the field on Sunday, Tennessee doesn't have a puncher's chance of keeping this close, especially after trading standout defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Bears earlier this week. The Titans' passing offense doesn't have the ceiling to go toe-to-toe with Joe Burrow , as the club ranks 29th in passer rating and is tied for last in yards per attempt.
While Cincinnati's offense garners much of the headlines, the Bengals' defense has been an underrated unit this season and was a key reason they were able to endure an offense-free first half in Week 7. Zac Taylor's defense has the third-best red zone efficiency (35% touchdown rate) in the NFL. That matches up well against a Tennessee red zone offense that scores a touchdown on just 47.4% of trips (27th in the NFL).
Projected score : Bengals 35, Titans 21 The pick : Bengals -12.5
In theory, the Chargers would've spent the bye week figuring out what has gone wrong in their 0-6 start to the year and come out firing in Week 8, when they'll technically be the road team but will be at their home stadium as they face the Rams at SoFi Stadium. I just don't see them putting together much of a fight, however.
Justin Herbert has been among the worst quarterbacks in the league so far this season and comes into Week 8 with a league-high 5.6% turnover-worthy throw rate. While the Rams haven't generated many turnovers, they have five interceptions this year, showing they are more than capable of taking advantage of any opportunity Herbert gives them. The Rams are also giving up just 186.3 passing yards per game this season, which is the fourth-lowest in the league. No matter which way you slice it, it should be tough sledding for Herbert in this matchup.
That means Matthew Stafford likely won't have to do much heavy lifting to clear this 6.5-point spread. That's especially true considering that the Chargers can be taken advantage of on the ground. They're allowing 123.8 rushing yards per game, so this could be a matchup where Kyren Williams and Blake Corum become the focal point of the attack. That backfield duo is coming off a win against the Raiders where they each went for over 90 yards rushing to go along with a touchdown. It wouldn't be shocking to see similar production on Sunday.
Projected score : Rams 30, Chargers 17 The pick : Rams -6.5
The Dolphins finally got into the win column for the first time all season with a road win against the Jets . While that's great for Jeff Hafley's club to get off the schneid, I don't see the momentum from that victory turning into a two-game winning streak. Since Mike Vrabel became the head coach, New England is 8-4-1 ATS on the road. As a road favorite in games, they are 3-2 ATS with an average margin of victory of 13 points.
While they'll be on the road, the Patriots have the rest advantage in this game after playing last Thursday. They're also simply the better team. Miami is allowing 5.7 yards per play this season and 7.8 yards per pass attempt (tied for third-highest in the NFL). Drake Maye should continue to find success through the air against a Dolphins secondary that is allowing a league-high 116.8 passer rating against. So long as they don't shoot themselves in the foot, this should be a double-digit victory for New England.

Along with Stefon Diggs , rookie wideout Antonio Williams has flashed potential, while veteran tight end Chig Okonkwo has been an underutilized piece of the offense that I expect will see more work down the stretch.
Washington's defense won't be mistaken for one of the best units in the league, but I think they should be able to keep Tanner McKee in check.
