title: Broncos host rival Chiefs in game that could decide AFC West
summary: Everything you need to know for Sunday's huge divisional game
full_text:
The 5-1 Kansas City Chiefs are hosting the 5-2 Denver Broncos at Mile High on Sunday. The Broncos are coming off a 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals and are currently on a three-game winning streak. Their last loss came against the San Francisco 49ers , who were undefeated at the time, on Oct. 4.
The Chiefs are looking to shake the loss of last week off, after their worst performance of the season by far. They lost 20-3 to the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks . Their three points scored were tied for the fewest from quarterback Patrick Mahomes .
This is the second meeting between the two teams, as they faced each other in Week 1.
Date: Sunday, Nov. 1 | Time: 4:25 p.m. ET Location : Empower Field at Mile High (Denver) TV: CBS | Stream: Paramount+ Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Chiefs -1.5 ( via DraftKings )
Division: This division is a close one, especially with K.C.'s loss last week. With the Raiders falling from grace after an excellent start, it looks like the AFC West will be a competition between the Chiefs and Broncos. This game will mean a lot down the line and I think it will show in their competitiveness on Sunday. Mile High is not an easy place to play, due to the fans and the elevation, and the Chiefs know this far too well, visiting there at least once a year. The Broncos lost their last matchup in Week 1, but won the previous three. Splitting the matchups would be big for Denver as they look to take the AFC West title for the second year in a row.
Injury news: The Chiefs are getting wide receiver Rashee Rice back. The WR has been sidelined with a hamstring injury since Week 4. Before the injury, he had 13 receptions on 17 targets for 190 yards and one touchdown in four games, three of which were starts.
I think the Chiefs will sweep the divisional series, but I think it will be close. I expect Rice to be a factor in his first game back. Pick: Chiefs, 30-27
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Ravens' Lamar Jackson returns from injury to face off with Bills' Josh Allen
summary: Everything you need to know to catch Sunday's huge AFC battle
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens are heading to Highmark Stadium to face the Buffalo Bills on Sunday. The Ravens come into the contest 4-3, while the Bills sit at 5-1. The two are in very different spots in their divisions. The Bills are in the lead in the AFC East, while the Ravens find themselves in unfamiliar territory, in fourth place, with the Cleveland Browns surprisingly leading the AFC North.
The biggest news from this game is the return of Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson , who has missed three games due to an ankle injury. In the meantime, Tyler Huntley has led the offense, going 1-2. On the other side of the field will be Bills quarterback Josh Allen , who once again finds himself among the best in the AFC.
The Ravens are coming off a 35-13 loss against the Cincinnati Bengals and are looking to snap a two-game losing streak. Their last win came against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5, and it took overtime.
The Bills are coming off a bye week and, before that, had a 33-30 win over the Las Vegas Raiders . They are currently on a two-game win streak, with their last loss coming in Week 4 against the New England Patriots .
Lamar Jackson: Before going down with the injury, Jackson went 3-1, with a 70.8 completion percentage, six touchdowns and one interception. Huntley has gone 1-2 with a 69.8 completion percentage, four touchdowns and one interception in four total appearances. In five games against the Bills, Jackson has 678 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions.
Bills vs. Ravens history: With Jackson and Allen in the league, Bills vs. Ravens games have become instant classics and games everyone will have circled on their schedules. Jackson is 3-2 against Allen in the regular season, but Allen has the playoff edge at 2-0. The all-time head-to-head matchup between these teams is tied at 7-7, including two Buffalo playoff wins. The Ravens lost their last two meetings against the Bills.
Keys to victory: The Ravens need to fix their issue of letting leads slip. They have lost back-to-back games where they had a 10+ point lead at halftime. The Ravens have a bad history of letting games slip away, and if they want to be a playoff contender, they need to fix that. The Bills had extra time to prepare for this game, which should help them. One of the areas they need to work on is turnovers, because despite being the highest-scoring offense in the league, they struggle with giving the ball away.
Date: Sunday, Nov. 1 | Time: 1 p.m. ET Location : Highmark Stadium (Orchard Park, New York) TV: CBS | Stream: Paramount+ Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bills -3 ( via DraftKings )
I think this one will be close. Jackson should come out with extra excitement and motivation after being sidelined for multiple weeks, but I think the home team has the advantage. I expect the Bills to win this one in a tough battle that comes down to the end, and it may just be a playoff preview. Pick: Bills, 33-30

title: Giant twist: John Harbaugh went unconventional route in trying to land Titans' Jeffery Simmons, per report
summary: Simmons ended up with the Bears
full_text:
Jeffery Simmons landed with the Chicago Bears on Thursday in a blockbuster trade that netted the Titans two first-round picks, but not before Giants coach John Harbaugh tried an unconventional method to try to get the star defensive tackle to New York. According to The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , Harbaugh called Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk to try to get to the front of the line in the Simmons sweepstakes.
It was a bold -- and potentially unpopular -- move. One GM told Jones that Harbaugh's call to the top "violates a code amongst primary football decision-makers, that they will only deal with each other."
According to Jones, Giants GM Joe Schoen had previously called Titans GM Mike Bogonzi, who told Schoen and other teams that they wouldn't trade Simmons. Harbaugh got the same answer from Strunk. Ultimately, though, the Bears sending 2027 and 2028 first-round picks and a 2027 fourth-round pick to Tennessee for Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick proved too good to pass up. Bears GM Ryan Poles had reportedly been keen on Simmons since the 2019 NFL Draft , when he and Borgonzi were both working for the Chiefs .
Harbaugh reports to Giants ownership, not Schoen, which is a bit of an unusual chain of command. Clearly, Harbaugh feels empowered enough to try a very unusual approach to trades.
The Giants have been a popular potential landing spot for many top names in the trade rumor mill. At 4-2-1 this season, Harbaugh and co. lead the woeful NFC East and are looking to add in the pursuit of their first playoff trip since 2022. The Giants, who already traded for J.J. McCarthy and recently made him their starting quarterback with Jaxson Dart injured, are expected to continue to look to add talent ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Defensive lineman and running back are two positions commonly tied to New York.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Garrett Wilson trade rumors: Jets responding emphatically to other teams asking for star WR
summary: New York wants to keep the former first-round pick and offensive star
full_text:
The New York Jets may have interested trade partners , but there's "no way" the franchise is moving wideout Garrett Wilson before the Nov. 10 deadline, according to ESPN .
Adam Schefter reports the Jets had similar off-limits feelings last season with Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams before moving both for draft picks at the deadline , but the "situation this year with Wilson is different for various reasons."
While the Jets are widely viewed as sellers at the deadline with a 2-5 record this season, the fifth-year wide receiver is reportedly loved by ownership. New York does not want to move him after signing Wilson to a four-year, $130 million extension that runs through the 2030 season last summer.
Last season, Wilson posted career-best numbers with 101 catches for 1,104 yards and seven touchdowns and is once again one of the offense's top threats, averaging a 25.8% target share in the passing game. Wilson has 37 receptions for 444 yards and three scores.
Wilson denied trade talks earlier this week and said previously this season he had no interest in leaving the Jets.
"I want to be here, man," Wilson said. "I want to win games, and that's the one thing we've been missing on here. I love it here. Do I love it more than I love winning? Nah, to be completely honest, but I'm hopeful. I've never been the most optimistic guy, but I've found a way and dug deep, and I've been optimistic for three, four, five years now. And that's why these [losses] each weekend hurt a little more."
The belief within the Jets' organization, per ESPN, is to build around Wilson with draft picks obtained through last season's multitude of trades and surround him with more talent through the 2027 NFL Draft cycle.
While Wilson said he wants to stay in New York, he did mention winning trumps all.
"No doubt, no doubt," Wilson said . "I'd be lying if I said it's not, but at the end of the day it comes down to ... winning and losing. Throughout my experience, when things go right, I tend to have a part in that. And when it doesn't, it seems avoidable.
"That's my main frustration that may show on the TV or something like that. But I don't want it to ever be misconstrued. This all comes from a place in my heart of wanting to win. I'm biased, but it also comes from experience where I played my part in that.
"It's frustrating, for sure, because I want to have an impact and I want to help the team. But really, I just want to help the team, man. Sometimes it might come off a certain way when they [show] video, but, man, that's all it's about."
Jets quarterback Geno Smith said Wednesday he's "looking to get him the football as much as I can" while being mindful of coverages and opposing defenses doing everything in their power to take him out of the game.
Wilson's reception and yardage totals lead the team this season.
author: Brad Crawford

title: Three other women accused Packers' Josh Jacobs of abuse after RB's arrest, police records show
summary: Jacobs was arrested in May and later pleaded no contest to two misdemeanor charges
full_text:
After Packers running back Josh Jacobs was arrested on domestic violence charges in May 2026, three more women came forward with alleged physical incidents involving the Packers running back, according to Hobart/Lawrence Police Department records released to NBC 26 late Friday night .
Jacobs was arrested and jailed on five charges in late May: battery, criminal damage to property and disorderly conduct, all involving domestic abuse; strangulation and suffocation; and intimidation of a victim. The strangulation and suffocation charge was a felony, and the other four were misdemeanors. Jacobs turned himself in three days later and was released after one night in jail. He had previously denied the allegations through his legal team.
Details of the incident were not immediately disclosed. In August, however, an incident report revealed Jacobs had a "physical struggle" with a woman at his residence. Later, in the garage, "Jacobs grabbed her and threw her to the ground and she struck her head, suffering an injury. Jacobs then took her phone from her while she was on the ground. [The woman] laid on the ground for a while and then struggled to walk back into the house," according to the report.
Jacobs was charged with two Class A misdemeanors : battery and damage to property. He pleaded no contest to both charges in September.
Friday's police document release, though, reveals that after Jacobs' arrest, three more women contacted the police during the police's investigation and detailed previous incidents involving Jacobs.
One woman contacted investigators in June, shortly after Jacobs' arrest, and told police the allegations sounded similar to her experience with Jacobs in January 2022. The woman alleged Jacobs slapped her across the face, threw her phone in the pool, grabbed her by her hair, threw her onto a bed, pinned her down, threw her on the floor and said "I should kill you right now," spit on her and grabbed her by the throat.
The woman said she believed her alleged experience could be relevant to the case and she wanted people to believe the woman involved in the May 2026 incident, per NBC 26. She also said she did not report the incident and remained friends with him.
Another woman contacted the police later in June to describe an incident from April 2021. The woman alleged Jacobs grabbed her by her arms, pushed her against a wall and threw her belongings outside. She said she suffered bruising to her arms and pain and swelling in her rib area, per the report. The woman said she called the police at the time; records indicate the responding officers observed no sign of injury, bruising or damage.
A third woman contacted the Hobart/Lawrence police in July and said that, in a May 2022 incident, Jacobs placed his hands on her head and neck, dragged her, scratched her chest and took her cell phone. She said she suffered bruising and scratches, and she did not report the incident or receive medical treatment because she wasn't a U.S. citizen at the time, and Jacobs told her she could be deported.
Furthermore, the records released to NBC 26 disclosed more details from the May 2026 arrest, per ESPN . Police records noted that Jacobs lunged at the woman, pinned her on a bed and covered her mouth and nose so she felt she couldn't breathe. The woman also indicated she believed she lost consciousness during the incident in the garage. Police have denied requests to release or allow others to view the video of the May 2026 incident, but it did release footage of Jacobs' arrest .
"We will review these allegations as part of the investigation, which has remained open," the NFL said in a statement Saturday .
Jacobs spent the first six weeks of the season on the commissioner exempt list, meaning he could not play or practice but could attend workouts and meetings, receive treatment and get paid. He has played in the Packers' last two games since coming off the list but remains under investigation, as the statement above indicates.

title: Intriguing players to watch in Falcons vs. Bucs
summary: As Week 8 follows on the heels of Halloween, the Atlanta Falcons hope to avoid a house of horrors at Raymond James Stadium in a high-stakes NFC South clash against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. After a 0-4 start, the Bucs’ season looks resurrected with recent wins, and the Falcons hope to end their hopes in […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 27: Kyle Pitts #8 of the Atlanta Falcons scores a touchdown during the first half of an NFL football game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on October 27, 2024 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images As Week 8 follows on the heels of Halloween, the Atlanta Falcons hope to avoid a house of horrors at Raymond James Stadium in a high-stakes NFC South clash against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . After a 0-4 start, the Bucs’ season looks resurrected with recent wins, and the Falcons hope to end their hopes in a nightmare scenario. But to survive the scares in Tampa Bay, the Falcons will need to summon some supernatural performances from five key players. Michael Penix Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. will need to pack his holy water and grip his crucifix tightly as he attempts to exorcise the blitzing demons of Todd Bowles’ defense. The Bucs love to bring the heat, and Penix has shown poise under that extra pressure, posting the 6th-best DVOA according to FTN Fantasy . However, when those blitzes actually create pressure, the script flips into a horror movie: Penix ranks 31st against pressure per the same source. To banish demonic doubts, Penix must use his quick release to attack the soft spots over the middle before Tampa’s ghoulish pass rushers can drag him down. Kyle Pitts While Tampa Bay prepares its haunted house, tight end Kyle Pitts enters Week 8 as their ultimate recurring nightmare. Like a classic horror-movie villain in a hockey mask, no matter how many times the Bucs think they’ve stopped him, Pitts always comes back. In eight career games against Tampa Bay, Pitts has terrorized their defense with six touchdowns while averaging over 78 receiving yards per game. Considering he averages roughly 40 yards per game against all other opponents and a third of his career touchdowns have come against Tampa Bay, Pitts channels a slasher-flick energy against the Bucs. If he wields the machete again on Sunday, Atlanta’s offense will be in great shape. Ryan Neuzil Pitts isn’t the only monster haunting this matchup. The Bucs feature a terrifying creature in 350-pound nose tackle Vita Vea. That places the onus squarely on Falcons center Ryan Neuzil to gather his silver bullets and hold the line against a beast that ravenously devours run plays. If the Falcons hope to establish the ground game against Tampa Bay’s second-ranked run defense, Neuzil and the interior offensive line will need a heroic, monster-slaying effort. Gervon Dexter On the other side of the trenches, defensive tackle Gervon Dexter will need to play the Grim Reaper. The Bucs boast a dangerous rushing attack, and Dexter must help control the line of scrimmage. But his soul-harvesting duties don’t end there, as quarterback Baker Mayfield has also struggled under pressure this season. If Dexter can help the Falcons’ front collapse the pocket, they can force Mayfield into grave mistakes and collect crucial takeaways just like they did in last week’s win over the San Francisco 49ers . Kendal Daniels For the second straight week, rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels will don the green dot to lead the defense in Divine Deablo’s absence . Stepping into the caller’s role, Daniels will have to haunt the A- and B-gaps to help Dexter and the defensive line bury the Bucs’ run game. If the rookie phantom can diagnose plays quickly and fill his assignments without giving up the ghost, Atlanta’s defense will be well-positioned to stop the Buccaneers. Surviving a road trip to Tampa Bay on Halloween weekend won’t be easy, but the Falcons are well-equipped to pull off another frightful upset. If they can, they’ll take complete control of the NFC South. Can you name any other Falcons that will be tricked or treated in this matchup?

title: Falcons vs. Buccaneers: What will Week 8’s win or loss mean for Atlanta?
summary: Just when it looked like hope in the season was about to start getting drained out following a 2-4 start and a meeting against the undefeated San Francisco 49ers on tap, the Falcons had an unexpected victory in dominating fashion to give this roller coaster ride another swing upwards, as has been their MO for […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - DECEMBER 11: Kyle Pitts Sr. #8 of the Atlanta Falcons scores a touchdown in front of Kindle Vildor #22 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the second quarter at Raymond James Stadium on December 11, 2025 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images Just when it looked like hope in the season was about to start getting drained out following a 2-4 start and a meeting against the undefeated San Francisco 49ers on tap, the Falcons had an unexpected victory in dominating fashion to give this roller coaster ride another swing upwards, as has been their MO for years. Of course, Falcons fashion would be losing the next game after an exhilarating victory to let the fanbase down and send this ride going the right back down the other way. If they want to be taken seriously, it’s imperative that they buck the trend this weekend against the Buccaneers. Atlanta makes the trip down to Florida for its first game against the Bucs of the season and it may well be the most important one of the campaign up to this point. Here is the scenario the Falcons face if they beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 8, as well as if they lose. If the Falcons win They would climb back up to .500 at about the halfway mark of the season which, given the schedule and the 0-2 start behind Cooper Rush, would feel like a minor miracle. Back to back victories against the 49ers and Buccaneers would have much of the fanbase buying back in. They would also have weathered the eight game storm without the suspended James Pearce Jr., who is eligible to return next week. With Carolina’s defeat against the Packers on Thursday Night Football (I guess beating Green Bay on TNF isn’t for everybody), the Falcons would move into sole possession of first place in the NFC South, and would drop Tampa Bay and New Orleans to two games behind them in the win column, solidifying this as a two horse race for the time being. The algorithm at playoffstatus.com currently gives the Falcons a 17% chance of winning the division and a 37% chance of making the playoffs as of today. Those numbers would increase to 23% and 46%, respectfully, which I know don’t seem like much, but that’s huge movement when dictated by just one game in the middle of the season. The Birds would continue a recent period of success against the Bucs, winning their sixth meeting in the last eight against Tampa Bay, dating back to 2024. If the Falcons lose Then it will be another case of “typical Falcons,” with another big let down following a euphoric victory. No matter the head coach or front office over the last decade, this will continue being the groundhog day type plague that continues tripping this franchise up. To make matters worse, this would also be Atlanta’s second divisional loss in three games. You don’t have to look further than last season to realize how detrimental these divisional losses can be as the Falcons wound up tied for first in the NFC South but were mathematically eliminated a month before the end of the season because of their inferiority when it came to the tiebreakers. The Falcons would remain a half game behind the Panthers and would actually fall to third in the division due to the head to head tiebreaker Tampa would possess while sitting at an identical 3-5 record. Carolina, remember, also owns the tiebreaker over the Birds as of this moment. Atlanta’s odds at the division would fall from 17% to 15% and their overall playoff odds would fall from 37% to 28%, as any hope of even potentially fighting for a wildcard spot would take a major blow. Their next two games are against the Bengals and Chiefs, which could take things from bad to worse in a hurry.
author: Adnan Ikic

title: The Falcoholic Reacts: New NFC South expectations
summary: Many would believe the Falcons were favorites to win the NFC South from 2023 to 2025. They arguably had the most talented roster in the division. Their skill position group was prolific. The offensive line was largely solidified. They possessed enough difference-makers defensively. Despite all the personnel advantages, they fell short in all three seasons.  […]
full_text: Many would believe the Falcons were favorites to win the NFC South from 2023 to 2025. They arguably had the most talented roster in the division. Their skill position group was prolific. The offensive line was largely solidified. They possessed enough difference-makers defensively. Despite all the personnel advantages, they fell short in all three seasons. Disappointing quarterback play and questionable coaching were considered the biggest reasons behind their shortcomings. It forced the organization to start fresh and enter a transition year with minimal expectations. Those expectations have changed since Week 3, after the Falcons beat two playoff teams convincingly from last season and humiliated their biggest rivals in primetime. There is growing buzz that the Falcons can end their dreaded playoff drought. While they still face several major challenges on the schedule, no NFC South team looks more stable than them. A win against Tampa Bay would put them in an excellent position to take more control of the division and raise expectations even higher. Many fans believe they should be expected to win the NFC South with a road victory. It’s been a rollercoaster season for the Falcons, filled with adversity and excitement. For all the personnel setbacks and frustration over certain decisions, Kevin Stefanski’s team continues to play inspired football. They are unified, resilient, and violent. Teams are in for a battle when they face them. It’s why the fans are largely happy about the team’s direction. This result is brought to you by FanDuel Sportsbook.

title: Falcons vs. Buccaneers series history (Part 1): Win-loss record, matchup results
summary: The Falcons are back into NFC South play as they reach the halfway mark of their divisional games in the 2026 season with a trip to Tampa Bay for a date with a Buccaneers team which took control of the incredibly close all time series history behind Tom Brady, before the Falcons swung the pendulum […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - OCTOBER 14: Matt Ryan #2 of the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 14, 2018 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Scott Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Falcons are back into NFC South play as they reach the halfway mark of their divisional games in the 2026 season with a trip to Tampa Bay for a date with a Buccaneers team which took control of the incredibly close all time series history behind Tom Brady, before the Falcons swung the pendulum back into their favor in recent years. Atlanta currently owns a very narrow 33-32 all time series lead as they continue to work to undo the five consecutive Bucs victories from 2020-22. To illustrate just how tightly contested recent years have been, each of the last six consecutive matchups have ended in a one score game. This has been a history of winning streaks for one side or the other. In addition to the five straight Tampa had at the start of this decade, they also won six matchups in a row from 1997-2003, as well as three separate three-game winning streaks sprinkled in there. The Falcons, meanwhile, served their counterpunch in the Matt Ryan era, winning six out of seven matchups in the top half of the Ryan era from 2008-2012, and then another six out of seven in the back half between 2016-2019. The Falcons are currently on a run of five victories in the last seven matchups. When these teams met last The Falcons were already mathematically eliminated from post season contention at 4-9 but they had a chance to go up to Tampa on Thursday Night Football and play spoiler against a Bucs team now in a two horse race with Carolina for the NFC South. Tampa, looking for a season sweep of the team they had beaten to open the season, had their hands full with tight end Kyle Pitts, who was embarking on a career performance. Pitts had already found the end zone twice by the time halftime came with his team leading 14-13. The favored Bucs restored order and dominated the third quarter, however, scoring two touchdowns, forcing two punts and a turnover to take a 28-14 lead into the final frame. From there, Bijan Robinson scored, Kyle Pitts completed the hat trick of touchdowns, Dee Alford secured a big interception of Baker Mayfield and Kirk Cousins led a game winning drive which culminated in a Zane Gonzalez field goal as time expired. This win put the Panthers in the driver’s seat of the division and wound up being the difference in Carolina breaking their playoff drought while the Bucs stayed home for the playoffs.

(Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Happy Halloween, Falcons Fans! No tricks today, just ten sweet 2027 NFL Draft prospects to watch in week 9 of college football. As the season flips toward all eyes being on the College Football Playoff, with the first rankings coming out on Tuesday, the prospect pool will shrink, and there will be a clearer vision as to who will be coming out and who will be coming back to college for another year. Have a day 🔥 pic.twitter.com/lz6sPmdazR — big ounce (@_bigounce) October 4, 2026 One of the Falcons’ biggest needs heading into this draft is cornerback and Texas Tech’s Brice Pollock fits the bill of a potential long-time corner in the NFL. Pollock plays with a ton of instincts, mostly in off man and zone coverage, but he has the tools and recognition to continually get his hands on the football, grabbing two interceptions this season despite limited targets. Kam Davis, RB, Liberty vs. Florida International Williams Stadium – Lynchburg, VA – 3:30 pm EST – CBS Sports Network Liberty's Kam Davis has been so impressive tonight. Davis is a powerful runner who can explode for chunk gains when he gets into open space. He was a former four-star prospect before being mostly unused at Florida State. At Liberty, the former Albany, GA native is able to better show off his ability in the open field. Kari Ashley, TE, TCU vs. Kansas Amon G. Carter Stadium – Fort Worth, TX – 3:30 pm EST – FS1 TCU TE Kari Ashley (6-4, 225) is “the most freaky athlete we got” coming from Navarro CC & GA Tech Needs to get a little more chatter here pic.twitter.com/jhKRRMi4RE — Clint Goss (@NFLDraftDome) October 24, 2026 I’m never above having a Feldman’s Freak on the list and Kari Ashley is certainly one of the freakiest. A former linebacker turned tight end at Navarro Community College, Ashley has been one of the most productive tight ends in the country, so much so that he is only one of five tight ends that have been added to the Biletnikoff Award Watch List. Gamble is a back-end of day three to UDFA guy that deserves a shot at making a roster due to his athleticism and instincts at cornerback. For a team like the Falcons, Gamble would instantly add special teams value while potentially developing into a rotational cornerback. Not to mention he has one of the best names in the business. title: Ravens Discussion: Predictions for Week 8 matchup vs. Bills
summary: The Baltimore Ravens will take on the Buffalo Bills today in a much-anticipated Week 8 contest. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s predictions for the game. Dustin Cox The Ravens have often responded with big wins in previous seasons when their backs were against the wall. That was with John Harbaugh at the helm, however, so we […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 07: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens runs the ball for a touchdown during the second quarter against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on September 07, 2025 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens will take on the Buffalo Bills today in a much-anticipated Week 8 contest. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s predictions for the game. Dustin Cox The Ravens have often responded with big wins in previous seasons when their backs were against the wall. That was with John Harbaugh at the helm, however, so we will have to see if Jesse Minter is able to rally the troops the same way. This game heavily hinges on how healthy Lamar Jackson is behind a shaky offensive line. If Jackson plays to the level he was performing to start the season, then Baltimore has a legitimate path to victory on Sunday. The Bills defense has struggled against the pass, so Jackson and Zay Flowers could do some real damage through the air. If Buffalo is able to get quick pressure and Jackson isn’t healthy enough to evade rushers as usual, then it could be a long day for Declan Doyle. Continuing to scheme up easy plays to Flowers and letting him make plays after the catch will be needed to ease the burden on Jackson in his first game back. X-Factor: Trenton Simpson. The Ravens defense will have their hands full with Josh Allen. Simpson has been one of the best players on Baltimore’s defense to start this season, and his speed could come in handy when Allen inevitably escapes the pocket looking to make a big play through the air or as a runner. Simpson tracking down Allen on extended plays could make a huge difference if he is able to force Allen into a quicker decision with the ball. Score Prediction: Ravens 31, Bills 30 Nikhil Mehta Baltimore’s secondary is already on skates heading into a matchup with Josh Allen, and Lamar Jackson is back just in time to face one of the NFL’s worst passing defense. This could be a shootout of epic proportions, and it’s going to come down to turnovers. The Ravens have a poor record in that regard against the Bills, but Allen isn’t always careful with the ball either. Vega Ioane’s absence and Jackson’s still-ailing ankle will, I think, ultimately keep Baltimore’s offense from making all of the plays they need to in the fourth quarter, and the defense will be inches away from the game-changing turnover that never comes. This is an opportunity for the Ravens’ highest-paid defenders to step up and lead by example – can anyone deliver? X-Factor: Nate Wiggins. Wiggins doesn’t fall into the aforementioned group above, but he’s extension-eligible next offseason, and he hasn’t proven where he ranks among the league’s corners. The key? Playmaking. He needs to use his speed not just to be sticky, but to break on passes, create turnovers, and maybe even rack up some return yardage. Score Prediction: Bills 38, Ravens 34 Frank Platko There is a lot riding on this game for the Ravens. While they aren’t necessarily in desperation win-now mode yet and can technically afford another loss, a victory would go a long way for both positive vibes and playoff hopes. A win over the Bills on the road could serve as a turning point for the team to turn a new page with Lamar Jackson coming back. Obviously, the Bills are going to get their share of points no matter how well the Ravens’ defense can play. Josh Allen and Buffalo’s offense is as dangerous as any in the NFL and they have an established offensive floor. We’ve yet to see Jesse Minter’s defense really dominate a game from start to finish and exceed expectations. They were just embarrassed by the Bengals last week in the second half. How will the Ravens’ defense respond against another elite quarterback? This a “play for your pride” type of a spot. X-Factor: Trey Hendrickson. The Ravens signed Hendrickson with the idea of him being the needle-moving pass rusher that can help the team close out victories. While he’s been playing through a finger injury, we’ve yet to see Hendrickson consistently make game-changing plays and convert pressures to sacks. The Ravens could use him to come through against Allen and make a big play or two. Score Prediction: Bills 29, Ravens 27 Zach Canter The Ravens are knee deep in “can’t lose” territory heading up to Buffalo. The Bills, much like the Bengals, are coming off a bye and boasts the best offense in the NFL statistically. They also have one of worst defenses overall, so it looks like this will turn into a shootout. Under different circumstances, I’d probably take the Ravens. I think the offense is capable of going shot for shot with the Bills and the Ravens defense is good enough to deliver one more stop than the Buffalo’s is. However, Lamar Jackson is returning from injury and probably isn’t 100%. They are going to be missing their first-round guard Vega Ioane and the Bills are coming off a bye week. So, I think the Ravens fall just short in this one. The offense will have just a couple missteps in Jackson’s first game back, and the defense just won’t be able to do enough to limit Josh Allen to support the offense while they get back in rhythm. X-Factor: Mike Green. If the Ravens do want to win this game, the defense is going to have to find a couple spots on the Buffalo offense. Trey Hendircskon will have his hands full working against Dion Dawkins and Madubuike winning inside will be important. But Bills right tackle Spencer Brown is expected to miss this one. Mike Green beating a backup tackle to put pressure on Allen and not letting him escape to his arm side is going to be vital to avoid those back breaking plays Allen is capable of delivering. Score Prediction: Bills 34, Ravens 24
author: Dustin Cox

full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - AUGUST 22: Baltimore Ravens cornerback T.J. Tampa (27) looks on after the NFL preseason game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Minnesota Vikings on August 22nd, 2026, at U.S. Bank in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens activated cornerback T.J. Tampa from injured reserve and elevated offensive lineman Chuma Edoga and outside linebacker Adisa Isaac from the practice squad. All three will be available to play the Buffalo Bills on Sunday. Tampa, 24, went down with a knee injury on his fifth special teams snap of Week 1. He returned to practice in Week 7 and progressed to full participation this week. The third-year cornerback will add depth on the boundary to a secondary that has been scrambling for answers in recent weeks. Marlon Humphrey and Nate Wiggins have dominated the available outside snaps with only occasional rotational looks for Chidobe Awuzie. Tampa figures to remain fourth in the pecking order initially, but his skillset might be a fit for Jesse Minter’s zone scheme. Edoga and Isaac will fortify the Ravens in the trenches on either side of the ball right guard Vega Ioane (knee) and outside linebacker Tavius Robinson (pectoral) sidelined on Sunday. This is Edoga’s third elevation; to appear in another game for Baltimore this season, he must be signed to the active roster. Isaac made his season debut last week but only appeared on special teams. Unless he earns a role on defense, the Ravens might be more inclined to use up Kaimon Rucker’s practice squad elevations before giving either an active roster spot.
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Ravens-Bills Keys to Victory: can Lamar Jackson outduel Josh Allen?
summary: Baltimore finally gets to experience Lamar Jackson football once again. It’s safe to say the two-time MVP won’t be at 100% only three weeks removed from his high ankle sprain – just look at AJ Brown in New England. Unfortunately, the Ravens have no time for Jackson to start slow. They are 4-3, coming off […]
full_text: Jan 19, 2025; Orchard Park, New York, USA; Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) avoids a tackle by Baltimore Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike (92) to gain a first down in the first quarter of a 2025 AFC divisional round game at Highmark Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con Baltimore finally gets to experience Lamar Jackson football once again. It’s safe to say the two-time MVP won’t be at 100% only three weeks removed from his high ankle sprain – just look at AJ Brown in New England. Unfortunately, the Ravens have no time for Jackson to start slow. They are 4-3, coming off back-to-back losses against AFC divisional opponents with two tilts against two more AFC opponents in five days. First up, the Ravens are facing the Bills. It’s a tall task trying to take a win from Josh Allen in Buffalo, but the Ravens desperately need one. Here’s how Baltimore can come away with a win and get the season back on track. Let Lamar air it out Lamar Jackson is back. The Ravens finally have their center situation sorted out with Cam Jurgens. It’s time to restart the run game and get Derrick Henry backon track. Except the Ravens will now be missing rookie guard Vega Ioane, and the Bills’ run defense, led by Ed Oliver and Deone Walker, is better than their pass defense, which ranks near the bottom of the league. According to SumerSports, the Bills are tied for last in EPA per play, 31st in total defensive EPA, 30th in success rate, and 29th in EPA per pass play. Can you say air raid? This is a game prime to get the Jackson-Zay Flowers connection going once more. Add in Rashod Bateman in the middle of a comeback season and Ja’Kobi Lane, who will hopefully get more than one half with Lamar Jackson, and you’ve got weapons galore to rain down on Buffalo. There’s more than a good chance that this game turns into a shootout anyway, so establishing the air attack quickly with Lamar Jackson will give the Ravens the best chance at winning this game when it will likely come down to the last score in the last minute. Throw different defensive fronts at Allen There aren’t many things a team can do to contain Josh Allen. It’s one of the reasons he’s been one of NFL’s the top quarterbacks the last couple of years. Luckily, the Ravens have the best quarterback in the NFL coming back to duel with him. But Baltimore’s defense has got to make some plays and make life easier for the offense on Sunday. It’s hard to ask for a sub-20-point performance against what is statistically the best offense in the NFL this year, but they have to find one more stop than the Buffalo defense does. So how can the Ravens attack Allen effectively? For that, we look back at the 2024 regular season matchup between these teams, one of Allen’s worst games in the last couple of years. The Ravens’ pass rush impacted him a ton that game, logging eight quarterback hits and three sacks. They were effective in limiting James Cook, too, and protected their lead lead by varying their looks at the line of scrimmage to keep Allen off balance. While Baltimore’s secondary has been iffy this season, their pass rush has been good. The Ravens played a ton of line games in the first half against Joe Burrow while he was under center with great success. The Bills happen to use a ton of under-center concepts as well. The Ravens need to get to Allen, force him away from his throwing arm side, and hit him. Stunts, loops, delayed blitzes – use them all. Send Roquan Smith, Trenton Simpson, Kyle Hamilton through different spots of the line. They just have to remember to tackle. Aggressive man DB play Jesse Minter should not give up on the zone scheme that got him his head coaching gig. But his system has not taken full root in Baltimore. In Sunday’s matchup, he should lean into what this defense has been good at so far: aggressive, press-man coverage. After facing the Bengals’ elite wide receiver duo, the Bills’ wideouts present a much less complicated problem. It’s a well-rounded group with Khalil Shakir’s movement skills and Keon Coleman’s contested catch ability, but the Bills added DJ Moore this offseason to add a true alpha body to the room and take pressure off of the other guys. Moore is coming into this one having missed the last two games for the Bills and with a week full of limited practices off of the bye week. Pressing that trio will take away Allen’s quick reads and give the pass rush the extra split-second they so badly need to convert their pressures into sacks. The Ravens aren’t quite in a “must-win” situation for keeping their season alive, but they are firmly in “can’t lose” territory after two brutal losses. Play to strengths right now; fix the program later.

full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 01: Sam Williams #54 of the Cleveland Browns sacks Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers during the fourth quarter of the game at Huntington Bank Field on October 01, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Updated Standings: Cleveland Browns 5-2 Pittsburgh Steelers 5-2 Cincinnati Bengals 4-2 Baltimore Ravens 4-3 Baltimore Ravens Matchup: @ Buffalo Bills, 1:00pm EST The Ravens are reeling a bit after two straight losses to divisional opponents. Last week, they suffered a 22-point defeat at home against the Bengals, where they were outscored 35-0 in the second half. The Ravens have failed to score a second-half point in each of their last two games. Fortunately, they received some positive news this week with Lamar Jackson returning to full participant status in practice and he will start in this matchup. Baltimore’s offense badly needs a breakthrough performance against a high-powered Buffalo Bills team. The Bills have one of the league’s top scoring offenses led by star quarterback Josh Allen and running back James Cook alongside him. Jesse Minter’s defense has yet to demonstrate the consistency to slow down opposing units. The Ravens will need to find a way to clean up some their repeated defensive mistakes in this game, namely missing open field tackles and suffering coverage breakdowns. Jackson coming back gives the Ravens a real chance to score enough points to win on the road here. This is, of course, assuming he won’t have any rust and can perform at the level he was four weeks ago. The Bills’ defense is allowing the second-most yards and third-most points per game this season. They’ve been better against the run than the pass. The Ravens need to reignite their rushing attack as well, which has struggled to generate explosive runs and convert short yardage third downs in recent weeks. Cincinnati Bengals Matchup: vs. Tennessee Titans, 1:00pm EST The Bengals took care of business off a bye week last Sunday, emerging victorious in Baltimore to improve to 4-2. After struggling in the first half, the Bengals exploded on offense over the final two quarters, scoring five consecutive touchdowns. They’ll look to carry this momentum over in Week 8, with a favorable matchup against the Tennessee Titans at home on deck. Tennessee’s defense took a big hit prior to this game, as they traded away All-Pro defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons — their best player on either side of the ball. Simmons was the Titans’ leading pass-rusher and premier run defender up front. The Bengals should be able to keep Joe burrow upright and have an opportunity to get their run game going a bit. At just 81.2 rushing yards per game as a team, the Bengals are the third-least productive rushing attack in the league. Cincinnati’s defense similarly projects well in this matchup, although the Titans are coming off their best two scoring performances of the year in back-to-back weeks — totaling 50 combined points. Tony Pollard has been the Titans’ driving offense force, and keying in on the run game will be key for the Bengals. Pollard had 129 rushing yards with three touchdowns in Week 7. The Bengals should be able to survive in man coverage against the Titans’ pass-catchers if they crowd the box to stop the run. Cleveland Browns Matchup: @ Pittsburgh Steelers, 1:00pm EST The Browns were on the winning end of their matchup with the aforementioned Titans last week, where they narrowly won 27-24. It was yet another down-to-the-wire victory by four points or less, which has been the script in all five of Cleveland’s wins this season. One of those came against the Steelers in Week 4, and now the two divisional foes will be rematching this Sunday in Pittsburgh. Last week, the Browns tied their highest scoring output on the year (27) and totaled a season-high 491 yards on offense. Running back Quinshon Judkins returned from injury and had a 96-yard, two-touchdown performance on the ground. The Steelers’ defense has been stingy, ranking No. 7 in lowest rushing yards allowed and No. 5 in points allowed per game. If the Browns cannot find similar success in the run game again, they will likely need to create a turnover on defense and maximize their possessions late. On defense, the Browns will need to key in on the Steelers’ backfield. Jaylen Warren has three 100+ yard rushing games and is averaging 5.5 yards per carry, and Rico Dowdle has 135 scrimmage yards since returning from injury two weeks ago. In Week 4, the Browns gave up 93 yards to Warren but picked off Aaron Rodgers twice and got five sacks as well. Causing havoc like that will be important for them to get another win against the Steelers, especially in a tough road environment. Pittsburgh Steelers Matchup: vs. Cleveland Browns, 1:00pm EST The Steelers won their third consecutive game last week with a 16-10 victory over the New Orleans Saints in Paris. It was the type of gritty, low-scoring contest that Pittsburgh has a knack for emerging victorious out of, and their fourth win this season by seven points or fewer. The Browns have similarly had success winning close games this year, so something will have to give this Sunday. The Steelers are seeking to avenge their three-point loss in Cleveland a few weeks ago. Pittsburgh’s offense has been middle-of-the-pack for most of this season, and last week they averaged only 5.9 yards per pass through the air. The Steelers are still struggling with wide receiver depth without Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson, but their running backs are each involved in the passing game and can do damage as receivers out of the backfield. Expect Rodgers to target Warren and Dowdle both as quick outlets when the Browns bring pressure. Defensively, the Steelers have improved to Top 10 in rushing yards allowed, points allowed and sacks per game. If the Steelers can get consistent pressure on Deshaun Watson, they should have a good chance of creating a turnover. In what is projected to be a low-scoring battle, flipping a possession or two and giving their offense better field position may be a deciding factor.

title: My challenge to the Buffalo Bills against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 8
summary: I’m challenging the Buffalo Bills to do something specific in this Week 8 game against Lamar Jackson and the Baltimore Ravens. How about a truly convincing win over a quality opponent? Maybe even a wire-to-wire victory. No comeback needed. Heck, let’s even up it to a two-score margin. Parity has never been more ubiquitous in […]
full_text: I’m challenging the Buffalo Bills to do something specific in this Week 8 game against Lamar Jackson and the Baltimore Ravens. How about a truly convincing win over a quality opponent? Maybe even a wire-to-wire victory. No comeback needed. Heck, let’s even up it to a two-score margin. Parity has never been more ubiquitous in this game, which is largely why the NFL is so damn good and endlessly entertaining. A win is a win in this league, but I can’t write that all wins are viewed as equal. And existing solely in one-score game land is living dangerously. Over time, essentially all clubs regress to the mean in those tight contests. Now, teams with superstar quarterbacks and a collection of other excellent players can stay on the right side of the ledger in the hard-fought battles, but it’s not how any organization wants to regularly operate. And, right now, even at 5-1, just for their reputation and perceived staying power, the Bills are dire need of a game in which they were, undeniably, the better team throughout. It’s been a while for the Bills to secure that type of a win against a legitimately strong opponent. Since the beginning of 2020, Buffalo owns the league’s best collective point differential… by an enormous margin. They’ve outscored their combined opponents by 902 points. The Ravens have the second-best point differential in that time frame… at +581 points. That’s almost unfathomable, isn’t it? A season ago, the Bills beat the eventual 10-7 Steelers 26-7 in Pittsburgh, a thoroughly dominant, run-game driven thrashing of an eventual above .500 playoff team. That game felt out of reach for the Steelers for the vast majority of the contest. Obviously though, that Pittsburgh team was thoroughly flawed despite the regular-season record it managed. In the 2024-2025 wild-card round, the Bills beat an upstart 10-7 Broncos team with rookie quarterback Bo Nix 31-7 at home. Earlier that year, Josh Allen’s thunderous fourth-down scamper late against the, at the time, undefeated Kansas City Chiefs that finished 15-2, catapulted the Bills to a nine-point victory. But even that game got dicey late, of course. And it was Allen’s heroics that lifted Buffalo to a two-score win. A few weeks prior to that, Allen and Co. commanded the game from start to finish in Seattle against the eventual 10-7 Seahawks in a 31-10 win. What I’ve listed above are the Bills’ only triumphs by more than a touchdown over teams that finished above .500 in the past two seasons. And yes, blowout wins over eventual playoff teams are, quite naturally, reasonably rare for every club in the modern NFL. The ability to win close games is what separates the bad from the good and the good from the great. But Buffalo is past destroying bad-to-average teams. We know the Bills can do those things. They’ve been decidedly better at it than anyone else in football in the post-2020 Allen era. This core mission of this team is beating good teams in January and February, and while they’ll have to wait for their next opportunity to do that, today represents a prime test on the first day of November. I want to see the Bills start this game with loads of energy, feeding off what should be a raucous crowd, and play sound, reasonably complementary football in a win that won’t have any of said attendees — or the millions watching around the country — gnawing their fingersnails late. You know, a game in which Buffalo rises to the occasion and sends a message to the rest of the NFL that they, on this afternoon in Orchard Park, were clearly a better team than the Ravens.

title: Ravens defense has been a challenge for Josh Allen
summary: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen has started against the Ravens six times — including the playoffs — in his NFL career before Week 8’s clash, and he hasn’t exactly flourished in those matchups with Baltimore. He’s been surprisingly held in check as a runner too. Allen’s average completion percentage in those six games is just […]
full_text: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen has started against the Ravens six times — including the playoffs — in his NFL career before Week 8’s clash, and he hasn’t exactly flourished in those matchups with Baltimore. He’s been surprisingly held in check as a runner too. Allen’s average completion percentage in those six games is just 59.3%. His passing-yard average is just 211 with a pedestrian 6.06 yards-per-attempt average, and his rating is a mere 82.7. However, his touchdown-to-interception ratio is 5 to 1. His highest rushing-yard total (70) came in a 23-20 comeback in 2022. Other than that, Baltimore has held Allen to 30 yards or less on the ground. Allen has played the Ravens defense three times the past two years (twice in 2024), and of course, Baltimore’s personnel has changed over that time to a certain degree, but key pieces like Roquan Smith, Kyle Hamilton, and Marlon Humphrey remain. Despite his relative struggles against the Ravens in his NFL career to date… we can’t forget about Allen’s most recent outing facing this Baltimore team. Through three quarters in Week 1 last season, Allen was 18-of-26 for 143 yards with one touchdown through the air and no interceptions. Then he erupted. In the Bills’ furious comeback, Allen went 15-of-20 for 251 yards with one passing touchdown and two scores on the ground… in the fourth quarter of Buffalo’s 41-40 victory. He finished with 394 yards passing. Let’s see if that season-opening game a year ago was a turning point for Allen in his games against the Ravens defense.

title: How do the Buffalo Bills and Baltimore Ravens stack up?
summary: During the bye I decided to compare all of the Josh Allen era seasons of the Buffalo Bills on both offense and defense. I determined that this year’s team has both the best offense we’ve ever seen with Allen, it’s being paired with the worst defense he’s ever had in the NFL. In order to […]
full_text: During the bye I decided to compare all of the Josh Allen era seasons of the Buffalo Bills on both offense and defense . I determined that this year’s team has both the best offense we’ve ever seen with Allen, it’s being paired with the worst defense he’s ever had in the NFL. In order to make that determination, I needed to pull some data which led to a semi-valid but completely fun rating system. I figured it would be a fun sendoff to this exercise to use it to compare the Buffalo Bills and Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore offense vs. Buffalo Defense If you’re seeing this methodology for the first time, you can click on either of the links above to get a more full picture, or read this very short description. I took seven mostly distinct metrics and put those into the table along with the respective league ranking in each measure. Then I add up the rankings to get a complete score, with lower being better. Got it? Here’s the chart. I started with the side of the conversation that I think most people have an idea of what to expect. The Ravens’ offense against the Bills’ defense. I know Bills fans (myself included) are quite down on the defense and remember, there’s good reason! It’s the worst one we’ve seen in a long time. Numerically with the completed score on the right, I think the numbers suggest what we’re all feeling; this is a poor matchup. There’s 98 points of separation between the two teams. What does that number mean? It means there’s a big gap; the metric is mostly for fun after all and isn’t meant to be a precise measure of anything really. Disclaimer alert! Lamar Jackson was out for three weeks with an injury so these numbers might be skewed down a bit. With that aside, so far the Ravens’ offense has been average almost entirely. Their lone bright spot is avoiding turnovers, and their sole sore spot is that they allow a lot of sacks. If you’re interested in the splits; Lamar Jackson has been taken down seven times, while Tyler Huntley is at ten. They both have one interception on the season. I don’t know if there’s any surprises here, and if we’re being objective I think we all know Lamar Jackson can play. I’m not counting on this Bills defense making too many stops unless their bye week prep was near miraculous. The question this year seems to be this; can the Bills offense dominate opponents and outscore them? Let’s see if the gap between the Bills’ offense and Ravens defense is larger or smaller than “98.” Ravens defense vs. Bills offense If you trust my scoring system, then it should predict a Baltimore win. There’s 55 points between the two which you might have picked up is smaller than 98. That said, these matchups are fantastic for Buffalo and this also shows why I don’t think the scoring total is strictly accurate. No one score more often or more total points per drive than Buffalo. While the Bills are turnover prone and Josh Allen has taken his fair share of sacks; the Bills are overcoming these flaws and scoring at an incredible pace. It’s also possible the Ravens hold true to form and basically avoid getting a turnover off of Buffalo which would be nice. My final verdict is that despite the numbers of the total score, it comes down to my tiers. The Bills’ defense is terrible but flirting with merely “bad.“ That’s going against an average offense. On the flip side you have a mediocre defense taking on an elite offense. Yes, you could flip this statement around and make it about anchors/deadweight/etc; but there’s only one team with an elite side at the moment and it’s the Bills. Until that changes, I like their odds.

title: Parker Brothers Tailgate Menu for the Buffalo Bills 2026 season
summary: Tailgating has become synonymous with the Buffalo Bills and their passionately loyal fanbase, football fans from every walk of life who routinely show up exuding energy regardless of the location of the game or the temperature outside to fervently support their team. And I’m writing the Parker Brothers Tailgate menu because I’ve been friends with […]
full_text: Tailgating has become synonymous with the Buffalo Bills and their passionately loyal fanbase, football fans from every walk of life who routinely show up exuding energy regardless of the location of the game or the temperature outside to fervently support their team. And I’m writing the Parker Brothers Tailgate menu because I’ve been friends with Rory and Ray since Kindergarten and have remained close friends with these brothers through a lot with the Bills over the years. It’s a bond that has always extended beyond Bills tailgates, but as we’ve gotten older, the Bills tailgates have become our central meeting ground, a guaranteed place to reconvene every fall and winter. And I sincerely cherish the yearly regathering with these two. I’m sure you know the exact feeling of camaraderie with your tailgating group. What started as a nano-tailgate with a deep fryer for wings and fries has gradually morphed into a full-scale tailgating operation, often feeding 50-plus patrons thanks to multiple flat tops, cooking apparatuses, and condiments galore. I cannot recommend the Parker Brothers Tailgate enough. And here is their menu for the 2026 Bills season. (Rory and Ray will be situated in the new “white” lot — behind Prohibition 2020 — for the 2026 campaign, and they welcome you to join them.) Week 2 – September 17: Detroit Lions, 8:15pm — Birria tacos This was a new menu item in 2025, and it went over like gangbusters. And who hasn’t experienced the birria taco craze at their local Mexican restaurant or taqueria? Well the Parkers are bringing that succulent experience to the grand opening of the new Highmark Stadium. Slow-cooked, marinated beef, melted Oaxacan cheese, and a consomé that knocks your socks off the moment you take your first bite. Birria tacos will hit the spot on a momentous evening in Orchard Park with weather that should still feel like summer… before literal and figurative fireworks inside the new stadium. Week 3 – September 27: Los Angeles Chargers — No tailgate (wedding in Lake George) For the first time I can remember, Rory and Ray will not be at a Bills tailgate, working tirelessly to feed the masses before unwinding while watching their Bills play. Family wedding in the Adirondacks will keep them away for this one, but trust me, they’ll be back with more energy than ever after their own bye week. Week 4 – October 4: New England Patriots, 1pm — Stingers What wings are to Buffalo, stinger subs are to the Parkers tailgate. Well, stingers and garbage plates. Every year, the stinger tailgate attracts more friends and random passers-by than any other because of the Parkers’ attention to detail with their stinger construction. Thick chicken fingers, dipped in country sweet sauce, combined with perfectly cooked shredded beef, with any combination of lettuce, cheese, onions, banana peppers, and mayo on a fresh sub roll that can be toasted if you’d like (highly recommend it). All ahead of a colossal showdown with the defending AFC champs in the House That Josh Built. Week 8 – November 1: Baltimore Ravens, 1pm — Surprise, Surprise Despite the pestering of my Parker Brothers sources, this tailgate remains a mystery. All I could manage to coax from said source was this, and it’s awesomely cryptic, it’s actually making me hungry right now: “This tailgate has never been done before, maybe never again,” and “I’ll go out on a limb and say no one has ever tried it ever.” ….as if you needed more encouragement to get to Bills-Ravens. Week 11 – November 22: Miami Dolphins, 1pm — Turkey 2 Ways Have you ever had deep-fried turkey? If the answer is no, this is one glorious sliver of life you have yet to experience. The Parkers call this Turkey 2 Ways because you can get a few slices of classically cooked Thanksgiving turkey. And if that’s your jam, I respect that. I recommend a taste of the Parkers deep-fried version that of course features a crunchy exterior and impossibly juicy meat as the focal point around mashed potatoes, corn, and everything else you’ll eventually eat on Thanksgiving with your family. Week 12 – November 26: Kansas City Chiefs, 8:20pm — Cheesesteaks Why aren’t the Parkers doing a Thanksgiving tailgate on Thanksgiving night? Well, they figured the tryptophan would probably be overwhelming at this stage of Thanksgiving, so they’re venturing away from all the food you’ve likely eaten in the hours leading up to this perennial enormous regular-season battle between the Bills and Chiefs. And the Parkers Cheesesteaks could hold their own on any corner on the streets of Philadelphia. Trust me. Ask for extra cheese. Thank me later. Week 15 – December 19: Chicago Bears — Italian beef A cousin of the Cheesesteaks, I actually slightly prefer the Italian beef — my last name should be a dead giveaway I’d have this take. Of course, this menu item from Rory and Ray is a nod to one of Chicago’s most revered culinary offerings, which just so happens to be the city’s version of the beef on weck. The spicy giardiniera — finely diced peppers, carrots, celery — elevate this sandwich into the stratosphere. And the warm, seasoned roast beef will warm your insides ahead of this super-fun AFC-NFC showdown between two of the best improvisational quarterbacks in the NFL. Week 18 – January 10: New York Jets, TBD — Smash burgers I adore smash burgers, and every time I eat one, I wonder… how and why were we not always eating burgers this way… two patties, pressed thin, with ample amounts of melted cheese to hold them together? And the Parkers have perfected the on-site smash burger… Ray is normally on the flat-top, precisely flattening each patty before loading with cheese. Rory’s responsibilities come in the made-to-order building of your burger. And he will walk you through the process once your patties are ready to be assembled between two buns. Because the Parkers have gotten so good with the presentation — and taste — of their smash burgers, this is an exquisite cap to the Bills 2026 regular season at this tailgate. Playoffs — TBD Among the menu items the Parkers have done in the past that would be possible during a Bills playoff run: Garbage Plates (unequivocally my favorite, thanks in large part to Mrs. Parker’s meat sauce) Hibachi (a gigantic undertaking but Michelin-star worthy) Burritos (made to your exact specifications, Chipotle-style) Breakfast (bacon, sausage, eggs, all sizzling on the griddle) Deep-fried everything (bring anything you want, the Parkers will deep fry right in front of your eyes) Spaghetti and meatballs (I never knew I needed this Italian classic before a football game, until I went to a Parker Tailgate) What is your tailgate scene like? Are you already planned out with specific menu items? Leave a comment explaining everything in detail!

summary: On her latest Making Monsters podcast, Taylor Doll is joined by former Chicago Bears cornerback Jerry Azumah to talk about the newest Chicago Bears player, Jeffery Simmons, and the immediate impact he’ll have on this defense. They also dive into the Bears v. Seattle Seahawks game and what it will take for the Bears to […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 4: Nick Emmanwori #3 of the Seattle Seahawks in action during the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at Lumen Field on October 4, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images On her latest Making Monsters podcast, Taylor Doll is joined by former Chicago Bears cornerback Jerry Azumah to talk about the newest Chicago Bears player, Jeffery Simmons, and the immediate impact he’ll have on this defense. They also dive into the Bears v. Seattle Seahawks game and what it will take for the Bears to upset the defending champion on the road. Taylor is then joined by Bob Condotta of the Seattle Times, who shares the Seahawks’ perspective after they made a big trade for Quenton Nelson to try to spark their run game and protect Sam Darnold. Taylor and Bob chat about all things Seattle, plus this possible chess match between Ben Johnson and Mike Macdonald, and how Macdonald’s defense will attack the Bears. “They don’t blitz a ton. You know, traditionally, they’re not the biggest blitzing team ever. What they do more is try to bring pressure from different spots than you’ll see,” Condotta said. “So, it’s not always necessarily bringing like six guys, but it’s bringing four or five guys, but not from spots you necessarily thought those guys were coming from.” Condotta then discussed Seattle’s biggest X factor. “And that’s where Nick Emmanwori has become such a factor because he’s basically, essentially a strong side linebacker, but people make a big deal out of the Seahawks always playing nickel because they look at Emmanwori being listed as a safety, but you know, essentially a strong side linebacker. But you know, they can put him on the defensive line, and he’s just like a rush end.” ”It makes it kind of hard to know what they’re doing with him on this play, where what is he going to do, and you know you can rush him and drop someone else, and that’s where I think McDonald is really at his most dangerous is devising things like that.“ Besides previewing the game, Azumah also got into the big Simmons trade, and what else he’d like to see the Bears do. “I would like to see a defensive back, particularly a corner, to go over to the Chicago Bears,” he said about another possible trade. “I think that they could use the depth. There’ve been some issues in the secondary, but you know, Dennis Allen, he runs a very precise system, and the DBs have to basically match up to the wide receivers, and sometimes they lose. So I think that with Simmons being there, I think that that’s going to help out the secondary tremendously, but I wouldn’t mind seeing a depth move at corner.” Check out the full show in either of the embeds below, or anywhere you get your podcasts. title: The Bengals offensive line has been REALLY good this season
summary: It’s so interesting how when there’s a problem, whether on your favorite sports team or in everyday life, you complain non-stop about it. Then when it’s remedied, you don’t say a peep, maybe not even acknowledging that not only is it remedied but also working really well. The Bengals’ offensive line fits that exact description. […]
full_text: It’s so interesting how when there’s a problem, whether on your favorite sports team or in everyday life, you complain non-stop about it. Then when it’s remedied, you don’t say a peep, maybe not even acknowledging that not only is it remedied but also working really well. The Bengals’ offensive line fits that exact description. For years, Bengals fans complained about the team’s offensive line. Sometimes unfairly, but the criticism was fair more often than not for the first six years of Joe Burrow’s career. But over the last four years, the Bengals have quietly built what is now one of the NFL’s best offensive lines. Through six games, the Bengals have allowed just 10 sacks. And this is the heart of their success this season: Five of those sacks came in Week 2 against Houston. That means, in the other five games, Joe Burrow has only been sacked an average of one time per game. One time per game. That’s it. It’s been four years since the Bengals were in the Playoffs. The last time they played a playoff game was in the AFC Championship Game in January of 2023. They did so with three backup offensive linemen taking the field that night at Arrowhead Stadium. That night, the Bengals gained zero yards in the first quarter, and Joe Burrow was sacked on the Bengals’ final offensive play of the game. Less than two months later, the Bengals swung big and signed the best left tackle in free agency in Orlando Brown Jr.. Brown has signed multiple contract extensions with the Bengals since then. After Week 2, there was concern about him, and rightfully so. He had a rough preseason and training camp. But since Week 2 against Houston, have you even noticed him? It was worth keeping your stock in him. With the 18th pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, the Bengals drafted Amarius Mims out of Georgia. There was concern over his limited playing time in college, but that’s not at all the conversation now about the Bengals’ franchise right tackle. He looks like the second coming of Willie Anderson. Watch the play where Burrow stepped up in the pocket and found Tee Higgins for a 44-yard gain Sunday. At the outset of the play, Mims erased Ravens edge rusher Mike Green completely out of the play. It was impressive. How about the interior of the Bengals’ offensive line? Ted Karras is the only starter from the Bengals’ offensive line from that 2022 AFC Championship still with the team. He’s as solid as they come and a true leader on this team. Dylan Fairchild is unnoticeable at left guard. Yes, he’s had a couple of key holding penalties this season, but he’s playing really well in his second season. He looks like a home run who the Bengals drafted in the third round of the 2025 Draft. Dalton Risner signed with the Bengals last August, just a week before the season started. He’s blocking incredibly well both in the passing and running games. Since becoming the full-time starter at right guard in the middle of last season, the Bengals’ offense has been much more fluid upfront. In the second half Sunday, Joe Burrow had clean pockets every time he dropped back to pass. When was the last time you saw the Bengals control the line of scrimmage like that, especially in a division game? The Bengals finally have a really good offensive line in front of Joe Burrow. They deserve their credit, even if they want to go through life anonymously. Fans complained about the Bengals’ offensive line for years and, more often than not, rightfully so. But now, fans aren’t talking about the Bengals’ offensive line even though they deserve a lot of credit. That’s a good thing. Still, though, the Bengals’ offensive line is playing really good football heading into November.

title: Appreciating the career year Tee Higgins is having with the Bengals
summary: When the Cincinnati Bengals drafted Tee Higgins in the second round of the 2020 Draft, it was a revival of something “cool” in Cincinnati. With their first two picks in that franchise-changing 2020 Draft, the Bengals selected Joe Burrow (No. 1 overall) and Tee Higgins (No. 33 overall). In doing so, they brought back a […]
full_text: When the Cincinnati Bengals drafted Tee Higgins in the second round of the 2020 Draft, it was a revival of something “cool” in Cincinnati. With their first two picks in that franchise-changing 2020 Draft, the Bengals selected Joe Burrow (No. 1 overall) and Tee Higgins (No. 33 overall). In doing so, they brought back a combination that took Cincinnati by storm 15 years prior; 9 + 85 = Cool. Carson Palmer and Chad Johnson made the Bengals cool in the mid-2000s. FOX19’s Jeremy Rauch did a story shortly after the 2020 Draft about how Burrow and Higgins would be bringing that cool combination back to The Jungle. Before the Bengals drafted Ja’Marr Chase the next year, with Chase now on his way towards becoming, arguably, the greatest wide receiver in Bengals history, it was Tee Higgins in the spotlight as Joe Burrow’s No. 1 wide receiver. The Bengals drafted Higgins to give Burrow a legitimate weapon to throw to, a rookie wide receiver to develop alongside Burrow in his rookie season. Burrow and Higgins quickly developed a strong connection, hooking up for four touchdowns and six straight games with Higgins going over 50 receiving yards. Higgins eclipsed 100 yards in two of those games. Six years later, and after five years of living in Ja’Marr Chase’s shadow, Tee Higgins is finally having a career year, his moment in the sun, you could say. But are we truly appreciating what Tee Higgins is doing through six games this season? He’s been playing like a WR1. Like a top 10 wide receiver in the NFL. Need proof? Higgins is currently No. 8 in the NFL with 571 receiving yards. In two of his last three games, Higgins has a combined 305 receiving yards. He has 266 receiving yards in his other four games, which is still a solid 66.5 receiving yards per game. Against Jacksonville in Week 4, Higgins was the Bengals’ best healthy wide receiver for three quarters. He caught 11 passes for 157 yards when the Jaguars’ defense knew the ball was going to him. Then against the Ravens, after being held without a catch in the first half, Higgins caught six passes for 148 yards and a touchdown in the second half. He took over the game, averaging 24.7 yards per reception and all six of his catches gaining a first down. There’s a reason Joe Burrow said Tee Higgins is a need back in 2024. Higgins can change any game with his vertical route running, big-play ability, and his knack for making chunk catches over the middle of the field. But he hasn’t been a streaky receiver this season. Higgins has 50+ receiving yards in five of the Bengals’ six games this season. In fact, he has over 90 receiving yards in four of his six games. Plus, he has five+ receptions in four of the Bengals’ six games. Higgins’ average of 95.2 receiving yards per game is by far his career-high. Prior to this season, it was 77.9 in 2021. Right now, Higgins is on pace for 94 receptions for 1,617 yards and six touchdowns. Higgins’ career-high in receptions is 74 in both 2021 and 2022, when the Bengals’ offense was producing explosive plays every week and becoming the well-oiled machine we know it as today. Tee’s previous career-high in receiving yards is 1,091 in 2021. You know why Burrow said Tee is a need? Because when he’s playing like he’s playing through six games this season, that’s when this Bengals’ offense is at its best and most explosive. Higgins is currently averaging 17.3 yards per reception. His next-closest career-high in a single season is 15.6 in 2023. Even in the game against Houston when Ja’Marr Chase made his ridiculous highlight-reel catch in the corner of the end zone, Higgins was, arguably, the Bengals’ best and most important receiver on the field. Higgins led the team with 95 receiving yards in that game and made two key third-down catches for first downs. Ja’Marr Chase had two catches on the Bengals’ fourth touchdown drive against Baltimore that sealed the game, including a brutal hip turn to escape two Ravens’ defenders that turned a short pass into a 30-yard gain. Higgins, though, was the star in that second half. Ja’Marr Chase is still, arguably, the best wide receiver in the NFL. After all, he’s tied for fourth in receiving touchdowns in the NFL with five through Week 7. He’s going to have that huge game soon that we have seen one or more times in every season of his career. Right now, though, let’s appreciate the career year Tee Higgins is having. He was a need for a reason. Joe Burrow and the Bengals’ offense are benefiting mightily from him right now.
