(Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns announced their inactives for today’s game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. For much of the week, we thought the team would have to do some maneuvering of moves on the offensive line, since RT Tytus Howard missed practice all week with a concussion. However, on Saturday, the team got some good news on his status, and he is active for today’s game. Also active is CB Myles Harden , who was the lone player in doubt with a questionable status heading into the game. All things considered, Cleveland is as healthy as can be heading into this game. The biggest question mark heading into the game was who the team’s backup quarterback would be, now that QB Dillon Gabriel is back for the first time this season. Head coach Todd Monken did confirm on Friday that QB Shedeur Sanders would be the team’s backup still, so then the question shifted to who would be designated as the third quarterback on the inactive list. The answer is in: it’s Gabriel, meaning QB Taylen Green is ineligible to play for the first time this season. Gabriel will only play if both Sanders and QB Deshaun Watson suffer injuries. The rest of the Browns’ inactives are the usual crew: Browns Inactives QB Dillon Gabriel (third QB) QB Taylen Green RB Audric Estime C Parker Brailsford LB Justin Jefferson CB Noah Igbinoghene Steelers Inactives QB Will Howard (third QB) QB Drew Allar RB Eli Heidenreich WR Ben Skowronek CB Brandin Echols CB Doneiko Slaughter Meanwhile, the Steelers, also don’t have any major additions to their inactive list. However, it is worth noting that wide receivers Michael Pittman Jr and Roman Wilson are on injured reserve, and the team elevated WR Brandon Smith from the practice squad for some depth help.

title: Browns vs. Steelers Week 8 is a big example of why we are glad CLE didn’t punt on the season
summary: While yesterday was Halloween, Sunday of Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season feels like it could be a trick or treat for Cleveland Browns fans. Few expected the Browns to be 5-2, including 2-0 in the AFC North, heading into today’s game, but here we are. A divisional face-off with the Pittsburgh Steelers that […]
full_text: While yesterday was Halloween, Sunday of Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season feels like it could be a trick or treat for Cleveland Browns fans. Few expected the Browns to be 5-2, including 2-0 in the AFC North , heading into today’s game, but here we are. A divisional face-off with the Pittsburgh Steelers that will decide the divisional lead and potentially impact NFL trade deadline decisions to kick off November. There was a time this offseason when many wondered if Cleveland would punt on the season, given QB Deshaun Watson’s contract and a swath of long-term veterans hitting the free agent market. The belief was GM Andrew Berry would trade back in the NFL draft, limit his veteran free agent signings, and build for the future when a young franchise quarterback was added to the team. Full disclosure, it was at that point the rest of this article was written. A combination of communication and timing issues kept it from being published; this is me taking responsibility, but I held on to it believing I would either be able to use it like this or, if things went horribly wrong this season, as a “see, they should have punted.” Excited to edit the piece slightly, with the former being the reason. It is games like Week 8, with so much on the line and so much excitement, that Curtiss had in mind when he encouraged the team to not punt and instead to build: Rooting for an NFL team can either be fun or miserable. Based on the moves that the team does during the offseason, fans are either bracing for a Super Bowl run or preparing for a rebuild. For the Cleveland Browns, at one point this team was in the playoff discussion not so long ago. Now, the team is in the middle of a roster “retool,” not a rebuild. Offensively, the unit looks much improved on paper, but the quarterback position is still unsettled. Defensively, this is still one of the top units in the league, assuming that defensive end Myles Garrett will still be on the team when training camp rolls around ( We all know what happened there ). The fanbase is mixed on what the Browns will be this season. Half of the fanbase believes the team will be picking top 5 in the draft again next year, while the other half believes that this team could sneak into the playoffs. It’s something that’s worth discussing. Internally, the Cleveland organization might have a different view of what the team will be than the fans’ perspective. Browns owner Jimmy Haslam is a polarizing figure in this city. Haslam is willing to do what it takes to put a winning product on the field, but oftentimes he gets far too involved in the process of doing that. He has at least taken accountability of that, to some extent: Some context here: #Browns Jimmy Haslam: “Ownership takes full responsibility for where we are. To win eight games in two years is horrible. It’s totally unacceptable, OK? And it’s not gonna continue, OK? I want the fans to know we're as frustrated as you are." — Mary Kay Cabot (@MaryKayCabot) January 6, 2026 Haslam owning up to the team’s recent struggles is growth in terms of accountability. He understands why fans are frustrated, and he is doing whatever it takes to fix it. That is why it was in the best interest of the Browns to be competitive instead of punting this season. Giving up on a season before it starts is rarely beneficial to anyone, especially a skeptical one. However, the way the team operated this offseason shows that they aren’t punting; instead, they want to be competitive. The offense has been overhauled, from the offensive line to the skill positions. Quarterback aside, the unit looks better on paper. The schedule should also be taken into account as well. Being competitive this season can be beneficial for all parties. It helps establish a standard for a very young roster. Teaching the new players brought in the last two years that losing is not acceptable. Last season, the team was not as bad as their record indicated, and this upcoming season it would be disingenuous to think that this team won’t be better than last season due to the moves they made in free agency and in the draft, despite the Garrett trade. Now, Browns fans wake up after an extra hour of sleep with a chance to watch their team and see if they are ready to really compete for an AFC North title (which would be their first) and still have excitement heading into the third month of the 2026 NFL season. A huge improvement over the last two seasons; so glad the team didn’t punt on 2026.

full_text: The Cleveland Browns have had multiple players step up on both sides of the ball this season, and some of their efforts may have gone largely unnoticed. There are a few players in particular who deserve recognition. Emmanuel McNeil-Warren was selected in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft and has already proven why he can be such a valuable asset to the Browns. He has stepped up in key moments to disrupt opposing offenses, particularly in the matchups against the Pittsburgh Steelers and Baltimore Ravens. His ability to make big plays that can affect the outcome of the game deserves more respect and attention. Harold Fannin Jr. has been one of the more productive players in the Cleveland offense. He has recorded 25 receptions for 257 yards and three touchdowns this season, giving Deshaun Watson a reliable target in the passing game. Although he has earned plenty of respect from Browns fans, he deserves more recognition on a national level. Some may say we’ve underrated Jared Verse by even suggesting Cleveland could listen to trade offers for him . title: Browns roster moves: Things going Cleveland’s way, finally
summary: The Cleveland Browns received a bit of good news on Saturday regarding the game-day roster for Sunday’s key divisional game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. full_text: (Photo by Al Pereira/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns received a bit of good news on Saturday regarding the game-day roster for Sunday’s key divisional game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Starting right tackle Tytus Howard, who was originally listed as questionable while dealing with a concussion, cleared the league-mandated concussion protocol on Saturday and can play on Sunday. That means the Browns will be at full strength on the offensive line as they look to break a 23-year, regular-season losing streak to the Steelers in Pittsburgh. Starting cornerback Myles Harden is still questionable, however, as he is dealing with a hamstring injury, which could test Cleveland’s depth in the secondary if Harden is not able to go. The Browns appear to be confident, however, as they only made one practice squad elevation for the game, and that was to elevate rookie tight end Carsen Ryan from the practice squad. Ryan was released prior to the game against the Tennessee Titans to open a roster spot for running back Dylan Sampson to return from injured reserve, and subsequently signed back with the Browns to their practice squad. The seventh-round selection from BYU has played in six games for the Browns, but has only played two snaps on offense, registering no stats, and 73 snaps on special teams, making one tackle. Pittsburgh made a pair of roster moves on Saturday, signing wide receiver Brandon Smith to the 53-man roster from the practice squad, and elevating wide receiver Brandon Johnson from the practice squad. title: Keys before kickoff: Cowboys vs Cardinals Week 8
summary: The 3-4 Dallas Cowboys look to begin a winning streak this week, facing off against the 2-5 Arizona Cardinals at AT&T Stadium. Here are three keys to the game. Run. The. Ball. Again. This is a copy and paste headline from last week’s keys before kickoff against the Eagles. Realistically, the mental reminder to run […]
full_text: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images | Getty Images The 3-4 Dallas Cowboys look to begin a winning streak this week, facing off against the 2-5 Arizona Cardinals at AT&T Stadium. Here are three keys to the game. Run. The. Ball. Again. This is a copy and paste headline from last week’s keys before kickoff against the Eagles. Realistically, the mental reminder to run the ball should be the priority just about every week. This football team is simply better, as any team would be, with a dominant rushing attack. Dak Prescott thrives off the play-action, the receivers face lighter coverages when teams have to commit resources in the box, and the defense gets to rest while the offense works down the field on an eight-minute drive. Against Philadelphia last week, Brian Schottenheimer remembered his team features one of the NFL’s best run blocking offensive lines. Dallas ran the ball on 37 designed attempts, paying immediate dividends in a 38-21 win over their division rival. This week against the Cardinals, the plan should be similar. This Cardinals defense has struggled against the run throughout the season, ranking 29th in rush success rate allowed, per SumerSports. It’s an extremely malleable defense that changes the looks they give opposing offenses weekly, but even with those changes they have not been able to slow down the rushing attack much this season. And when they commit the resources in the box to slow down Williams, Dallas should be able to exploit the secondary with their big playmakers on the outside. Contain Trey McBride The Cardinals tight end leads the NFL in receptions (59 for 472 yards with four touchdowns) and is Arizona’s clear number one threat. He’s a volume target for quarterback Jacoby Brissett on an offense that lacks much firepower elsewhere. Dallas will need to contain McBride in the slot, out wide, on screens, on downfield throws, and eliminate the big yards after the catch. McBride truly is the ultimate weapon that deserves the utmost respect from opposing defenses each week. Defensive coordinator Christian Parker will have to devise a game plan to limit the one big weapon Arizona possesses. If he’s able to do so, this is a game that Dallas should win relatively easily, regardless of the history between the two teams. Get off to a quick start The quality of the Cowboys opponents have helped the defense play better over the last three weeks, at least from the perspective of the final scoreboard. But they are still far from being considered a “good” defense. One of those reasons is the fact that they cannot seem to get consistent stops early. Last week against a bad Eagles offense, Dallas surrendered two touchdowns on the first two drives. They would go on to let up just seven points for the rest of the game, but the lack of early success will certainly bite them if it continues this season. The Cardinals offense has failed to put up 20 or more point in three of seven weeks. Four of their losses have been by two or more scores. If you can get a couple of stops early against Jeremiyah Love and Trey McBride, Arizona has shown that they’ll let these games get out of hand in a hurry. The Cowboys have not shown the ability to shut out opponents early this season, but the opportunity will be there this week against another bad team. Offensively, Dallas needs to end their drives with seven, not three. The Cardinals will surely mix things up on defense, as they do every week, so the Cowboys need to be willing to adapt to what they see on the field. Balance and complementary offense will be a crucial factor in this week’s matchup. When the Cardinals commit resources to stopping Javonte Williams, get the playmakers on the outside involved. When they sit back in a shell coverage to remove the deep threat, make them pay for their light boxes with a steady rushing attack. There is also a chance we see the Cardinals attack Dallas in a similar manner to the Buccaneers and Packers games. If so, Brian Schottenheimer and Dak Prescott need to demonstrate the ability to overcome the disguised blitzes and a stacked line of scrimmage. The Cowboys have a shot this spooky Halloween weekend to end the 20-year nightmare that has been the Arizona Cardinals. If Dallas can jump out to an early lead, the Cardinals have demonstrated the lack of offensive firepower to keep up. If the Cowboys allow Arizona to hang around, however, this team will fight tooth and nail in a bitter dogfight. Dallas has not shown the world that they have the ability to put games away early. What better time than now to do just that, and to put an end to this matchup that’s plagued them for two decades.

title: 3 things to buy, 1 thing to sell for the Cowboys vs Cardinals
summary: The Dallas Cowboys finally put together a complete offensive performance in Philadelphia, and now they will try to carry that momentum into their matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. Javonte Williams delivered a career night against the Eagles, CeeDee Lamb found the end zone twice, and the Cowboys’ rushing attack finally looked like the unit it […]
full_text: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys finally put together a complete offensive performance in Philadelphia, and now they will try to carry that momentum into their matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. Javonte Williams delivered a career night against the Eagles, CeeDee Lamb found the end zone twice, and the Cowboys’ rushing attack finally looked like the unit it was supposed to be at the start of the season. The Cardinals have struggled defensively against the run, their offensive line is dealing with injuries, and the Cowboys are beginning to show some improvement against opposing rushing attacks. Concerns remain, particularly about Dallas’ tight end production and third-down defense. Here are some buy/sells for Week 8. Buy: Javonte Williams After waiting six weeks for Dallas to give him a substantial workload, Javonte Williams finally showed what he can do when the coaching staff commits to the ground game. His career performance against Philadelphia should earn him another healthy workload against Arizona. Williams rushed for 155 yards and a touchdown on 25 carries against the Eagles, averaging 6.2 yards per attempt. It was his best performance of the season and the most rushing yards by a Cowboys running back in nearly a decade. More importantly, it helped Dallas establish an offensive identity that had been missing during its consecutive losses to Tampa Bay and Green Bay. Through seven games, Williams has recorded 472 rushing yards and eight touchdowns on 110 carries, averaging 4.3 yards per attempt with eight rushing touchdowns so far in 2026. Arizona should provide another favorable opportunity. The Cardinals have allowed 126.4 rushing yards per game, ranking 24th in the league. Dallas finally showed what its offensive line can do when it moves downhill, and Williams should have opportunities to exploit that matchup. The biggest takeaway from Philadelphia was that Williams needs to be a focal point of this offense, not an afterthought. Schottenheimer should keep feeding him to achieve the balance he always talks about. Buy: CeeDee Lamb This is getting easy; this conversation comes up, and putting CeeDee Lamb in the mix is a no-brainer with how he’s performed so far this season. Lamb continues to remind everyone why he is the centerpiece of Dallas’ passing attack. Against Philadelphia, Lamb caught five passes for 74 yards and two touchdowns, giving Prescott another dependable option in the red zone. Over seven games, Lamb has caught 53 passes for 651 yards and six touchdowns. He leads the Cowboys in receiving yards and has been one of the team’s most consistent offensive weapons throughout the season. The Cardinals have struggled to consistently contain opposing offenses, and their secondary will have to account for both Lamb and George Pickens. That creates opportunities for Lamb to find favorable coverage, particularly if Dallas continues to establish Williams and force Arizona to respect the run. Lamb has six touchdowns through seven games, and his yardage production, second only to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, has become a Cowboys staple as Dallas looks to build consistency. Expect him to remain a major part of the offensive game plan against Arizona. Buy: The Cowboys’ run defense This might be the most surprising buy of the week, but the Cowboys’ run defense deserves some credit for its recent improvement. It is far from a finished product, but after being gashed by Tampa Bay, Dallas has shown signs that it can finally, at the very least, slow down opposing rushing attacks. The Cowboys allowed Tampa Bay 241 rushing yards in Week 5, a performance that exposed how vulnerable the defense can be against a physical ground game. Since then, however, Dallas has allowed just 57 rushing yards to Green Bay and 121 to Philadelphia. Yes, the Saquon Barkley injury did play a role here. That averages 89 rushing yards allowed per game over the last two weeks, a significant improvement from the problems Dallas faced earlier in the season. The defensive front has started creating more disruption, and the return of key second-level contributors has helped the unit play with more consistency. Arizona’s backfield presents an interesting test. Rookie Jeremiyah Love is expected to return after missing two games with an ankle injury, but the Cardinals will be without right guard Jon Gaines II, while center Hjalte Froholdt is questionable. Tyler Allgeier has also been dealing with a toe injury. Even with Love returning, the uncertainty along the offensive line could make it difficult for Arizona to establish the ground game, and Love hasn’t exactly set the world on fire when healthy. If the defensive front controls the line of scrimmage and prevents Love from finding room to operate, it will force Jacoby Brissett to shoulder more of the offensive workload. The Cowboys have not suddenly become an elite run defense, but the last two games have been encouraging. Another decent performance against Arizona would go a long way toward showing that the improvement is real rather than a temporary stretch. Sell: The Cowboys’ tight end position Man, there was a time the tight end position in Dallas was a lock. Now the position has increasingly disappeared from Dallas’ passing attack, and it is becoming difficult to view the group as a difference-maker. Jake Ferguson’s production has fallen off sharply, while Brevyn Spann-Ford hasn’t received enough opportunities in the passing game to become a consistent contributor. Ferguson has struggled to establish himself as any sort of contributor. Drops have been an issue, and against Philadelphia, Ferguson finished with no receptions on his lone target and played fewer than 56% of the offensive snaps for the second straight week. Spann-Ford has seen more opportunities recently, including a season-high 52.9% snap share against Philadelphia. He caught both of his targets for 11 yards, but his overall production remains limited. Through seven games, he has recorded just nine receptions for 79 yards on 13 targets, leaving plenty to be desired from a position that was supposed to provide another reliable option for Prescott. The Cowboys have talented receivers in Lamb and Pickens, and the emergence of Williams as a consistent rushing threat has helped diversify the offense. But the tight end position should still be contributing more than it has. Whether it is Ferguson struggling to regain his confidence or Spann-Ford being used primarily as a blocker, Dallas is not getting much production from the group. For now, the Cowboys should continue leaning on their receivers and running backs while searching for more answers at tight end.
author: Jorge Guajardo

title: 5 things to watch when the Cowboys host the Cardinals
summary: The Dallas Cowboys will be trying to do something they haven’t done all season. Win two games in a row. Standing in their way is the lowly Arizona Cardinals, who sit at 2-5, last place in the NFC West. The Cowboys are coming off a convincing Monday night win over the Philadelphia Eagles and it […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys will be trying to do something they haven’t done all season. Win two games in a row. Standing in their way is the lowly Arizona Cardinals, who sit at 2-5, last place in the NFC West. The Cowboys are coming off a convincing Monday night win over the Philadelphia Eagles and it would be refreshing to see them do a little more of the good stuff and a little less of the bad stuff. Will they be able to pull it off? Here are five things to watch when the Cowboys host the Cardinals on Sunday. 1. Trey’s company Who’s Jacoby Brissett throwing to? That’s the easiest question one could ask as we all know that tight end Trey McBride will get a heavy dose of targets. That’s usually the case as McBride is one of the best tight ends in the league. He can do it all. Find soft spots in coverage, overwhelm smaller defenders, and turn routine plays into big gains. He’s a monster. No tight end in the league has been targeted more than McBride this season. Who will draw the assignment of keeping him contained? Rookie safety Caleb Downs is the optimal choice. While he’s better playing downhill, Downs will have to roam outside his comfort zone and chase after McBride. The young defensive back has had his fair share of challenges in coverage this season, but he’ll need to squeeze and come at times to minimize the damage of the Cardinals’ biggest receiving weapon. 2. UnCeeDed territory While McBride leading all tight ends in targets surprises no one, you might be shocked to learn that CeeDee Lamb leads all wide receivers in targets this season. The Cowboys star receiver was hot just a few weeks ago, reeling off three straight games with over 100 yards receiving. He’s since cooled off, stringing together three straight without reaching 75 yards receiving. It is now time for him to get back on that hot streak? Doing so against the Cardinals would be good timing, as he’s never caught a touchdown pass against them before. In fact, Arizona is the only NFC team that has kept him out of the end zone. Despite not having a huge yardage outing, Lamb is coming off a two-touchdown performance against the Eagles, and he now goes against a defense that has allowed the most points in the league. 3. Klaymation Last week defensive coordinator Christian Parker went against his old team and his group arguably put together their best performance. Granted, it was against a depleted Eagles offense. This week offensive coordinator Klayton Adams will get another crack at his former team. Last year, when he faced the Cardinals, the Cowboys offense only put up 10 points, their lowest output of the season. Last year was against Jonathan Gannon’s group, this year he’ll face Mike LaFleur and a new staff, however, defensive coordinator Nick Rallis remains. Does Adams’ old team know his style all too well? The Cowboys’ offense is coming off its best rushing performance of the year and it would be great if Adams’ group could build off of it. Another game where Javonte Williams wears down the defense with a little sudden acceleration of Tyler Goodson mixed in would be welcomed. And there is no better time against a former team who had your number this time a year ago. 4. Love on the run The Cardinals aren’t the only defense that struggles with the run, as it’s still been a problem for the Cowboys’ defense as well. Dallas was fortunate they faced an ailing Saquon Barkley last week, otherwise, the Eagles could have attacked on the ground more effectively. This week, they should get another running back returning from injury who also happens to be a top-3 overall pick in the draft. Jeremiah Love has been nursing an ankle injury and is still waiting for a breakout game. The Cardinals will attempt to attack with the run to take pressure off quarterback Jacoby Brissett. Whether it’s Love, Tyler Algier, or Bam Knight, the Cardinals will look to exploit any weaknesses in the Cowboys’ run defense. 5. Ending the streak The Cardinals have won four straight against the Cowboys, which is weird because Arizona hasn’t been a good team in recent years. The last two times they’ve played, the Cardinals have finished 3-14 and 4-13, but for some reason, they always show up against Dallas. But they don’t just beat the Cowboys, they embarrass them. During this four-game drought, the Cardinals have led by at least 12 points in each of those games. This game feels eerily similar. Arizona is bad again, and everyone expects the Cowboys to beat them, but for that to happen, the Cowboys must break this curse and show up ready to go so they can leave all that disappointing play behind them. That might be easier said than done, as this year’s team has been notorious for putting up disappointing showings.

title: Cowboys news: Dallas has a Cardinal problem
summary: The Cowboys will try to get rid of the curse of the Cardinals this Halloween weekend and in the process get a win streak started. New acquisitions like Joey Porter Jr. seem to be paying off for Dallas, but others like Rashan Gary are having a tougher time. Let’s get to the Cowboys news. Cowboys […]
full_text: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images | Getty Images The Cowboys will try to get rid of the curse of the Cardinals this Halloween weekend and in the process get a win streak started. New acquisitions like Joey Porter Jr. seem to be paying off for Dallas, but others like Rashan Gary are having a tougher time. Let’s get to the Cowboys news. Cowboys lengthy history of problems with Cardinals stretches 2 decades – Ben Grimaldi, Cowboys Wire Cowboys have a boogeyman that has made past matchups downright spooky. The Dallas Cowboys have a problem with the Arizona Cardinals , spanning the course of 20 years and 10 matchups. A few teams have had the Cowboys’ number over that same time period, but none have a hold over Jerry Jones’ organization quite like the Cardinals . The Green Bay Packers and San Francisco 49ers are the prime examples of giving the Cowboys a tough time recently, but Dallas has won three games over the Packers and five over the 49ers in the last 20 seasons. Despite being the more consistent team over the past two decades, the Cowboys have rarely been able to solve the Cardinals’ riddle. Early returns on Joey Porter Jr. trade prove Cowboys duped the Steelers – Jason Kandel , The Landry Hat The Cowboys look like they got another steal from Pittsburgh. Last season, George Pickens broke out after coming over to Dallas from Pittsburgh, and this season, Joey Porter Jr. is the one validating Jerry Jones’ decision-making. It was a risky play to send a 2028 second-rounder to the Steelers in exchange for a CB in a contract year , but fortune favors the bold. Thankfully, early returns suggest this has been a great move . While Porter Jr. has been limited to just three games with America’s Team, the play we’ve seen from him suggests that, despite this team’s many issues on defense, he’s been as advertised as the shutdown CB1 fans were hoping for. 6 Make-or-Break Players Standing Between the Cowboys and Back-to-Back Wins in Week 8 – Sahil Goswami, Athlon Sports These players will decide if the Cowboys can make it two straight wins for the first time this season. Lamb has never beaten the Cardinals in seven seasons. He has 53 catches for 651 yards and six touchdowns, including two scores against the Eagles, and his 89.6 grade ranks eighth among 76 receivers, per PFF . “We’ve played them in prime time, they beat us there. So, we need to treat them as if they are a Super Bowl contending team,” Lamb told DallasCowboys.com . Arizona allows 8.5 yards per pass attempt and has given up 17 touchdown passes, most in the league. Linebacker Jack Gibbens allowed five catches on five targets for 99 yards against Denver, according to PFF, and the big plays keep coming . Cowboys’ Jerry Jones Defends Struggling $32 Million Starter – Sean Deveney, Heavy.com Jerry Jones gives encouraging words to one of his underachieving players. On Friday, in an appearance on 1 05.3 The Fan in Dallas , team owner Jerry Jones was asked about Gary, and suggested that the struggles are not on Gary, but on the fact that the Cowboys defense has had so much upheaval and is trying to pull itself together. Said Jones: “He is part of a new group. I probably underestimated the challenge of coming in and changing out the coaches, changing out 60, 70% of the personnel, and a new scheme and how maybe even some new technique, all of those generally contribute to playing. Because he is an outstanding football player.” 3 things Cowboys HC Brian Schottenheimer can carry into week 8 – Connor Livesay, Blogging the Boys Here’s what the head coach should bring over into their game against Arizona. One of the major changes in the offense we saw last week was their aggressiveness to push the ball down the field in the passing game. After six weeks of seeing Dak Prescott’s ADOT rank near the bottom of the league, the Cowboys generated explosive plays at an extremely high clip against a defense that had not given up many explosive passing plays to start the season. With so many defenses sitting on the stop-routes that have been in heavy rotation to start the year, the Cowboys were able to hit multiple big plays using sluggos on the outside, which should be there for them yet again against a Cardinals secondary that has struggled to slow down opposing passing games in 2026 (31st in dropback epa/play and 20th in dropback success rate).

They play four out of their next five games at home and will face only one team with a winning record. The Cowboys […]
full_text: Christopher Torres/Fort Worth Star-Telegram/Tribune News Service via Getty Images After last week’s 38-21 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles, the Dallas Cowboys have a chance to stack multiple wins together with a favorable schedule ahead of them in the month of November. They play four out of their next five games at home and will face only one team with a winning record. The Cowboys kick off the month of November against the Arizona Cardinals and close it out against the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving. Both of these games should be winnable, and we’ll make a case for why they can win all of them in November. Arizona Cardinals (2-5) 4 th in the AFC West Despite getting upset by them a year ago, the Cardinals shouldn’t pose a threat to the Cowboys. There in the midst of a rebuild and could be looking to tank the season in order to draft the next franchise QB. With their playoff hopes still alive and with home field advantage, Dallas should be able to take care of business. Indianapolis Colts (2-4) 2 nd in the AFC South The Colts may still be currently sitting second in the AFC South division, but all signs indicate their preparing for the future. They’ve already traded Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, and there are rumors RB Jonathan Taylor and WR Josh Downs could be moved as well. Selling off all their talent should give the Cowboys a path to victory, despite this being the only away game in November. San Francisco 49ers (6-1) 1 st in the NFC West The 49ers are only team with a winning record the Cowboys will face in November. They are currently on their bye week trying to get healthy with many key players injured. On the flipside, Dallas is getting healthy at the right time. The 49ers hot start has started to wobble as they struggled to hold off the Commanders, and then lost to the Falcons. The Cowboys will be at home – so between injuries, home field advantage, and the 49ers slowing down after a very hot start, maybe the Cowboys can squeeze out an upset. Tennessee Titans (1-6) 4 th AFC South After shipping out DT Jeffrey Simmons to the Chicago Bears, and with potential other trades in the works before the November 10 deadline, the Colts are yet another team who are preparing for the future by acquiring as much draft capital as possible. Facing a struggling QB and a talent deprived Titans roster should work in the Cowboys favor, earning them another “W”. Philadelphia Eagles (2-5) 3 rd in the NFC East Division rival games can always go either way, but with the way the Eagles season is going, and after the Cowboys thoroughly throttled them last week, there’s no reason to believe Dallas can’t secure a Thanksgiving day victory at home. The only question is will Tanner McKee still be their starter or will former Cowboys QB Joe Milton take over? Either way, the Cowboys should add another in the win column. What is your prediction for how many of these five games the Cowboys will actually win? Hit the comments and let us know.

title: Cowboys vs Cardinals: Writer predictions for Week 8
summary: Dallas returns home with some momentum after a convincing 38-21 win over Philadelphia. The Cowboys are now 3-4 and face a 2-5 Arizona team that has struggled for consistency on both sides of the ball. The challenge for Dallas is making sure Monday night’s performance becomes the start of something rather than another one-off result. […]
full_text: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images | Getty Images Dallas returns home with some momentum after a convincing 38-21 win over Philadelphia. The Cowboys are now 3-4 and face a 2-5 Arizona team that has struggled for consistency on both sides of the ball. The challenge for Dallas is making sure Monday night’s performance becomes the start of something rather than another one-off result. When Arizona has the ball Arizona will continue with Jacoby Brissett at quarterback, and the biggest threat in this offense is tight end Trey McBride. McBride produced 111 receiving yards against Denver and leads Arizona with 59 catches for 472 yards. Expect the Cardinals to use him heavily over the middle, especially against Dallas linebackers and safeties. Dallas will try to keep everything in front of them and force Arizona to put together long drives. The opportunity for the Cowboys pass rush is also there. Brissett was pressured on more than half of his dropbacks against Denver, while Dallas generated two sacks and an interception against Philadelphia. The Cowboys only have 10 sacks for the season, so this is another matchup where Quinnen Williams and the defensive front need to turn pressure into actual negative plays. When Dallas has the ball Dallas should start exactly where it finished in Philadelphia with Javonte Williams. The Cowboys rushed for 204 yards against the Eagles, with Williams producing 155 yards and a touchdown on 25 carries. That balance completely changed the offense. Dak Prescott only needed 27 pass attempts, was not sacked and threw three touchdowns without an interception. That is the formula Dallas has been searching for all season. Arizona gives them every reason to continue with it. The Cardinals allowed 377 total yards and 30 points to Denver last week, including a 62-yard quarterback run and several explosive plays. Arizona entered that game at the bottom of the NFL in points allowed, so Dallas should make this defense handle Williams before spreading the field with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Lamb scored twice against Philadelphia, while Pickens added another touchdown, giving Prescott several different ways to attack once Arizona starts committing defenders toward the run. Now onto the predictions from your BTB writers… Tom Ryle (4-3) I wasn’t really surprised to see the win last week, or to see the early game issues, but the finish was better than I expected. Frankly, they need something very similar against the Cardinals for the same reasons. This is not a good Arizona team and it has been getting kicked around by the good teams it plays. If the Cowboys really expect to be taken seriously, they need another strong win. I don’t know if this is more a prediction or a hope, but I’ll say DAL 34 ARI 19. Brandon Loree (5-2) Since 2021, the Dallas Cowboys haven’t won a game where they’ve scored 18 points or less. Conversely, Dallas has the fifth-most wins when they score 21 or more points. The Arizona Cardinals seem to have the Cowboys’ number, winning the last four matchups. Arizona isn’t great defensively, but their offense can be feisty headlined by Trey McBride and Jeremiyah Love potentially coming back from injury. I think this week’s game comes down to a Brandon Aubrey field goal, and the Cowboys are on the positive side of the stat above, winning 24-21. Dyllan Rivers (4-2) I feel less comfortable this week against a struggling Cardinals teams that still has some healthy playmakers on offense. Assuming he plays, the Cowboys have to eliminate running back Jeremiyah Love as well as tight end Trey McBride. I think they do just enough defensively to get the ball back to the offense to stack some scores at some point against a struggling Cardinals run defense. I’ll take Dallas 34-24 Matt Holleran (3-4) The Cowboys showed last week they are capable of beating an inferior opponent. The Arizona Cardinals fit that billing again this week, but it’s hard to trust the Cowboys when any sort of consistency is expected. I see this being a sloppy game, but when it matters most, Dallas’ offense makes the plays they need to. The Cowboys get a win and move back to .500 on the year. Give me Dallas in a weird one, 26-24. Mike Poland (3-4) The Cowboys have momentum and home field advantage here. Arizona are struggling to finish drives. They rank 22nd in the NFL in total offensive yards but rank 26th in points per game, and that’s down to the fact they rank dead last in redzone efficiency. They can move the ball to some degree through the air, but once in the redzone they fail to convert. On the opposite side, the Cardinals defense is allowing the most points per game, have the 11th-worst redzone efficiency, and rank 15th in third-conversion allowed. Dallas takes the win here 28-17.
author: Mike Poland

title: It’s been a very long time since the Cowboys won a home game vs. Cardinals
summary: Over the last decade, the NFC has had some Hall of Fame-level quarterback play, and the Dallas Cowboys have faced memorable names like Aaron Rodgers and Drew Brees. They’ve even played some Hall of Very Good quarterbacks in Matt Ryan, Russell Wilson, Eli Manning, and Cam Newton. Somehow, the rogues’ gallery of signal callers for […]
full_text: Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images | Getty Images Over the last decade, the NFC has had some Hall of Fame-level quarterback play, and the Dallas Cowboys have faced memorable names like Aaron Rodgers and Drew Brees. They’ve even played some Hall of Very Good quarterbacks in Matt Ryan, Russell Wilson, Eli Manning, and Cam Newton. Somehow, the rogues’ gallery of signal callers for the Cardinals—Kurt Warner, John Skelton, Kevin Kolb, Carson Palmer, Kyler Murray, Joshua Dobbs, and Jacoby Brissett—has an 8-1 record vs. Dallas since 2008. The last time the Cowboys beat Arizona at home was in 2005, when it was still Texas Stadium; Drew Bledsoe was the quarterback, and Bill Parcells was the head coach. Even against an NFC powerhouse like the Green Bay Packers, Dallas has managed a 2-7-1 record against their hated rival. The Cardinals have given the Cowboys the worst record against any NFC opponent during this stretch. Cowboys Regular Season Records vs NFC opponents since 2008 ( via Stathead ) Arizona Cardinals: 1-8 Green Bay Packers: 2-7-1 Chicago Bears: 3-5 New Orleans Saints: 4-6 Atlanta Falcons: 4-4 Seattle Seahawks: 5-5 Carolina Panthers: 5-3 Minnesota Vikings: 5-3 San Francisco 49ers: 5-3 Detroit Lions: 6-4 Los Angeles Rams: 6-3 Tampa Bay Buccaneers: 7-3 New York Giants: 24-12 Philadelphia Eagles: 20-16 Washington Commanders: 25-11 Can this version of the Cowboys finally get a home win against the Cardinals? Not much has changed on the roster from when Dallas faced them a year ago on Monday Night Football . Head coach Mike LaFleur is a new face, but Brissett is still at quarterback (for now), Trey McBride is at tight end, and Michael Wilson is still their No. 1 wide receiver. On the defensive side of the ball, Josh Sweat is there (for now), and he seems to have a career game whenever he plays the Cowboys. Same goes for safety Budda Baker. Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb said this week that he’s never beaten the Cardinals since he was drafted and that their energy has always been better than Dallas’s coming into the game. “They’ve always had more energy,” Lamb said via Todd Archer on X . “Just coming out in the game, they’re more excited regardless of if it was at 12 o’clock, Sunday night, Monday night. We played them in primetime, they beat us there. So just coming in, treating them as if they are a Super Bowl contending team, which they may be, you know what I’m saying? So hats off to them in their prep and we just got to go match them, if not overpower them.” The Cowboys are looking to get their first winning streak of the season going after taking care of business against a Philadelphia Eagles team that’s a shell of what it was even a year ago. With the New York Giants continuing to win and two games up over Dallas in the loss column, they need a win on Sunday to stay in the NFC East. Dallas came into the year preaching that things would be different this season. A win on Sunday will prove it, considering it’s been the same for Dallas at home against Arizona for over twenty years.
author: Brandon_Loree

title: Broncos WR Jaylen Waddle is trending in the right direction to play today vs. the Chiefs
summary: According to NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport, Denver Broncos star wide receiver Jaylen Waddle is “trending in the right direction” to play in today’s game vs. the Kansas City Chiefs. Waddle is listed as questionable for today’s game, but it appears the Broncos will have their explosive star wide receiver for today’s key divisional matchup. […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - OCTOBER 15: Denver Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (17) celebrates after a touchdown in the second quarter during a game between the Seattle Seahawks and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images According to NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport, Denver Broncos star wide receiver Jaylen Waddle is “trending in the right direction” to play in today’s game vs. the Kansas City Chiefs. Waddle is listed as questionable for today’s game, but it appears the Broncos will have their explosive star wide receiver for today’s key divisional matchup. #Broncos WR Jaylen Waddle, who has been dealing with a chest injury that he aggravated last week, is trending in the right direction to play, source says. — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 1, 2026 As we know, Waddle reaggravated a chest injury late in the victory over the Arizona Cardinals. He took an end around, bobbled and fumbled the ball, but was able to get back on it. However, he landed hard on his shoulder/chest and was removed from the game. Waddle did practice on a limited basis twice this week, which is a good sign, and he has already played through this injury, so hopefully it is not something that hampers him too much during today’s game. This seemed like the likely outcome after the Broncos did not elevate a wide receiver from the practice squad on Saturday. Instead, they elevated reserve running back Cody Schrader, who will serve as the Broncos RB3 today with RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie on the short-term IR, along with undrafted rookie offensive lineman Gavin Ortega. If the team felt Waddle would not have played, we likely would have seen a wide receiver elevated so all signs point to Waddle being good to go. This is big news for the Broncos because the Chiefs will be without rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane and veteran starter L’Jarius Sneed. Delane was downgraded to OUT on Saturday, while Sneed was placed on the injured reserve. Broncos quarterback Bo Nix and the Broncos pass catchers will need to take advantage of a weakened Chiefs secondary and have some explosive plays down the field today. Time for Jaylen Waddle to step up and Marvin Mims Jr. to make some money for himself with a big showing today. Trade rumors are swirling: Jonah Coleman is starting, Waddle is active, Mims is expected to see a larger role, and Bo Nix is looking to continue the momentum he built last week vs. the Cardinals. It should be a fascinating game for the Broncos offense and hopefully one that is full of big plays and an eventual Denver Broncos victory.

title: Broncos Country really confident about beating the Chiefs
summary: The 5-2 Broncos are hosting the 5-1 Chiefs, a team that looked for a minute like it might roll right through the division, the conference and the league on its way to the bye week of the playoffs. Until last week when the Seahawks published the blueprint on taking care of the Chiefs — pressure […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - DECEMBER 25: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos celebrates during an NFL football game against the Kansas City Chiefs at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 5-2 Broncos are hosting the 5-1 Chiefs, a team that looked for a minute like it might roll right through the division, the conference and the league on its way to the bye week of the playoffs. Until last week when the Seahawks published the blueprint on taking care of the Chiefs — pressure Mahomes, stop the run and also RUN. Although the Broncos couldn’t do any of those in their first meeting at Arrowhead on Monday Night Football, the offense has started to find some good rhythm, Bo Nix is looking like theQB we need, and the defense has gotten its act together. And even though it will take all that and maybe a little extra from the crowd, a huge chunk of Broncos Country sees a check in the W column by tonight. But even if Broncos Country is ahead of itself, the Broncos are treating this game like any other game — just gotta win it. “It’s the next one,” wide receiver Courtland Sutton said Wednesday. “It’s the most important one because it’s the next one. … Everyone understands that the divisional games weigh a little bit heavier in terms of the overall standings when we get to the end of it. But it’s the next one.” Keeping Bo Nix upright and not running for his life will be a big part of the formula, and Mike McGlinchey understands that the O-line’s role today is a big one. “All that matters is what happens right in front of your face, not the great story of the playoff picture or anything that everybody [externally] want to draw up,” tackle Mike McGlinchey said. “We’ve just got to focus on what we can control and go out and put our best foot forward this week.” Most importantly, Nix seems mentally and physically ready for this second go-round with the Chiefs. “We know it’s a big one. That goes without being said,” he said. “After falling to them already this year, this one is important to us. I expect a good game.” Broncos edge rusher Nik Bonitto says that defensive coordinator Vance Joseph still has a visceral reaction to the Week 1 game against Kansas City in which his defense missed 24 tackles. title: Ultimate Fan: Tackle, bring pressure, stop the run
summary: Woooooheeeee, ultimate fans! We almost didn’t have a UFG for Week 8, but huge thanks to DNVRNortwoods for coming through big at the last minute (even on Halloween!) And for Chiefs Week we absolutely had to have a UFG! After a big win over the Cardinals last week, today’s game to see who sits atop […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 14: Kenneth Walker III #9 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs the ball against the Denver Broncos during the first quarter in the game at Arrowhead Stadium on September 14, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Woooooheeeee, ultimate fans! We almost didn’t have a UFG for Week 8, but huge thanks to DNVRNortwoods for coming through big at the last minute (even on Halloween!) And for Chiefs Week we absolutely had to have a UFG! After a big win over the Cardinals last week, today’s game to see who sits atop the AFC West is huge. It’s less about the records and the ranks, though, and more about Denver’s continued progress toward a consistent offense and a dominating defense. Ironically, it’s the Broncos’ defense that has the most to prove after its embarrassing display versus the Chiefs in Week 1 in which it set a record for yards off missed tackles. But today’s game is at Mile High, which means Broncos Country better be ready because they are the difference today in what should be a tight game. But we’ll let our ultimate fan get into that! Let’s do this, Broncos! Divisional duel at our 🏠 pic.twitter.com/g9x4kzTbpa — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) November 1, 2026 Week 8: Broncos v. Chiefs MHR – Last week’s game was a fun win. Do you trust it? Were the Cardinals enough of a powerhouse to make you fully confident heading into this week’s rematch with the Chiefs? DNVRNortwoods: Of course I trust it! Bo has always been a slow start, add the injury plus what’s not talked about…being a new dad! Dude has been through a lot to start the season, tack on facing the No. 2, 3, 5, 7, 14, 17, and finally the easy (AZ Cardinals) 32nd ranked defenses. To come out of that with our record and what Bo was going through overall, we are alright. I’m not saying everything is perfect or that we’re going to destroy the Chiefs, I’m just saying we’re on the right track. I think Bo and this offense has finally found the balance the team needs to find success. MHR – The Chiefs are coming off a somewhat stunning loss to the Seahawks. Not so stunning that they lost but that they got killed – no touchdowns for Mahomes or Walker III and several turnovers. What do the Broncos need to take from the Seahawks’ win for their own approach on Sunday? DNVRNortwoods: Vance put it perfectly when he was HC…STOP THE RUN! And remember how to tackle! MHR – Prior to the Cardinals game, there was a lot of doubt about Bo Nix. How did his 62-yard run and 52-yard TD pass make you feel about his ability to compete and lead this team to wins? More importantly, how do you expect him to hold up against the Chiefs? DNVRNortwoods: First off… EFF ALL THE DOUBTERS!!! I’ve Bolieved from the start. On that note, EFF YOU Fitzpatrick, “YOU SUCK” – AqibTalib (I second!). Do I think Bo is going to be a top 5 QB next week? No. I do think he had a get (in the) right (direction) game. He seemed out of his head when it came to his injury and trying to be perfect. Maybe we can finally enjoy a game where Bo just plays ball and has some fun doing it. I fully expect Bo to have fun, sling the ball, have some fire, and put together a solid top 16 performance. MHR – It’s been somewhat of a rough go for the Broncos’ wideouts as tough defenses and a lot of receiving options have prevented Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton from being the superstars that wide receivers always like to be. Who has a big day on Sunday – Sutton? Waddle (if he plays)? Mims, perhaps? DNVRNortwoods: We have to ask ourselves what is a big day for these Denver Broncos? For me a big day across the NFL is ~7-10 catches for 125+ and 1 TD. I don’t think either has that kind of game, I do think we could see 75+ and a TD out of Waddle if he is a go. If he’s not Sutton will be force fed and have himself a MASSIVE game! 12 catches for 140+ and a TD (one can dream). MHR – As a follow-up, do the wide receivers need to have a big day, or do you expect the run game to be the more important offensive strategy? DNVRNortwoods: Balance is key here. Give me 150 rushing (50 from Bo) and 225 receiving, and we win the day. MHR – Speaking of the run game, the stable of healthy backs has been a carousel all season, and this week it looks like JK Dobbins and Jonah Coleman will be the two. Should Coleman be the primary RB? How should Davis Webb/Sean Payton use the two backs this week? DNVRNortwoods: Since we didn’t trade for JT in time to get him in this game we need to see what Coleman has. Feed him! But don’t forget JK. Let’s call it a 60-Coleman, 40- JK split. MHR – There are rumblings that Denver may be active at the trade deadline and running back seems like a good position to go after. What would you think of adding one of the following potential RBs – Jonathan Taylor, Saquon Barkley, Breece Hall or even Tony Pollard? Any favorites? DNVRNortwoods: JT or nothing! JT is a healthy superstar. If we’re going to trade, we can’t settle for anything less. If the price is too high (1st rounder plus), pound sand. But we are in a window, and in Paton I trust, so if he thinks any price is worth a superstar to win a title, SEND IT! And I love me a fellow Sconnie! MHR – OC Davis Webb said that Chiefs’ DC Dave Spagnolo is really good at scheming to take away their opponents’ best offensive weapon. Who is that for the Broncos? How would you try to work with that prediction if you were Denver’s OC this weekend? DNVRNortwoods: Bo is our best weapon, and he’s a weapon of mass destruction when he has his sparkle. And I think Bo found his sparkle. If I were Denver’s OC, I wouldn’t try to outsmart Spags. Stick to your game plan and trust your guys to perform. We need to get Bo going, quick and efficient passes, designed runs, and tell him to rip it when the time is right. If Bo gets in a rhythm in all facets of his game, Spags can’t stop him. #Bolieve. MHR – Moving on to defense…we all remember the debacle that was Denver’s defense in Week 1. It even set a record for most missed tackles in a game. Embarrassing! Does the Denver D show up big this weekend to erase that memory? Assuming so, how do they do that? DNVRNortwoods: Remember how to tackle, put Mahomes’s ass in the dirt, and STOP THE RUN! MHR – When playing Mahomes, it can be a tricky tradeoff on whether you rush the passer or maintain tight coverage. What do you think Vance Joseph’s approach should be to containing Mahomes without getting exposed elsewhere if Mahomes escapes? DNVRNortwoods: Vance will want gap integrity over all else. He’ll disguise a lot of our coverages. PLEASE use our mug looks to our advantage. MHR – The Seahawks held Kenneth Walker III to just 36 yards…far fewer than the 170+ the Broncos allowed 7 weeks ago. Assuming Denver won’t let that happen again, how do they keep Walker in check? DNVRNortwoods: Gap integrity and REMEMBER HOW TO TACKLE! MHR – Despite Travis Kelce being 100 years old, he leads Kansas City with 343 receiving yards. And Sean Payton praised his instincts and sudden breaks. Who covers him: linebackers, safeties, or everyone? How do the Broncos keep him from being a factor when covering TEs has often been Denver’s achilles heel? DNVRNortwoods: Let Jahdae have more snaps; he has been a sure tackler and solid in coverage over the past few weeks. Let him be the Kelce killer today. MHR – Alex Singleton leads the NFL with 87 tackles and was AFC Defensive Player of the Week this past week, and Nix said Singleton’s relentless effort models how the whole defense plays. How much of a factor will Singleton need to be on Sunday? DNVRNortwoods: hopefully none, I want to see our front four destroy K9 all day! Realistically Singleton is going to need to have another monster game! MHR – Kansas City destroyed the Broncos in Week 1, 31-10. Nix said you can’t play the same game twice – and thank goodness. What three main things have to look different from that night for Denver to win on Sunday? How much of a factor can the Mile High crowd be for the…

title: The Broncos don’t need much motivation for their showdown with the Chiefs
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! Some games don’t need a message. Today is one of those. The Denver Broncos host the Kansas City Chiefs today. It’s a divisional game. It’s a shot at a redo. The AFC West lead and playoff positioning are at stake. There isn’t much that Broncos head coach Sean Payton has to […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 25: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks on against the Arizona Cardinals during the first quarter at State Farm Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Some games don’t need a message. Today is one of those. The Denver Broncos host the Kansas City Chiefs today. It’s a divisional game. It’s a shot at a redo. The AFC West lead and playoff positioning are at stake. There isn’t much that Broncos head coach Sean Payton has to say. At the same time, while a Denver win today would be nice, it’s also not the end of the season if they lose. So for Payton, it’s a big game, but there will be bigger ones. “I think that’s right. I think everyone understands it’s a divisional game. Here it is on the schedule. We’ve done a good job just compartmentalizing. Way back when, you put the season into quarters. We don’t do that. I know who we play this week, next week. Then there’s a bye. Then after that … It’s a divisional game, and those are important. That’s what it is.” The other factor in the messaging is the fact that the Broncos got flogged by Kansas City in Week 1. “Yes, no question,” Payton said to the media earlier this week. “In other words, these guys are grown men. They recognize the things we didn’t do well, offensively, defensively.” Now it’s just a matter of correcting those issues and putting the team in a better position to have success. “I’ve watched it several times,” Broncos quarterback Bo Nix said to the media. “I watched it after immediately and then watched it again this week to prepare. It definitely doesn’t leave me excited with how that game ended. There are a lot of things we can focus on and correct. What I’ve learned over the past is you can’t play the same game twice. “That’s going to be a completely different game than what Sunday’s game is going to be, and you have to play it as such. You have to show up with a different mentality and just compete and just do what you can to have a different outcome than last time.” Broncos links

Per wire, Broncos signed safety Taylor Rapp from their practice squad to their 53-man roster. Roster spot opened up with Harvey going to IR. Broncos are also elevating G-C Gavin Ortega from practice squad for game tomorrow against the Chiefs. — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) October 31, 2026 Rapp, who was on the Broncos’ practice squad, reached his max of three practice squad elevations and needed to be added to the 53-man roster if they wanted him to play again this season. With Harvey on the short-term injured reserve and starting safety Talanoa Hufanga ruled out, Rapp is now on the 53-man roster and expected to start during Sunday’s game vs. the Chiefs. With Harvey being placed on the short-term injured reserve, joining reserve running back Tyler Badie, the Broncos are calling on practice squad running back Cody Schrader to be their RB3 on Sunday. The last time we saw Schrader, he carried the ball 13 times for 42 yards while having 6 receptions for 90 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ preseason finale. Now, the preseason star will get a chance in the regular season as the Broncos face the AFC West-leading Kansas City Chiefs. As for Gavin Ortega, the undrafted rookie will provide added depth at guard and center on Sunday. The good news here is that the Broncos did not elevate a wide receiver for Sunday’s game. As we know, Jaylen Waddle suffered a chest/shoulder injury late in the game vs. the Cardinals and was questionable for Sunday’s game. The fact that they did not elevate another receiver is a good sign that Waddle will be active and good to go in a big game where the Broncos could take control of the AFC West.

summary: The Broncos suffer a big blow to their offense. According to reports, the Denver Broncos have placed second-year running back RJ Harvey on short-term injured reserve, sidelining him for at least the next four games. Harvey suffered a knee injury during practice this week and will now be eligible to come off the injured reserve […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 25: RJ Harvey #12 of the Denver Broncos runs during the first quarter of the game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. The Broncos defeated the Cardinals 30-16. (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Broncos suffer a big blow to their offense. According to reports, the Denver Broncos have placed second-year running back RJ Harvey on short-term injured reserve, sidelining him for at least the next four games. Harvey suffered a knee injury during practice this week and will now be eligible to come off the injured reserve for the Broncos’ home game vs. the Miami Dolphins on December 6th. To replace his spot on the Broncos’ 53-man roster, the team is reportedly signing veteran safety Taylor Rapp to the active roster, and he will start in place of the injured Talanoa Hufanga. The #Broncos are placing emerging RB R.J. Harvey on short-term IR as he recovers from the knee injury he suffered in practice this week, source says. Harvey will miss the next four games and is eligible to return as soon as the #Broncos game vs the #Dolphins on Dec. 6. pic.twitter.com/wBTJw6KHv4 — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 31, 2026 Harvey, who had a 50+ yard touchdown this past Sunday vs. the Arizona Cardinals on a screen play, has been the Broncos’ most consistent offensive playmaker. Now, the Broncos will be down another running back as they head into the second half of their schedule. Rookie Jonah Coleman is expected to be the Broncos’ lead back this Sunday, with veteran JK Dobbins serving as the backup, and Cody Schrader being elevated from the practice squad to be the Broncos RB3. With Harvey and Tyler Badie on the short-term IR and JK Dobbins struggling, the Broncos could pursue another back on the trade market. As we talked about this morning, the Colts made star running back Jonathan Taylor available on the trade market, and the Broncos were among the teams listed as intereste d. Could the Harvey injury make them go all-in and acquire Taylor? Other backs like Saquon Barkley, Tony Pollard, and maybe even Breece Hall are rumored to be backs on the trade block as we come closer to the NFL trade deadline, so we will have to see if the Broncos make a move. Right now, they have a currently unproven and inexperienced (Just 19 carries on the season) rookie back in Jonah Coleman and a struggling veteran JK Dobbins, as their rushers. They are just one injury away from Cody Schrader, a practice squad player, seeing significant snaps on offense. I believe they need to add some more depth to their running back room moving forward as we head into the colder months of the season. At the end of the day, this is a major blow to the Broncos’ offense. Harvey has been one of their more consistent and explosive playmakers this season, and now he will be sidelined for at least the next 5 weeks (4 games + bye week). We will have to see if this injury forces the Broncos into making a move for another running back in the coming days.

title: Colts are now open to trading RB Jonathan Taylor, and the Broncos are among the teams interested
summary: According to NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport, the Indianapolis Colts are now open to trading star running back Jonathan Taylor ahead of the upcoming trade deadline. In the report, both insiders list the Broncos among the teams that have shown some level of interest in trading for the star running back. The Colts […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts looks on prior to the start of the game against the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport, the Indianapolis Colts are now open to trading star running back Jonathan Taylor ahead of the upcoming trade deadline. In the report, both insiders list the Broncos among the teams that have shown some level of interest in trading for the star running back. The Colts have already traded Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the 49ers, and they do not appear done having a fire sale. The #Colts are now open to trading star RB Jonathan Taylor… and those talks are ongoing and active. Story from me and @AdamSchefter : https://t.co/9CovxSRESa https://t.co/9CovxSRESa — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 31, 2026 Schefter and Rapoport name the Packers, Vikings, Giants, and Seahawks, along with the Broncos , as teams that have shown at least some level of interest in trading for Taylor. The list of teams that have expressed at least some level of interest in trading for Taylor is thought to include the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings, New York Giants and Seattle Seahawks, sources said. As of now, the Vikings seem like the reported frontrunner for Taylor, but as we know, things can change, and circumstances can change a team’s level of desperation to acquire a player. For the Broncos, their run game has struggled to start the season. Veteran JK Dobbins, whom the Broncos re-signed this offseason and hoped would look like the back they saw last season, has struggled to start the year. He has recently unfollowed the Broncos on social media (if you care about that) and has gotten into a back-and-forth with 9NEWS Broncos insider Mike Klis. Also, second-year running back RJ Harvey suffered a knee injury during practice this week, which isn’t considered serious per reports , but he will sit out Sunday’s big game vs. the Chiefs. Last week, the rookie running back was activated off the injured reserve and instantly took over the Broncos backfield. He led the Broncos’ backs in snaps, touches, and yards and now will get the start vs. the Chiefs on Sunday. If Coleman were to have a big game against the Broncos’ divisional rivals, it would pour some cold water on these trade talks, but any struggles or injuries could intensify these talks. Right now, the return for Taylor appears to be a 2nd-round pick + more, according to reports. This report also seems to indicate that the Colts, who have been listening to offers for Taylor, have not been satisfied with the offers and are telling teams they need to send in their best offers now. Personally, if acquiring Taylor only costs a 2nd-round pick + more, I believe the Broncos should make that deal. A 1-2 punch of Taylor and Coleman instantly gives the Broncos one of the better running back pairings in the NFL and would instantly reshape their offense. This would take a lot of pressure off quarterback Bo Nix, make teams have to defend the run game, and open up the pass game and play-action game for Nix. Plus, if you want to win in the postseason, you need to run the ball. I believe giving up the draft capital, especially if it does not cost a first-round pick, is worth it for a team that is in a Super Bowl window right now. Even if they do not acquire Taylor, I still believe they need to upgrade their running back room. Coleman is a mostly inexperienced and unproven rookie at this point, Dobbins is struggling, and Harvey has continued to struggle as a runner (excellent as a pass catcher, though). We have already seen multiple big blockbuster trades go down, and we still have a few weeks to go until the trade deadline. I would be shocked if the Broncos do not make a move during this period, but we will have to wait and see. Stay tuned to Mile High Report for all your news and updates surrounding the Denver Broncos.

title: Broncos vs. Chiefs: 3 Players to Watch in Week 8
summary: The Denver Broncos host the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday. It’s a shot for Denver to earn their fourth straight victory. Even better, the Broncos can be the top team in the AFC West by beating the Chiefs. In order to make that happen, these three players will have to perform at a high level. […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 11: Alex Singleton #49 of the Denver Broncos reacts after a fumble recovery during the fourth quarter of the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos host the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday. It’s a shot for Denver to earn their fourth straight victory. Even better, the Broncos can be the top team in the AFC West by beating the Chiefs. In order to make that happen, these three players will have to perform at a high level. Bo Nix — Quarterback One good performance can be a catalyst and confidence boost for players hoping to get things going in the right direction. It wasn’t perfect by any means, but quarterback Bo Nix’s outing versus the Arizona Cardinals had quite a few bright spots. It also answered a few lingering questions Broncos Country and many analysts. The concerns on Nix’s ability to run should be put to bed after his transcendent 62-yard touchdown gallop. What I liked even more was his aggressiveness and willingness to throw the ball down the field. Nix was able to make some tight down the field throws against Cover 2 shells and delivered a handful of impressive throws on middle of the field concepts. Those splash plays were hard to come by in prior games. Steve Spagnuolo’s defense has been one of the best in the NFL to start the season. Even though their top two corners from last season are playing elsewhere, their passing defense has still been stellar. They’ve done a good job limiting explosive plays and keeping most top targets from doing much damage through the air. Nix and the Broncos’ aerial attack had just 115 passing yards in Week 1. That won’t be good enough to earn a victory on Sunday, so improvement will be necessary. Keep in mind, the Chiefs have forced ten turnovers in six games, with two in four contests—including two against the Broncos on Monday Night Football . Nix will need to find a way to be effective and not turn the ball over. Alex Singleton — Linebacker Alex Singleton’s Week 1 outing against the Chiefs was a big disappointment. Though it’s safe to say Singleton has really turned things around since then. In fact, this last three game stretch might be the best Broncos Country has seen from Singleton donning orange and blue. Against the Cardinals, Singleton was a heat-seeking missile. He notched an incredible 19 tackles and came away with several quarterback pressures and a key sack. That earned him AFC Defensive Player of the Week honors. Running back Kenneth Walker has been an explosive playmaker for the Chiefs. He is the engine that makes their offense go and certainly one of the NFL’s premier offensive weapons. Everyone knows limiting his impact is a big key to the game. Walker was absolutely dominant in Kansas City’s Week 1 pummeling of the Broncos. However, the Seattle Seahawks found a way to shut last year’s Super Bowl MVP in their Week 7 win over the Chiefs. He can be stopped. This time around, I’m optimistic Singleton and the Broncos’ defense will execute far better this time around and slow down Kansas City’s rushing attack. Jonah Coleman — Running Back As the Broncos gear up for the second half stretch of the season, establishing a formidable rushing attack will be critical. Last week against the Cardinals, the Broncos put together their best run game performance of the season. Rookie running back Jonah Coleman was a big part of that and was productive with his touches. After the game, Head Coach Sean Payton vowed to get Coleman more touches moving forward. That seems like a good bet with RJ Harvey’s status versus the Chiefs in doubt . I expect this to be a tough and gritty matchup with both teams trying to dictate the pace of the game on the ground. Denver’s offense has struggled to convert third downs all season long. There is no simple fix to that issue. However, I believe getting quality yards on early downs would certainly help. They have been in far too many third-and-long situations. Head Coach Sean Payton has been insistent trying to rectify the Broncos’ first down passing woes since he took over playcalling duties. This Sunday, I’d like to see a little more emphasis running consistently on first down—especially early on in games. Coleman has performed well that regard in limited playing time. He is averaging 4.7 yards per carry on first downs. He’s also more effective than J.K. Dobbins on second down rushes. I’d like to see Denver showcase the rookie running back against the Chiefs. It’s a big opportunity for him to show he should be leading the Broncos’ rushing group moving forward.

title: Best player prop bets for Minnesota Vikings vs. Detroit Lions, Week 8
summary: After a Week 7 victory in their first NFC North game of the season, the Detroit Lions host another divisional battle in Week 8. full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 25: Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions takes the field prior to a game against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field on October 25, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a Week 7 victory in their first NFC North game of the season, the Detroit Lions host another divisional battle in Week 8. This time, the Lions host the top team in the NFC North, the undefeated Minnesota Vikings. Detroit is on a two-game winning streak, something they haven’t had since early Week 5 in 2025. In my predictions last week , I went 1-2 in the top three bets, as the game was lower-scoring than expected, and tight end Sam LaPorta had a quiet performance on National Tight Ends Day. Quarterback Jared Goff did his job and got us back to .500. With us back at even, it’s time to get back on the winning side on Sunday. The odds are with FanDuel Sportsbook . 1. Kyler Murray under 224.5 passing yards (-113) Yes, I am trusting the Lions secondary here to slow down a quarterback. Safety Brian Branch is back at a full go after limited snaps last week, and it’s less about Detroit’s side and more about Minnesota’s struggles. Quarterback Kyler Murray hasn’t been the savior people expected at the position in this offense. He hasn’t had a good season so far, and this offense has been struggling mightily with him under center. Murray is averaging 162.4 yards per game this season, with his best performance being against the Miami Dolphins, where he threw for 247 yards. In two of his five games this season, Murray has surpassed that mark, though he left Week 1 early with an injury. In the first month of play, Detroit’s secondary averaged 304 passing yards per game. In their last two games, it was 267.5, and while that isn’t a big improvement, it’s a step in the right direction. Against a passing attack averaging 100 yards less than that, I think the Lions’ defense can meet it halfway and hold Murray to under 225 yards. Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $18.85 2. Amon-Ra St. Brown alt receiving yards: 90+ (+142) In his NFL career, St. Brown has 896 receiving yards against the Vikings over 10 games, averaging 89.6 yards per game. St. Brown is averaging 87.5 yards a game this season, so him hitting 90+ yards seems doable. Lions quarterback Jared Goff has been playing lights out, and his connection with St. Brown is still strong. St. Brown is coming off his best game of the season too, with 153 yards against the Green Bay Packers. Sure, the Vikings defense is the toughest Detroit has played this season, but their coverage hasn’t been excellent, ranked 15th in coverage according to PFF. In their last three games, they’ve held opposing passing attacks to under 100 yards, but the offenses aren’t as explosive as the Lions. When they’ve played an offense with a tough passing attack, the Packers threw for 353 yards. Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $24.40 3. Jared Goff alt passing yards: 250+ (-146) As I stated in my last point, Goff is playing at an MVP level and was in his bag against the Packers. Minnesota will test Goff and the offensive line heavily with their high-blitzing defense, but Goff shouldn’t be afraid. He’s been the best quarterback in the NFL against the blitz, so Minnesota might want to ease up on that pressure. Jared Goff is now the best QB against the blitz by EPA per dropback https://t.co/GiDGct8dek pic.twitter.com/EfAqv4i4RV — SūmerSports (@SumerSports) October 27, 2026 Goff is averaging 298 yards per game, so getting 250 yards should be simple for him. If this game is low-scoring, it could come down to field goals. Goff can still hit the number if Detroit moves down the field but doesn’t find the end zone. The only threat to this bet is if Detroit gets up too much, and with Minnesota’s offense struggling, it might lean on the running game, which limits what Goff can do. Gibbs doesn’t like getting held out of the end zone, since he hasn’t had back-to-back games without touchdowns since 2023. I think Gibbs will want to not just score, but do better than he did last time he played the Vikings. Wide receiver Isaac TeSlaa is averaging 32.8 yards per game, so asking him for 19 yards isn’t a lot. The last time he played the Vikings, he had three catches for 49 yards and a touchdown.
