(Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Dear Minnesota Vikings, As you may be aware, you are the most disrespected 6-0 NFL team that I have seen in my lifetime. Despite the fact that you are 2-0 in divisional games and have a defense that is allowing the league’s fewest points per game at 12.3, people are still calling you frauds. Those voices have only grown louder over the past few weeks, and now there are comparisons between your starting quarterback and the one you let go to New York. The promises of Kevin O’Connell in locker room speeches saying that this offense is going to improve reverberate off of a concrete wall into thin air. Yes, Kyler Murray is protecting the football and not committing costly turnovers. He has also been inconsistent at times and has missed quite a few throws due to poor timing or inaccuracy. We thought this year was going to be different. Heck, Max Brosmer was 1-1 last year in games where he produced almost zero (if not negative) offensive value. Meanwhile, this season’s offense has to scratch and claw for 60 minutes just to score ONE TOUCHDOWN! We are witnessing the same problems with stagnancy (which seems to be a prevalent theme in your offensive scheme, Kevin) every time we have possession of the football. Every drive feels like ten steps forward with two steps back, culminating in a 50-yard Will Reichard field goal. I don’t even want to watch when you have the ball in between the 40s, because I know you aren’t going to get anywhere near the endzone. For example, this past week, Myles Price set you up with immaculate field position, and what did you do with it? You ran the ball four times and failed to convert on fourth down, turning the ball over on downs. RIDICULOUS. The lack of production on offense is why everybody and their mamas with a microphone and a camera are posting their very loud opinions on the internet. This week you play a divisional rival in the Detroit Lions. This is a chance to prove that your team is elite in all three phases and a true Super Bowl contender. You cannot rely on the defense to hold teams to fewer than 13 points every game. The silver lining is that I believe this defense CAN hold ANY team to 13 points or fewer, but still, you cannot rely on their dominance every week. The tension in my soul wants the confirmation that this offense can score 30+ points when called upon. Nothing would make me happier than for you to shut up all of these armchair analyst CLOWNS who think they know everything about football even though they probably haven’t watched one snap of a Minnesota Vikings game. However, at the end of the day, I am a Minnesota Vikings fan. I know this is a franchise built upon the foundation of excellence on defense. I am also starting to understand why all of these talking heads are so low on you, the Minnesota Vikings. It’s because when they watch you play, they’re bored. They don’t care about history; they just want to be entertained. Nothing is less entertaining to faux media jabronis than elite defense and low-scoring games. Maybe it is a personal problem that has compelled me to write this letter. Why do I expose myself to these opinions on social media and the internet? Part of it is so I can write informed pieces about the narratives surrounding this Vikings team. The other reason is that it fuels my passion. I see the potential, and I know that if this offense can start executing, this is going to be an incredibly scary team. Please, just shut the critics up. Please, please, PLEASE! I now want to speak directly to you, Kevin. You need to get it together. I believe in your ability as a head coach in the NFL; I really do! You have cultivated a winning culture with this franchise, and the results have shown in the regular season. As I am sure you are aware, you have failed to lead this team to a single playoff victory in your tenure at the helm. Your system failed a young quarterback before he failed you (in some eyes), and as a coach brought in for your offensive prowess, you have not delivered on the expectation of efficient and effective offenses. So, what is the deal? Are you calling the right plays and your players just aren’t delivering the results? Are you lacking more explosive playmakers? Are you making the wrong decisions in certain situations, leading to uninspiring results? Do you need to focus more on managing the game and let someone else call the plays? What is it? All I’m going to say is, whatever the issue(s), please fix it. Figure it out so we can all stop asking these questions. To the offense: you need to be better. I’m looking directly at you, Will Fries. You’ve done a nice job cleaning up some of the penalties we were seeing in the first few weeks of the season, but that’s not enough. You need to start scoring some touchdowns. Just know, the whole world is laughing at you and sees you as the downfall of an otherwise dominant team. You frequently start with great field position only to squander it. You have possessed the ball more than any other offense in the NFL, yet you’re in the bottom 5 of points scored (probably lower if you’re only counting touchdowns). Things just aren’t adding up, and you better start materializing the vision of your head coach. You very well know the strength of your team is the defense. Blake, Eric, Jalen, Caleb, Dominique, Dallas, Andrew, Josh, Byron, Isaiah, and Harrison, I see the work you are putting in. Your excellence is not going unnoticed. You are part of an excellent and potentially historic defensive unit. You wreak so much havoc and create so much chaos that opposing offenses don’t know what to do to attack you. Sure, you’ve given up a few big plays this year and some touchdowns. However, you make the adjustments to thwart any offensive game plan. We saw it against Green Bay, New Orleans, and Indianapolis. You let Green Bay score 22 first-half points and then shut them out in the second half. You let New Orleans march down the field on a long drive and score a touchdown in the first quarter, only to hold them to 6 points for the rest of the game. You allowed Jonathan Taylor to break a long touchdown run, only to turn Danny Dimes into Danny Schillings and dominate the rest of the way. You are not the problem here, and I pray you continue to do what you do. Take care of your bodies and stay healthy, because we need you. I will leave you with these parting words. I believe in the 2026 Minnesota Vikings. I have high hopes and expectations for this team. You will be playing meaningful football in January and possibly February. You have the leadership, drive, and determination to bring Minnesota its first Lombardi trophy. You just have to not get in your own way. Believe in yourselves, believe in each other, believe in the Minnesota Vikings’ culture. You have thousands of fans rooting for you, and we will be here with you until the possibly bitter, but hopefully glorious, end. You have my support and the support of many others. I speak for many when I say I love this team and only want the best for you. Until Next Skol.

full_text: CHICAGO, IL - OCTOBER 22: Gabe Jacas #50 of the New England Patriots looks on from the field during an NFL football game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots rookie class has played a significant role through the team’s first seven weeks. First-round pick Caleb Lomu has seen extensive action in multiple games filling in for the injured Will Campbell and Morgan Moses. Second- and third-round selections Gabe Jacas and Eli Raridon have proved to be consistent contributors on their respective sides of the ball. The Patriots then also rank near the top of the league in rookie snaps on special teams. According to Patriots fans, however, Jacas has been the best of the group. In the latest SB Nation Reacts survey, 63% of participants said they have been most impressed with the rookie pass rusher. Much of the comment section highlighted the team’s first three selections: Coldhands Luke Lomu has looked better than Will Campbell or Morgan Moses. Him, for sure. Koda Tough choice between Raridon, Jakas and Lomu. All 3 have played great HaffaMeatball Lowkey Lomu because when you draft a lineman 1st round it’s because you need him to start asap. And he played like a starter. luckyfukikentucky Jacas by a hair. Followed closely by Raridon. Then Lomu who has shown a lot when he has filled in at both LT plus RT and some jumbo TE snaps. Another really solid draft. PatsGoingGoing I’d say Jacas, then Raridon, but it sounds like Lomu is coming on strong–and he’d be the most valuable if his recent performance holds. All in all, this week’s survey results look as follows: Through seven games, Jacas has played 57% of the team’s defensive snaps and is second on the team with 21 pressures — which is tied for 20th in the league among all edge defenders. Behind Jacas, 25% of voters went with tight end Eli Raridon. Serving as the No. 2 option behind Hunter Henry, the rookie has hauled in 12 receptions for 168 yards and a pair of touchdowns as he has flashed serious receiving upside. First-round pick Caleb Lomu then received 10% of the votes. Lomu has taken on a role as the jumbo tight end and also serving as the team’s No. 3 tackle. That has led to him playing extensive snaps in Week 5 and 6 as an injury replacement, where he surrendered just one total pressure. The voting was rounded out with Namdi Obiazor, as the sixth-round pick has taken a key special teams role. The group’s performance is part of the reason why the fanbase remains confident in the team, as 84% of voters believe the Patriots are trending in the right direction even after a loss. The Patriots will continue to count on their rookie class as the season progresses, where they hope the group will help them achieve their ultimate goal of winning the Super Bowl. They currently hold the 13th best odds on FanDuel Sportsbook to hoist the Lombardi Trophy, seventh best in the AFC.

title: What signing Lan Larison to the 53-man roster means for the Patriots
summary: The New England Patriots have finally filled the open spot on their 53-man roster. Second-year running back Lan Larison, who started the season on the practice squad, was promoted to the active team ahead of its upcoming game against the Miami Dolphins. Let’s assess what the move means for the Patriots. Improved running back depth […]
full_text: The New England Patriots have finally filled the open spot on their 53-man roster. Second-year running back Lan Larison, who started the season on the practice squad, was promoted to the active team ahead of its upcoming game against the Miami Dolphins. Let’s assess what the move means for the Patriots. Improved running back depth The Patriots entered the weekend with three running backs on their active roster, but one of them as a question mark to actually suit up versus the Dolphins. It turns out, TreVeyon Henderson will indeed not participate in the game due to the illness that kept him out of practice on Thursday and Friday. Instead of using a practice squad elevation on Larison to bolster the depth, the Patriots have added him to their 53-man team. The full position depth chart now looks like this: 53-man roster (4): Rhamondre Stevenson (38), TreVeyon Henderson (32), Corey Kiner (9), Lan Larison (34) Injured reserve (1): RB Myles Montgomery (39 | season-ending) What’s the benefit of brining Larison up instead of just elevating him? On the surface, there appears to be none. That said, besides the financial element we will get to in a second, the Patriots also add to their RB depth in a more sustainable manner: Larison was already standard-elevated for game day once, which in turn means he had only two such elevations left — a number that was effectively guaranteed to drop to one this weekend. Now on the 53-man team, those calculations no longer are a factor. Kickoff return considerations Entering Week 8, the Patriots are ranked 25th in the NFL in average kickoff return yards (24.9) and 27th in starting field position (28.5). There have been positive moments, but their kickoff return game has been relatively lackluster once again this year. Is Larison going to change this dramatically? He averaged 24.5 yards on his two runbacks earlier this year, which ranks above Kyle Williams’ 24.0 but below Corey Kiner’s 26.7. From that perspective, no massive spike should be expected. Still, his presence as an experienced runback option — he was a regular in that role throughout training camp — gives the Patriots some more flexibility. Not only could they decide to mix things up if performance calls for it, Larison also might help prevent exposing Kiner and Williams to extra contact. The team is getting quite thin at both running back and wide receiver and might need both of them on offense. Trade questions The NFL trade deadline is coming up on Nov. 10, and so far only one Patriots player — defensive tackle Christian Barmore — has been mentioned as a possible trade candidate . Should TreVeyon Henderson also be added to that list now that New England has signed another running back to the 53-man roster? There are potential arguments for him being available, including his rather uninspiring output so far in his sophomore campaign. If Henderson is not showing significant growth in some crucial areas, it might make sense to cut ties early rather than late as to not risk any further damage to his value. However, any such thoughts are purely speculative. Based on what we know, the Patriots are still high on Henderson and his potential within their offense. “TreVeyon will help us plenty here down the stretch,” said head coach Mike Vrabel last week. There is no indication this wasn’t a sincere statement. Cap impact Active roster or practice squad, NFL players are all compensated through a weekly salary whose height depends on their actual contract language. In Larison’s case, his most recent pact with the Patriots paid him $13,750 a week while on the developmental roster. Now on the 53-man team, he is getting a significant raise: his weekly salary now stands at $49,166.67. Calculated over the remainder of the regular season, this means his cap number jumps from $151,250 to $540,833.

title: Patriots add running back Lan Larison to 53, elevate former Dolphins wideout from practice squad
summary: After downgrading running back TreVeyon Henderson and wide receiver A.J. Brown to out, the New England Patriots traveled to Hard Rock Stadium with insurance at both positions. The organization promoted running back Lan Larison to the 53-man roster and elevated wide receiver Ryan Miller from the practice squad for Sunday’s game against the Miami Dolphins. […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WA - SEPTEMBER 09: Lan Larison #34 of the New England Patriots looks on from the sideline during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on September 9, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images After downgrading running back TreVeyon Henderson and wide receiver A.J. Brown to out, the New England Patriots traveled to Hard Rock Stadium with insurance at both positions. The organization promoted running back Lan Larison to the 53-man roster and elevated wide receiver Ryan Miller from the practice squad for Sunday’s game against the Miami Dolphins. Larison, 24, will serve as the third option in the running back room behind Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner after an illness thinned the depth chart. The 5-foot-11, 209-pound change of pace reverted to the practice squad in September after making his NFL debut versus the Seattle Seahawks. He caught two passes for nine yards and averaged 24.5 yards per kickoff return in the Super Bowl LX rematch, handling three snaps on offense and six snaps on special teams. Arriving in Foxborough as an undrafted free agent in 2025, Larison spent his rookie campaign on injured reserve following a foot injury. The UC Davis product cleared waivers at the 53-man deadline in August and was retained on the 17-man scout team at its formation. Two months later, he takes the open spot on the active roster. Miller, 26, signed to the Patriots’ practice squad midway through October after Romeo Doubs joined fellow veteran target Mack Hollins on injured reserve. The 6-foot-2, 217-pound standard call-up will head back to his former stomping grounds as the fourth healthy wide receiver behind DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams. Currently ranking fifth on the Dolphins in receiving yards, Miller reeled in a season-long, 77-yard touchdown from quarterback Malik Willis before making his way to Gillette Stadium. Originally entering the NFL as an undrafted rookie in 2023, the Furman alum spent three years with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers before being claimed off waivers by the New York Giants and then by Miami during training camp. He has appeared in 30 NFL games, including six starts, while totaling 17 receptions for 254 yards and four touchdowns. Linebacker Christian Elliss and cornerback Carlton Davis III move forward with questionable game statuses for the Patriots following the downgrades, while offensive tackle Marcus Bryant will remain on injured reserve for the divisional matchup. Sunday’s kickoff in Miami Gardens is set for 4:25 p.m. ET.

Brown, TreVeyon Henderson & Marcus Bryant to out for NE vs. MIA. pic.twitter.com/SfBea3LiQ3 — New England Patriots (@Patriots) October 31, 2026 Brown, 29, missed back-to-back practices to end AFC East prep after beginning the week as a limited participant. In his absence, the running back room features starter Rhamondre Stevenson and August pickup Corey Kiner on the active roster as well as Lan Larison on the practice squad. Bryant, 24, will remain on New England’s injured reserve for Sunday after having his 21-day practice window open midway through October. Due to a preseason ankle injury, the sophomore swing tackle had been designated to return at the league’s cutdown deadline in August. He recently upgraded from limited to full participation and did not carry a game designation. The No. 220 overall pick from last year’s draft class appeared in 12 games as a Patriots rookie, seeing 19 snaps on offense and 56 snaps on special teams. The downgrades leave linebacker Christian Elliss and cornerback Carlton Davis III as the lone questionable game statuses from the final injury report of the week. Sunday’s kickoff in Miami Gardens is set for 4:25 p.m. ET.

title: The importance of change during the Saints’ bye week
summary: This bye week for the New Orleans Saints is the most important one in the current era of the franchise. At a time when this team entered the season with so much hope and promise, built on how last season ended, the trust of the fan base is beginning to wane. The team showed flashes […]
full_text: PARIS, FRANCE - OCTOBER 25: Tyler Shough #6 of the New Orleans Saints fumbles the ball during the second quarter of the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Stade de France on October 25, 2026 in Paris, France. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images This bye week for the New Orleans Saints is the most important one in the current era of the franchise. At a time when this team entered the season with so much hope and promise, built on how last season ended, the trust of the fan base is beginning to wane. The team showed flashes of a promising future: a young head coach with previous success as an offensive coordinator, a rookie quarterback who appeared to be a budding superstar, two solid young offensive tackles who looked to be the bookends of what should have been a competent offensive line, and a front office that finally seemed to be turning the page and getting its act together. After the first half of the season, all of that appears to have been misjudged. Now, this team sits with only two wins, the offense that seems lost, and two recent draft classes that are beginning to look like major whiffs. The head coach can’t seem to put together an offensive game plan that allows the team to start games effectively and sustain success for an entire contest. So, this bye week means a lot. As things currently stand, the Saints are still on the cusp of competing for a very weak division. However, if they come out of this bye week with the same offensive issues, an inability to run the football, a team that has managed to score no more than six total first-quarter points all season, and consistent problems with blocking up front, then the statement made by the owner two weeks ago, which still looms over this team like a cloud, will only ring hollow in the ears of the Who Dat Nation faithful. If the Saints come out of this bye week without making changes to the coaching staff, they will absolutely have to demonstrate meaningful changes on the field. And if they don’t, trust will be broken, and apathy will begin to set in. The last thing any professional sports franchise should want is for its fan base to become apathetic toward the team. At least frustration stems from passion, and that passion can drive change and progress. Apathy, on the other hand, only leads to the team being ignored and fans finding better ways to spend their time and, most importantly, their money. This upcoming week will be incredibly important, and the results of the work, sacrifice, and development of this roster and coaching staff will be evident from the opening moments of the next game. Hope is gone. Faith is low. Trust is slipping away. The Saints must approach this bye week with a sense of urgency and make the necessary changes to restore confidence in this team and organization.

title: ‘Kudos and Wet Willies’, plus bye week thoughts on every Giants specialist
summary: To complete our bye week look at the New York Giants roster, let’s hand out Kudos and Wet Willies, and offer some thoughts on the team’s specialists. LS Ben Mann — His next poor snap will be his first one. Grade: Kudos P Jordan Stout — Stout is amazing. He leads the league with an […]
full_text: Dominic Zvada (34) and Jordan Sout | Getty Images To complete our bye week look at the New York Giants roster, let’s hand out Kudos and Wet Willies, and offer some thoughts on the team’s specialists. LS Ben Mann — His next poor snap will be his first one. Grade: Kudos P Jordan Stout — Stout is amazing. He leads the league with an average of 51.6 yards per punt, has punts of 78 and 74 yards, and a pair of 66-yarders, and has continually flipped the fields. Grade: Kudos PK Dominic Zvada — Zvada got off to a 9 of 9 start, but has gone just 4 of 9 since. He has also had a couple of issues not placing the ball where it was supposed to go on kickoffs. Grade: Kwillie … Zvada has a ton of talent. Can the Giants continue to wait for the consistency? Punt/kickoff returner Charlie Jones — Jones had a crushing fumble against the New Orleans Saints. He is averaging a career-best 11.1 yards returning punts, though, and had a couple of long returns vs. the Saints negated by penalties. At 23.8 yards per kickoff return and with the fumble against the Saints, he is still looking to find his footing there. Grade: Kwillie Kickoff returner Tyrone Tracy — Being used as a full-time kickoff returner for the first time, Tracy is averaging 28.9 yards on nine returns, ninth in the league. He will miss at least the next four games. Grade: Kudos Punt/kickoff returner Braxton Berrios — His season ended after four games. Grade: Incomplete

title: Survey results: Giants fans want DL help on the trade market
summary: The New York Giants are on a much-needed bye this week, but that isn’t stopping the flow of news. The 2026 trade deadline is approaching quickly and the Giants remain in the conversation despite not playing this week. The 4-2-1 Giants are in control of the NFC East and while they might not be surprised […]
full_text: Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor carries the ball | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Giants are on a much-needed bye this week, but that isn’t stopping the flow of news. The 2026 trade deadline is approaching quickly and the Giants remain in the conversation despite not playing this week. The 4-2-1 Giants are in control of the NFC East and while they might not be surprised by their success, the rest of the NFL media landscape is coming around to the fact that the Giants are a real factor in the post-season conversation. We’ve already had reporting that the Giants are approaching the trade deadline with an aggressive mentality to seize their opportunity to separate themselves as an NFC contender. In fact, the Giants are considered the 9th most likely team to make the playoffs at +130 ( per Fanduel ). They still trail the Dallas Cowboys (+108), but have closed the gap in perception. It’s a remarkable rise from being seen as the second-least likely NFC team to make the playoffs when the season started. John Harbaugh and Joe Schoen each tried to convince the Tennessee Titans to trade All Pro DL Jeffery Simmons, but were ultimately rebuffed. The Giants are also believed to be one of the teams pursuing star running back Jonathan Taylor. This week we asked which position Giants fans would like their team to pursue on the trade market. And while they likely would have approved of a trade for Simmons (if not the price), few fans want the team to go after a running back. Almost as many fans want the team to trade for a defensive tackle as the next three options put together. D.J. Reader has been fantastic for the Giants, returning to form in Dennard Wilson’s defense and has quietly been excellent this year. Shelby Harris has been a solid player next to Reader, and we’ve seen flashes incremental improvement from Darius Alexander as well as flashes from Bobby Jamison-Travis and C.J. Okoye. However, the defensive line could still benefit from more depth and talent. The top options of Simmons and DeForest Buckner are off the board. And while it’s possible that the Giants could pry a surprising player loose somewhere, someone like Colts’ nose tackle Grover Stewart stands out as a potential low-cost addition to the defensive line. It isn’t much of a surprise that almost a quarter of fans would rather the team hold their water than make a move. The Giants were burned badly when they attempted to short-circuit their rebuild process following the unexpected success of the 2022 season. Coaching decisions aside, it’s took a couple years to get back on track for a team that mistakenly believed that it was in “win now” mode. Of course, it’s also been widely reported that Harbaugh has believed since the very beginning that the Giants were better than their 2025 record said they were. One of the reasons why he chose the Giants over the Titans or Dolphins is that he believed they have a roster in place to be competitive in 2026. My personal take is that the 2027 NFL Draft promises to be a deep and talented one at several positions of need for the Giants. I’m in favor of using the trade market to add talent if the opportunity cost is in the Giants’ favor and it doesn’t hamper their ability to build the roster for the future. To me, that means using late picks that are unlikely to ever have much impact, or more premium picks if the return is a player who is young enough to be a multi-year contributor and likely to be more impactful than a player than a drafted player. Fewer than 1 in 10 fans, however, want the team to trade for a running back. That runs at odds with John Harbaugh’s desire to add a star “bellcow” to his backfield. Sinking significant resources into the running back position has been a chancy proposition historically. Highly drafted running backs seldom prove “worth it” to the teams that draft them, and high-cost free agents typically only succeed within the structure of a team that’s ready to maximize their potential. We’ve had solid performances from the Giants’ backfield this year, notably against the Dallas Cowboys, Tennessee Titans, and Houston Texans. And considering the trio of Cam Skattebo, Devin Singletary, and Tyrone Tracy (IR) are capable of being a solid grinding unit, the argument is that the Giants don’t need a Ferrari to go get the groceries. The counter to that is that John Harbaugh wants one. It’s also possible that a back who is better able to maximize runs, create on the margins, and turn good runs into explosive runs will have a greater than expected impact on the offense. The hope is that acquiring Taylor (or a player like him) would have a similar impact on the Giants’ offense as Christian McCaffrey and Kenneth Walker III have had on the San Francisco 49ers and Kansas City Chiefs (respectively). On the flip side, it’s surprising to me (personally) that very few fans are interested in acquiring a wide receiver. There’s a tendency among Giants fans to regard receivers as luxury pieces and generally prefer the team to not invest premium resources in the position. So in that regard, I’m not surprised they aren’t in favor of trading for a receiver. However, the Giants’ non-existent depth at the position is a real concern, and the prospect of a “Malachi Fields, Darnell Mooney, Jalin Hyatt” receiving corps isn’t exactly thrilling. There’s also the fact that while the Giants don’t faced stacked boxes all that often (20.4 percent of runs, 21st in the NFL per NextGenStats), they also don’t face light boxes that often. The Giants have only run against a light box on 30.3 percent of the time, which is 25th in the NFL. My position is that not only would adding a primary receiving weapon help insulate the team against a potentially devasting injury, it would do more to enable the Giants to force opposing defenses into more favorable rushing match-ups. But regardless of what the Giants do at the trade deadline, fans are confident. Giants’ fans have largely been confident in the direction of the team since the season started. And while it’s taken some hits over the course of the year, it’s rebounded and risen with every win. We aren’t quite up to the high after the win over the Dallas Cowboys, but the Giants underdog win over the Texans has a similar feel. So while fan confidence took a definite hit after the loss to the Saints, it bounced right back up. That’s to be expected, because even though the Giants had to go to overtime (again), they soundly outplayed the Texans. It’s tough to see fans being down on their team after a great win, particularly heading into an opportunity to get healthy before two divisional games.

title: Giants GM Joe Schoen explains the Jameis Winston extension
summary: New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston has gone through many ups and downs throughout the first half of the season. Winston went from being the backup that was thrusted into the starting role, but then was benched in favor of J.J. McCarthy following a poor performance against the New Orleans Saints. Winston has seen it […]
full_text: Jameis Winston | Getty Images New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston has gone through many ups and downs throughout the first half of the season. Winston went from being the backup that was thrusted into the starting role, but then was benched in favor of J.J. McCarthy following a poor performance against the New Orleans Saints. Winston has seen it all this season, and it’s only been less than two months since he signed a two-year, $13 million contract. Giants general manager Joe Schoen explained the reasoning behind Winston’s extension and defended the backup quarterback. “You’re always going to want a vet that can help the young guys while the coaches are up game planning and the quarterbacks are doing film on their own. Downstairs in the meeting room, to have a vet and just to know how valuable Jameis is to Jaxson and how valuable he will be to J.J. as well,” Schoen said. “To have the veteran presence in the room with the wisdom that Jameis has and can provide and the leadership, the multiplier effect that that will pay for those guys down the road is invaluable. So you’re always going to want a vet in the room anyways. And the way that Jameis had performed and along with the leadership, just the chemistry of that room and for the whole team, it just made sense. I’m glad we have him here.” The backup quarterback role isn’t always about stepping into games and performing when the starter gets hurt. The backup quarterback provides a calming presence to the room and sets the tone. It’s a job Winston has grown in and improved at throughout his career. While the Giants may have wished he would have performed better on the field, they are more than pleased with his overall contributions to the locker room and organization. “When you’re talking about a backup quarterback that also has leadership, that can lead not only that room, but the team. Can he go 2-2 in a four-game stretch? He went 2-1-1. And like I said, he’s led us in games where we’ve had leads in the fourth quarter or at least a tie. So you’re in the game in the fourth quarter with him and with a backup quarterback, that’s what you’re looking at,” Schoen said. Winston may not be the starter anymore, but his stint as the starter will have a large impact on how the Giants finish out the year. He may not have been perfect, but he kept the team afloat when they needed him and he’s doing what he needs to do now to be successful in his role. At the end of the day, that’s a pretty darn good backup quarterback.

title: NY Giants rookie report: Mostly good marks at the midterm
summary: The New York Giants have reached the midpoint of the 2026 season. They’re in their bye week coming off of an upset victory over the Houston Texans and in sole possession of first place in the NFC East. The Giants work in the 2026 NFL Draft was widely praised and the immediate reaction held that […]
full_text: ﻿New York Giants linebacker Arvell Reese. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants have reached the midpoint of the 2026 season. They’re in their bye week coming off of an upset victory over the Houston Texans and in sole possession of first place in the NFC East. The Giants work in the 2026 NFL Draft was widely praised and the immediate reaction held that they had one of the league’s strongest draft classes. That’s proving to be one of the keys to their success. One of the more impressive, and under-discussed aspects of the Giants’ 4-2-1 season is how much they’ve been relying on young players. The Giants are currently fourth in the NFL in offensive and defensive snap share going to rookies at 14.6%. Rookie Snap Count % through Week 7 pic.twitter.com/AYK9aptY2B — SFdata9ers🏈📊 (@sfdata9ers) October 27, 2026 That’s actually up from their 2025 numbers, when they were 13th in rookie snap share (11.8%). In other words, the performance of the Giants’ rookies has had a direct, and significant, impact on how their season has unfolded. Arvell Reese (LB) 438 defensive snaps (99%) 29 special teams snaps (1%) We don’t need to belabor the point when it comes to Arvell Reese. He’s already a star and the fifth overall pick is an absolute home run. Reese is still new to the position with all of 21 starts combined between Ohio State and the NFL. But he’s still proven to be all that the Giants could have possibly hoped he would be when he surprisingly fell to them. Reese is is a true “3-D” defender who’s a factor in run defense, pass coverage, and as a pass rusher. It doesn’t matter where the play is if it’s at the first or second level, Reese is seemingly always around the ball or making the play himself. He has a truly freakish blend of length, speed, and play strength that’s quickly turning him into a boogeyman as far as opposing tight ends, fullbacks, and running backs are concerned. His explosiveness has also made him an instant factor in the Giants’ pass rush. His ability to simply take over game when attacking gaps sparked the Giants’ defensive shift against the Arizona Cardinals and has helped to transform their defense under Dennard Wilson. Reese still needs to continue to develop as a space player, and he does occasionally get a bit out of control at times (see: his almost-sack of C.J. Stroud). But that will come in time, and perhaps not much time given how quickly he’s developing. It’s incredibly exciting to see what he might become even on the other side of this BYE week. Sisi Mauigoa (RG) 490 offensive snaps (100%) 31 special teams snaps (16%) Mauigoa hasn’t been quite the instant star that Reese was, but his trajectory is promising. Sisi got out to a hot start against the Dallas Cowboys, easily handling their defensive line. He showed off his elite power as well as his excellent movement skills (for a guard) in opening up running lanes as well as in his pass protection. Mauigoa struggled and his play was uneven over the next four weeks, with rough games against Aaron Donald and the Rams, as well as against the Washington Commanders and New Orleans Saints. There were still flashes of excellence, with him simply burying defensive linemen. Sisi Mauigoa finishes a block strongly while Jameis Winston pump-fakes 10 yards downfield. The Giants 🙌🏽 pic.twitter.com/XrQXuqMWpV — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) October 12, 2026 However, there were also too many instances of him losing to professional defensive tackles that led to negative plays, poor runs, or sacks. The good news is that he seemed to get back on track against the Houston Texans. Mauigoa had a great game and was a big reason for the Giants’ renewed run success, which is particularly encouraging considering it came against the NFL’s fourth-best run defense. Colton Hood (CB) 125 defensive snaps (34%) 46 special teams snaps (30%) There’s no two ways about it, the Giants’ second round pick has struggled when called upon this year. He’s been targeted 13 times and given up 10 completions (76.9%) for 102 yards and 3 touchdowns. The silver lining for Hood is two-fold. First, the Giants don’t currently need Hood to be excellent this year like they do some of their other rookies. Tae Banks and Greg Newsome II have both played very well as the starters and Paulson Adebo looked much improved when he came off the IR against the Texans. That gives Hood time and space to hone his craft during practice and take the lessons he learned in his two starts to heart. And in that, the second silver lining is that Hood seems to be getting excellent coaching. Dennard Wilson, Donald D’Alesio, and Addison Lynch have gotten great results out of the rest of the Giants’ defensive backs. That, and his spot on the depth chart, give confidence that (with time and work) Hood can play like the (fringe) first round prospect he was projected to be when the Giants’ drafted him. Malachi Fields (WR) 370 Offensive snaps (76%) 17 special teams snaps (9%) Fields is quickly becoming a quality secondary option behind Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely. He isn’t ready to be a primary option just yet, but Fields is proving to be too dangerous for defenses to merely ignore. He is remarkably fluid for a receiver his size, which could mean good things if he continues to develop as a route technician. Fields could be a very dangerous receiver once he learns to use his routes as a weapon, but he isn’t there just yet. He’s only 54th in the NFL in average separation (2.7 yards) and 20th in tight window throw percentage. The good news is that his size, play strength, and 38-inch vertical mean that he’s open even when he’s covered. He can play through tight coverage, extend to expand his catch radius to haul in well-placed passes, and fight through tackle attempts. Fields’ task over the bye week and the next 10 games is to work on becoming more consistent and improving his 53.3% catch rate. Considering Fields is also averaging 15.5 yards per catch, he could become one of J.J. McCarthy’s best friends. Bobby Jamison-Travis (iDL) 42 defensive snaps (32%) 12 special teams snaps (19%) The Giants’ first sixth-round pick has only played in two games, which doesn’t give us a whole lot to go on. He’s only appeared in two games, playing 21 snaps against the New Orleans Saints and 21 against the Texans. He played reasonably well against the Texans and was squarely in the mix of the Giants’ defensive line rotation. Jamison-Travis spent most of his time at nose tackle, playing either 0 or 1-technique over the center, though he did align at the 3-technique on occasion as well. Interestingly, Jamison-Travis had multiple snaps where he was on the field along with DJ Reader, and played both nose tackle and 3-technique. Jamison-Travis is a big, stout young man and he’s obviously a load for offensive linemen when he’s playing with good leverage. He’s capable of pushing centers and guards into the pocket or holding up against double teams. He understands how to put his hips in a gap to close it, and is strong enough to disengage and make plays on the ball carrier. His homework for the bye week (and beyond) is to continue to work on playing with consistently good leverage. He can be a bit too easy to move off the ball when he allows his pads to rise. J.C. Davis (OT) 25 offensive snaps (18%) 8 special teams snaps (13%) As with Jamison-Travis (and Jack Kelly), we don’t have much to go on with Davis. He’s only appeared in two games and played just 33 total snaps, all of which came in relief of Andrew Thomas against the Saints. Davis played “okay” against the Saints, all things considered. He can’t be compared to Thomas, even an injured Thomas, but did his job in a desperate comeback attempt. Davis put some good things on tape against the Saints, dealing with stunts relatively well and showing some impressive play strength in how he took on defenders. He also showed some great competitive toughness in his play as well. Davis looks like a glass eater who, even when he…
author: Chris Pflum

title: Draft prospects for the NY Giants in Week 9 of college football
summary: Good morning New York Giants fans! Happy Saturday and welcome to Week 9 of the 2026 College Football Season. The Giants are on their bye week this week and are guaranteed to control the NFC East regardless of what happens, so we’re all free to sit back and simply enjoy a weekend of football without […]
full_text: Miami defensive tackle Justin Scott recovers a fumble against Pittsburgh. | ISI Photos via Getty Images Good morning New York Giants fans! Happy Saturday and welcome to Week 9 of the 2026 College Football Season. The Giants are on their bye week this week and are guaranteed to control the NFC East regardless of what happens, so we’re all free to sit back and simply enjoy a weekend of football without stakes As usual, we’re using college football and the NFL Draft as a lens through which to look at the New York Giants. In particular, we’re going to look at the Giants’ needs as we perceive them, and focus on players who could fit those needs. Texas Tech vs. Arizona ESPN – Noon Don’t look now, but Arizona is quietly making noise and could force their way into the College Football Playoffs. Texas Tech is more highly regarded right now, but Arizona is a fun team to watch. Keep an eye on freshman linebacker Dash Fifita, younger brother of Arizona QB Noah Fifita. Dash is coming off a game against Iowa State with 2.5 tackles for a loss and 2.0 sacks… At 5-foot-7, 190 pounds. He won’t be draft eligible for two more years and might not be a draftable prospect due to his size, but he’s fun. For our purposes, however, I want to turn to the Texas Tech defense. Player spotlight: A.J. Holmes Jr. (iDL, Texas Tech) Holmes jr. transferred to Texas Tech a year ago, and was a productive member of that disruptive defensive front which carried them into the playoffs. He’s having a fantastic year as “The Guy” on Texas Tech’s defensive line. So far he has 6.5 tackles for a loss and 6.5 sacks (leads the Big 12) though 7 games, as well as 23 total tackles and a forced fumble. Holmes Jr. is listed at 6-foot-3, 300 pounds, but plays with solid leverage and anchor, as well as impressive explosiveness and power. He excels at firing out of his stance and using heavy hands to rock blockers backward before shedding and using his agility and burst to make a play on the ball. He would likely be best in a 1-gap system at the next level, and could fit the Giants as a 3 or 5-technique depending on their personnel package. As things stand now, Holmes Jr. is probably a second round pick, but he could work his way into the “1st – 2nd” range if he continues to produce as a disruptor. (8) BYU vs. Arizona State Fox – 3:30 p.m. Most of the nation will be watching BYU to see if they can rebound after their 39-31 loss to UCF a week ago. BYU catapulted themselves into the national spotlight and the Playoff conversation with their upset win over Notre Dame two weeks ago, but couldn’t avoid the letdown game the following week. For our purposes, however, we’ll be taking a look at the Sundevils. Arizona State has produced some interesting prospects over the last couple years, notably Cam Skattebo, WR Jordan Tyson, and now QB Sam Leavitt (currently at LSU). We’re going to stick to the offensive side of the ball and one of the fastest risers in recent weeks. Player spotlight: Reed Harris (WR, Arizona State) Both Harris and fellow WR Omario Miller could be of interest to the Giants, and both could be solid Day 2 picks. We’re going to focus on Harris, because he’s having a better year and his physical profile could be more appealing to the Giants. Harris is a transfer from Boston College and is an imposing presence on the field. He’s listed at 6-foot-5, 220 pounds and looks every bit of it. He appears to have solid speed and agility for a big receiver and plays with plenty of power. He has a massive catch radius as well as the ability to drag defenders as a ball carrier. There would likely be some overlap between Harris and Malachi Fields, however redundancy isn’t necessarily a bad thing. The Giants have increasingly used Malik Nabers in the slot and he’s responded well, getting nearly as many yards from the slot as out wide, despite having far fewer snaps as a slot receiver. Adding a second big wide receiver could allow the Giants to use Nabers as a slot receiver even more often, or create size mismatches with smaller corners. North Carolina vs. (1) Miami ABC – 7:30 p.m. We’re checking in on the ACC in the evening slate. The matchups between Ohio State and USC or Texas and Mississippi State may be more compelling, but the Hurricanes have a number of defensive players that could interest the Giants. Likewise, QB Darian Mensah could be one of the linchpins early in the draft, and sophomore WR Malachi Toney is simply a human highlight reel. Player Spotlight: Justin Scott (iDL, Miami) The Giants might not want to spend a first round pick on a defensive tackle — or the board may not line up for them even if they do. But, as noted up above, this is shaping up to be an impressively deep defensive tackle class. We’ve already talked about Miami defensive tackle Ahmad Moten, and his teammate is a high-upside player as well. Scott has a versatile frame at 6-foot-4, 305 pounds with enough length and strength to play any gap alignment in an even or odd front. He boasts an explosive first step and should be a dangerous gap-shooter in a one-gap defense, while also having a powerful lower body to take on blockers in the run game. In addition to great explosiveness and power, he also has the kind of wide-open motor and competitive toughness we’ve come to expect from this Miami defense. That combination should appeal to the Giants’ coaching staff, and Scott could easily step into Shelby Harris’ spot as a 3, 4i, or 5-technique. There’s currently some speculation that Scott could work his way into the first round conversation thanks to his traits. However, this could be a very deep defensive tackle class and there are prospects with similarly impressive traits who also have significant production to their name. As of this writing, Scott has 21 tackles but only 1.0 tackle for a loss and 0 sacks on the season. Unlike many of the defensive tackles the Giants have drafted lately, Scott is still young and won’t turn 21 until January. It’s possible that he could slide in a deep class and be available to the Giants somewhere in the second round.
author: Chris Pflum

title: NY Giants John Harbaugh violated norms, called Titans ownership about Jeffery Simmons
summary: New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh took the extraordinary step of calling Tennessee Titans ownership directly in an effort to acquire star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, according to a startling report from Jonathan Jones of The Athletic. Per Jones, that breaks with “traditional NFL trade-talk norms” where general managers deal directly with each other. […]
full_text: John Harbaugh | Getty Images New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh took the extraordinary step of calling Tennessee Titans ownership directly in an effort to acquire star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, according to a startling report from Jonathan Jones of The Athletic . Per Jones, that breaks with “traditional NFL trade-talk norms” where general managers deal directly with each other. Jones reported that Harbaugh contacted Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk after Giants GM Joe Schoen had been told by Titans GM Mike Borgonzi that Simmons, a 29-year-old four-time Pro Bowler and 2025 First-Team All-Pro, would not be traded. Strunk apparently gave Harbaugh the same message. That obviously changed when the Chicago Bears made a Godfather offer to the Titans of two first-round and a fourth-round draft pick. Per Jones, one GM said Harbaugh’s call to Strunk “violates a code amongst primary football decision-makers, that they will only deal with each other.” Valentine’s View Whether Harbaugh violated NFL traditions or not, the move tells you a couple of things about the Giants. This is clearly Harbaugh’s show. We have told you that before, but this is absolutely evidence that Harbaugh is front-and-center in every major decision, and that he will do whatever he believes necessary to get something done. Even if that steps on toes. The Giants are clearly intent upon seizing the opportunity they have in the NFC East. Forget building. Harbaugh wants the Giants to be the best they can be right now, and if there is a star player out there like Simmons or running back Jonathan Taylor who can help make that happen, the Giants will try to get it done. Whether going for it right now is the correct approach, after the Giants have spent most of the last 15 years floundering you have to appreciate the boldness. I think it is also important to note that Simmons and Taylor, who is now reportedly available , are players who would be more than short-term, 2026 upgrades. One other note in terms of surrendering draft capital. Whether it is too early for a Jaxson Dart vs. J.J. McCarthy debate, the Giants clearly understand that if they spend draft capital now, they possess two desirable, 23-year-old quarterbacks and they can use one in the offseason to recoup premium draft picks.

title: Colts willing to trade RB Jonathan Taylor, per report
summary: The Indianapolis Colts are now willing to trade star running back Jonathan Taylor, per a report from Adam Schefter of ESPN. Schefter adds in his report that the New York Giants are among the teams thought to have at least “some level of interest” in trading for Taylor. Schefter also lists the Seattle Seahawks, Denver […]
full_text: Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts are now willing to trade star running back Jonathan Taylor , per a report from Adam Schefter of ESPN . Schefter adds in his report that the New York Giants are among the teams thought to have at least “some level of interest” in trading for Taylor. Schefter also lists the Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos, Minnesota Vikings, Green Bay Packers as teams believed to be interested in trading for Taylor. It’s no secret that while new Giants head coach John Harbaugh likes the trio of Cam Skattebo , Tyrone Tracy , and Devin Singletary , he has coveted a “bellcow” running back. The Giants reportedly pursued Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III in free agency and it was likewise reported that star Notre Dame running back Jeremiyah Love was tied with Arvell Reese at the top of their board. It was widely believed that the Giants would have drafted Love at fifth overall if he was still available. One of the issues with the Giants’ backfield is that while they lack an explosive option out of the backfield, and Taylor has been one of the NFL’s most explosive runners. Last year he was tied for sixth in the NFL with 16 designed runs of 15+ yards, and was third in “breakaway” runs. He also led the NFL with 18 rushing touchdowns to just two (2) fumbles last year. Our own Ed Valentine wrote earlier this week that the Giants should capitalize on their opportunity to win the NFC East this year and go all-in on the 27-year old Taylor. After a report that head coach John Harbaugh personally called Tennessee Titans ownership in an effort to get defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons , who landed with the Chicago Bears, you can expect the Giants to be aggressive in pursuit of Taylor. The move would likely cost significant draft capital, possibly a first round pick to replace the one the Colts traded to the New York Jets. That’s real consideration oncern in a 2027 draft class that’s shaping up to be very talented and deep at a number of positions of need for the Giants. Acquiring Taylor would also require significant cap space and financial maneuvering. However, the argument is that Taylor is among the very best runners in the NFL and could complete a true “three headed monster” with wide receiver Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely. And frankly, if Taylor becomes the apple of Harbaugh’s eye, it becomes Joe Schoen’s job to do everything in his power to acquire the running back. So what do you think Giants’ fans? Do you think the Giants are serious contenders for Taylor? And should they be?
author: Chris Pflum

title: NY Giants defensive review: Kudos, Wet Willies, and thoughts on every player
summary: The New York Giants defense under coordinator Dennard Wilson has become an aggressive unit that is playing well despite the loss of Brian Burns, questions on the defensive line, and churn in the secondary due to injuries. Let’s go position-by-position with Kudos, Wet Willies, and thoughts on every player. Defensive line D.J. Reader — Dexter […]
full_text: Abdul Carter | Getty Images The New York Giants defense under coordinator Dennard Wilson has become an aggressive unit that is playing well despite the loss of Brian Burns, questions on the defensive line, and churn in the secondary due to injuries. Let’s go position-by-position with Kudos, Wet Willies, and thoughts on every player. Defensive line D.J. Reader — Dexter Lawrence is an elite player who has returned to form this season with the Cincinnati Bengals. It isn’t worth crying over spilt milk, though. Reader has been everything the Giants could have hoped for in a replacement. Maybe more. Pro Football Focus, in fact, ranks Reader as the best defensive tackle in football so far this season with an elite 90.4 grades. Lawrence (87.6) is No. 2). Want to see a major difference in grading systems? Pro Football and Sports Network, which puts much more weight on pass rush, has Reader as its 53rd-ranked defensive tackle, with Lawrence at No. 2. Regardless of all of the number gobbledygook (now that’s a cool Halloween word), Reader has been outstanding for the Giants. They just need to get him some help. Grade: Kudos Shelby Harris — The fact that Harris is the Giants’ second-best defensive lineman tells you why the position is an issue, and a priority for the team to address before the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline. The 35-year-old, in his 13th NFL season, is not the player he once was. Statistical sites, in fact, tell us that Harris is clearly having what is by far the worst season of his career. Pro Football Focus tells us Harris is No. 102 of 126 qualifying defensive tackles, and that his 49.2 grade is the first would be the first time in his career he has graded below 60.0. Pro Football and Sports Network shows a similar degradation in Harris’ play. Harris is still playing a ton of snaps (238 thus far, 54%), and doing what he can. At this point in his career, though, the Giants appear to be asking too much of him. Grade: Kwillie Darius Alexander — One reason the Giants are asking so much of the aging Harris is that Alexander, a 2025 third-round pick, has not given them enough. PFSN ranks Alexander 119th among 121 qualifying defensive tcles this season, and PFF ranks him No. 102 of 147 qualifiers in their grading system. Alexander’s talent and athleticism tell you he should be much more than he has been. Grade: Wet Willie Bobby Jamison-Travis — The rookie sixth-round pick did not see action until Week 6 against the New Orleans Saints. He played well against the run vs. the Houston Texans in Week 7, giving reason to hope he can contribute, but 42 total defensive snaps is not enough to give a legitimate grade. Grade: Incomplete C.J. Okoye — The Giants acquired the 6-foot-6, 365-pound 24-year-old from the Baltimore Ravens, where he had played for John Harbaugh, for the low price of a 2028 seventh-round pick. They hoped Okoye would take a step forward in his development and become a solid rotational run defender. It hasn’t happened, and Okoye has played just 87 defensive snaps (14.5 per game) across six games. A man as big and strong as Okoye shouldn’t be pushed out of a hole by blockers as easily and as often as Okoye is. Grade: Wet Willie Chauncey Golston — The veteran defensive end had earned a big role on defense before a neck injury short-circuited his season. Grade: Incomplete Edge defender Abdul Carter — The No. 3 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft has spent the season reminding everyone why the Giants drafted him so high a year ago. His sack numbers (2.0) just don’t yet reflect how good the 23-year-old has actually been. Carter has been a nightmare for opposing blockers this season, and is one one three qualifying edge defenders with elite Pro Football Focus grades of 90.0 or higher. With a 90.3 mark, he joins Will Anderson (90.8) and Aidan Hutchinson (92.2). PFSN penalizes him for the lack of sacks, ranking him a ridiculousy low No. 58 among 122 qualifiers. Abdul Carter is tied with Will Anderson Jr. for 3rd in the NFL in total pass-rush wins, but that hasn't led to an overly impressive pressure rate or sack total. Couple of thoughts on why Carter's still been an impactful pass rusher and the pressures + sacks should come below pic.twitter.com/e6s9wdYsio — Ben Linsey (@benlinsey_) October 26, 2026 Carter had a rocky rookie season, marked by maturity issues. This season, he has stepped up as both a player and as a vocal locker room leader. Grade: Kudos Kayvon Thibodeaux — The No. 5 pick in the 2022 NFL Draft is always a lightning rod for disagreement when it comes to trying to assess his play. The pure numbers would tell you that Thibodeaux, starting after Brian Burns’ unfortunate season-ending injury, has been terrible and the Giants should either trade him before the upcoming deadline or happily let him walk in free agency at season’s end. He is 12th on the team in tackles (15), doesn’t have a tackle for loss or a sack, and has just one quarterback hit. But, there are other more advanced and less visible to the naked eye measures that tell you there are plenty of ways in which Thibodeaux has been quietly effective. Kayvon Thibodeaux in the last 3 games Pass Rush Win Rate: 18.3% – 7th in the NFL (among EDGE's) Run Stop%: 9.2 – 4th in the NFL (among EDGE's) Stops: 6 – 1st in the NFL (among EDGE's) pic.twitter.com/cENtBdKC50 — Marshall Green (@MarshallGreen_) October 26, 2026 Two things can be true at the same time, and in this case probably are. Thibodeaux is a good player, and if he were a third-round pick he would probably be looked at as a fantastic find at that point in the draft. Quietly effective, though, is not what you are hoping for from a No. 5 overall pick. Grade: Kwillie Brian Burns — I feel terrible for Burns. He is a pro’s pro, a nice guy, and a locker room leader who approaches and plays the game the right way. In eight NFL seasons, though, Burns has never had the good fortune of playing for a team that has made the playoffs. This Giants team has the chance to do that, and his season-ending knee injury means Burns won’t have a chance to help make that happen. Grade: Incomplete Trace Ford — The second-year former undrafted free agent gets credit for perseverance. The Giants cut him in 2025, and he spent part of the season on the team’s practice squad. They cut him again this year, and he again landed on the practice squad. Burns’ injury opened an opportunity for him to be a game-day elevation, and he parlayed that into a spot on the 53-man roster. Ford has shown some potential with 10 tackles and three hurries over four games and 70 defensive snaps. Grade: Kudos Inside linebacker Arvell Reese — I don’t care how good David Bailey, Jeremiyah Love, or Carnell Tate turn out to be, how did the New York Jets, Arizona Cardinals, and Tennessee Titans let this guy fall to the Giants with the fifth pick in the 2026 NFL Draft? Arvell Reese with one of the best HUSTLE plays you’ll ever see out of a LB. The Giants rookie LB is built like and plays like an absolute CYBORG 😳👽 pic.twitter.com/NM3QZjyjS9 — Rookie Watch (@RookieWatxh) October 26, 2026 “Man, how good has he been? He’s been awesome. He’s been phenomenal since the day he got here,” GM Joe Schoen said during his bye week press conference. “And that’s probably why Coach and I, even in that [draft] video, we were shocked he was there. So, he’s just a quiet kid that goes about his business and he’s all ball all the time. “That play he made the other day where he should have had the sack on (Houston Texans quarterback) C.J. (Stroud) and then turns around and hauls tail all the way down the field and puts the guy flat on his back while punching for the ball. I mean, you don’t see many people with his size that can move like that. And then just, that’s internal. That’s just want to. To go towards the quarterback and then turn and run, you can’t coach that. You either got that or you don’t. And his effort and the way he plays and flies around, I mean, you see him on film, he’s moving at a…

full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-SEPTEMBER 27: Running back Breece Hall #20 of the New York Jets is checked for injury during the second half of an NFL football game between the New York Jets and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, September 27, 2026 (Photo by Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Breece Hall will not be suiting up for the New York Jets when they take on the Las Vegas Raiders today. Hall will be inactive for the fifth consecutive week after he suffered a quadriceps injury against the Detroit Lions in the Jets’ third game of the 2026 season. The Jets are hopeful Hall will finally get back into the lineup next week against the Kansas City Chiefs. Hall’s absence has created an opportunity for Braelon Allen at running back, and Allen has taken full advantage. In the four games Allen has started in Hall’s absence this season Allen has put together two 100+ rushing yards games. Overall, Allen has averaged 4.6 yards per carry this season while already posting career highs in rushing yards with 418 and yards from scrimmage with 493. Allen has arguably been a more effective back than Hall, and he has presumably earned a larger role in the Jets’ offense even when Hall is back in the lineup. The full Jets inactive list for today’s game is as follows: Breece Hall David Bailey Joseph Ossai Nahshon Wright Tim Patrick Kohl Levao Max Mitchell Notable among those names is Nahshon Wright. Wright signed with the Jets in the offseason after earning a Pro Bowl nod last year with the Chicago Bears. Unfortunately that signing has not worked out for Wright or the Jets. Wright has been active for just three games for the Jets. He has played just 22 snaps, all on special teams. It probably would behoove the Jets to move Wright at the trade deadline, assuming there is any market for him.

title: Jets vs Raiders Pre-Game Ball
summary: Plenty of people hand out game balls after the game. That’s easy. Watch the game, see who does well, give them the game ball. We’re doing something a little different. We’re handing out a pre-game ball. Before we watch the game, let’s settle on a player or players we think might be a decisive advantage […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - NOVEMBER 13: The Jets offensive line during a game between the New England Patriots and the New York Jets on November 13, 2025, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Plenty of people hand out game balls after the game. That’s easy. Watch the game, see who does well, give them the game ball. We’re doing something a little different. We’re handing out a pre-game ball. Before we watch the game, let’s settle on a player or players we think might be a decisive advantage for the Jets in the upcoming game. Occasionally we might hand out a pre-blame ball. If we think the Jets are going to get slaughtered, we’ll try to identify a prime culprit. One caveat: the quarterback is off limits. Nothing personal against quarterbacks, but they are obviously the most important players on the field. We could give out a pre-game or pre-blame ball to the quarterback virtually every week, but that would be boring, so we’re not going to do it. We’ll try to identify somebody besides the quarterback for the glory or the ignominy. This approach comes with the obvious drawback that predictions are difficult, especially about the future. We’re destined to get many of these wrong. No matter. We’ll have some laughs along the way. Let’s get to it. The pre-game ball for the Jets game against the Las Vegas Raiders goes to (drum roll please) – the offensive line! The Raiders have struggled in run defense this season. They have allowed a league worst 5.0 yards per carry on the year. They have allowed an average of 143+ rushing yards per game, good for 31st in the NFL. The Raiders have allowed 165+ rushing yards in three of the last four games. In short, the Raiders’ run defense has been putrid. The Jets have not run the ball particularly well this year. They have averaged less than 97 rushing yards per game, good for 24th in the NFL, and they have averaged just 3.8 yards per carry, good for 26th in the NFL. The Jets have done better lately, averaging 113 rushing yards over the last three games. On Sunday the Jets will get guard Dylan Parham back in the lineup for the first time since game 3 of the season. With the full set of starting offensive linemen healthy and ready to go on Sunday, the Jets should be focused on running the ball against the Raiders’ very bad run defense. I don’t know who will be running the ball. Breece Hall may or may not suit up for this game. But whoever is running the ball, this is a game the Jets’ offensive line needs to dominate. Clear holes for the running backs consistently. Allow for long, grinding drives. Give Geno Smith time to throw. That’s how the Jets can win this game. Jets offensive line, come on down! It’s time to live up to your pre-season billing against an opponent tailor made for your success. You get your opportunity on Sunday. Let’s see you dominate. What about you? Who would you give the pre-game ball to? Let us know in the comments

title: Jets vs Raiders: Five Questions with Silver and Black Pride
summary: The New York Jets are at home in East Rutherford, New Jersey on Sunday for the 8th game of their 2026 campaign. They will be facing the Las Vegas Raiders. The Raiders have lost four straight games after starting the season 3-0. Previewing this matchup, Matt Holder, a writer at Silver and Black Pride, was […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 12: Cornerback Nate Hobbs #39 and safety Tre'von Moehrig #25 of the Las Vegas Raiders break up a pass to wide receiver Garrett Wilson #17 of the New York Jets in the fourth quarter of their game at Allegiant Stadium on November 12, 2023 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Raiders defeated the Jets 16-12. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets are at home in East Rutherford, New Jersey on Sunday for the 8th game of their 2026 campaign. They will be facing the Las Vegas Raiders. The Raiders have lost four straight games after starting the season 3-0. Previewing this matchup, Matt Holder, a writer at Silver and Black Pride , was kind enough to answer a few questions regarding the 2026 Las Vegas Raiders. 1. The Raiders started the season with a bang, going 3-0 out of the gate, before falling back to earth recently with a four-game losing streak. What was going right for the Raiders early on, and why have they reversed course recently? A big part of it was the schedule. The Raiders got to start the season against the Dolphins (who could lose to them?), Chargers and Saints. Those teams are a combined 3-16, while the Chiefs, Patriots, Bills and Rams (the four-game losing streak) are all legitimate playoff/Super Bowl contenders. Granted, the Rams aren’t the juggernaut many thought they’d be, but Los Angeles was on a mission last week. The other major factor is Las Vegas’ defense. In the first two games, the unit held Miami and the Chargers to 13 and 14 points, respectively. Then, New Orleans managed to put up 27 points, and it started to feel like the defense was showing some cracks. That proved true, seeing as the Raiders averaged over 35 points per game allowed in October. Ultimately, the Raiders’ defense is too reliant on creating turnovers. They had nine in the first three games, including four fourth-quarter turnovers to fuel a comeback against the Saints. However, they have just three in the last four games, with two coming in the second half against the Rams last week when the game was already out of hand. The quality of opponents and quarterbacks certainly played a role in that, as well as defensive coordinator Rob Leonard showing signs of being a first-time play caller. Leonard has a decent scheme (he’s running a similar system to Mike Macdonald in Seattle), and he was able to create some confusion with safety rotations and unique coverages in the first month of the season. However, now that the book is out on him, good offensive play-callers have been able to pick on Leonard’s tendacies. At the end of the day, this was supposed to be year one of a two-year rebuild in Vegas. This is a team that was literally the worst in the NFL last year, and Klint Kubiak has managed to pull them out of the basement by winning those first three contests. But the 3-0 start was a mirage when it comes to the Raiders’ playoff hopes, and the last four weeks proved that. 2. The Raiders hope they have found a long term answer at quarterback with the first overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft, Fernando Mendoza. When do you think we’ll see Mendoza take over at quarterback? Who do you think should be starting at this point, Cousins or Mendoza, and if it’s Cousins, what would cause you to change course and get Mendoza in there? If it were up to me, Mendoza would be taking over as the starter this week. Cousins is far from the team’s biggest issue — he’s actually played above expectations this season — but it’s clear the Raiders aren’t going to the postseason with him because the rest of the roster just isn’t ready yet. To me, why delay the inevitable? It’s time to start planning for the future by giving the rookie as much experience as possible and letting him work through the struggles. Get the bad games out now, learn from them and grow for 2027 and beyond. But of course, that’s irrelevant since Kubiak doesn’t agree and his opinion is what really matters, not mine. I wasn’t surprised at all that Kubiak announced Cousins will remain the starting quarterback this week because Las Vegas is technically still “in the hunt”. The head coach literally said that when he made the announcement. Also, I think the staff wants to figure out the offensive line woes and the running game before throwing Mendoza to the wolves. I get that; I just don’t think those changes are going to happen until the offseason. It’s trending toward the No. 1 pick taking over after the bye week. The Raiders have a late bye this year (Week 13), meaning he wouldn’t start until December. However, the schedule softens up with games against the Chargers, Broncos (tough matchup), Titans, Cardinals and Chiefs (who might have nothing to play for in Week 18) to round out the season. Meanwhile, the Jets, 49ers, Seahawks, Broncos and Browns are up next, and all five teams have pretty strong defenses. 3. Can you give us a synopsis of what the 2026 Raiders draft class has looked like so far, and what you expect from them as the year goes on? One of the potentially concerning parts of the Raiders’ rebuild is that safety Treydan Stukes is the only player from the draft class who is starting consistently right now. As mentioned above, Mendoza will take over at some point, but obviously, he hasn’t done anything yet. Stukes has been a good rookie free safety, but third-round picks edge Keyron Crawford (out for the season with an injury) and offensive lineman Trey Zuhn III (the offense’s jumbo tight end right now) have barely contributed. Granted, that could change this week because Kubiak hinted at shaking up the offensive line (for the second time in the first half of the season), and Zuhn would be the next man up at guard. Cornerback Jermod McCoy was considered the “steal of the draft”, as a first-round talent who went in the fourth. However, McCoy has looked like a guy who hasn’t had many live reps since 2024 when he has been on the field, even though he’s played a limited number of snaps this season. Running back Mike Washington Jr. has contributed (40 carries, 195 yards, 1 TD) as the No. 2 back behind Ashton Jeanty, and has the better yards per carry (4.9 to 3.1) of the two backs. Granted, defenses definitely key in on Jeanty more when he’s in the backfield. Fifth-round corner Hezekiah Masses has provided some good moments with a team-leading three interceptions (the defense has five total) and has made four starts. However, Masses is very reliant on his ball skills and isn’t sticky in coverage, giving up a lot of yards in coverage, too. That’s led to him splitting reps with second-year pro Darien Porter over the last few weeks. That’s pretty much all of the notable rookies since safety Dalton Johnson (fifth-rounder, active for one game so far), wide receiver Malik Benson (sixth-rounder, special teamer) and defensive tackle Brandon Cleveland (seventh-rounder, currently on practice squad) round out the class. 4. Every team has a player or two who may be somewhat unfamiliar to other teams’ fans but is known to be an unsung hero by fans of his own team. Who are the Raiders’ unsung heroes? If possible, give us one guy on each side of the ball. Defensively, there aren’t many options, but I’d say Stukes is the unsung hero. The rookie hasn’t been perfect, but he has made a few plays in both coverage and against the run to provide some hope for his long-term outlook. When Stukes was injured early in the season, there was a clear drop-off in the Raiders’ safety play, and he’s been a big improvement over what the Raiders had on the back end last year. Also, linebacker Nakobe Dean could fall into this category since he’s responsible for four turnovers this season, but I feel like most people already know who Dean is. Offensively, there are two I can’t pick between: wide receiver Tre Tucker and tight end Michael Mayer. Tucker’s production comes in spurts — his biggest calling card is as a deep threat — but he ranks 16th in the league with 474 receiving yards heading into Week 8.…

full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 11: T'vondre Sweat #99 of the New York Jets in action during the game against the Cleveland Browns at MetLife Stadium on October 11, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) | Getty Images Prior to the New York Jets’ game against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, the Jets placed defensive tackle T’Vondre Sweat on the injured reserve list. He will miss at least the next four games. The Jets also signed defensive tackle Payton Page to the active roster and elevated offensive tackle Brant Banks and edge defender Quinton Bell from the practice squad. Payton Page is a 24 year old, 6’ 4”, 300 pound defensive tackle out of Clemson. He was originally signed as an undrafted free agent by the Jets in 2025. Page played in 4 games with the Jets in 2025, registering 6 tackles and 1 tackle for loss. He has spent the entire 2026 season to date on the Jets’ practice squad. Brant Banks is a 26 year old, 6’ 7”, 307 pound second year offensive tackle out of Rice. He was signed as an undrafted free agent by the Green Bay Packers in 2025 and played two games for them last year, playing a total of six snaps for the Packers, all on special teams. The Packers released Banks in August, 2026 and the Jets signed him to the practice squad. He has yet to play a snap in the NFL in 2026. Quinton Bell is a 30 year old, 6’ 4”, 258 pound edge defender out of Prairie View A& M. He was originally drafted by the Raiders in the 7th round of the 2019 NFL draft. Bell was cut by the Raiders prior to the 2019 season. He has since bounced around the league, including stints with the Miami Dolphins, Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Atlanta Falcons, Philadelphia Eagles, San Francisco 49ers and now the Jets. In 33 NFL games Bell has played mostly on special teams. He has 38 tackles, 4 tackles for loss, 1 sack, 1 forced fumble, 1 pass defended and 1 fumble recovery in his career.
