title: Previewing the Jets’ opposition: Las Vegas Raiders
summary: The Jets and Raiders represent two franchises that have been trying to rebuild for a long time, without much success. Having picked first and second in the 2026 NFL draft, the teams meet on Sunday with each trying desperately not to fall out of contention yet again. While the Jets could easily be better than […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 25: Tonka Hemingway #97 of the Las Vegas Raiders celebrates with teammates after a sack against Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams during the first quarter at Allegiant Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jets and Raiders represent two franchises that have been trying to rebuild for a long time, without much success. Having picked first and second in the 2026 NFL draft, the teams meet on Sunday with each trying desperately not to fall out of contention yet again. While the Jets could easily be better than their current 2-5 record, the Raiders stand 3-4 having won their first three only to then lose four straight. When these teams last met, in 2023, Las Vegas beat the Jets 16-12 in a frustrating game that dropped the Jets below .500. Whoever loses this one will be similarly frustrated. Let’s break down the Raiders’ roster going position by position: Quarterbacks The Raiders got rid of Geno Smith during the offseason and replaced him with someone even older, the 38-year old Kirk Cousins. So far, Cousins is off to a productive start and the Raiders have the number four passing game in the NFL as he leads the league with 16 touchdown passes. However, while the Raiders have been marching up and down the field and are 2nd in the league in terms of red zone visits, they are down in 29th for touchdown conversion percentage in the red zone. They were 1-for-5 down there in Sunday’s loss to the Rams. Of course, the biggest quarterback story for the Raiders is currently on ice, as the number one overall pick Fernando Mendoza won’t get a chance to show the Jets what they missed out on unless Cousins is hurt or benched during Sunday’s game. His first start probably isn’t too far away though, and he did complete six of eight passes in garbage time action so far this season. The number three is Aidan O’Connell, who beat the Jets as a rookie in the aforementioned 2023 game. Offensive Line The Raiders’ offensive line was awful last year, although two of the players they got rid of – Dylan Parham and Jordan Meredith – are actually faring quite well with the Jets. Former Raven Tyler Linderbaum was brought in at center to stabilize things, signing a massive $81 million deal. The jury is still out on this deal because, while the offensive line is definitely improved, his own performance has been somewhat underwhelming. He leads the team with five offensive penalties in seven games. The Raiders also brought in Spencer Burford on a low-cost one-year deal and he’s currently starting at left guard. Burford is best known for blowing a costly assignment in overtime during the 49ers’ recent Super Bowl loss. The other three players listed as starters are all returning from last year’s group: Kolton Miller at left tackle, DJ Glaze at right tackle and Jackson Powers-Johnson at right guard. However, Powers-Johnson was recently benched for Caleb Rogers with the suggestion being that he doesn’t fit the system and could be traded at the deadline. He is also listed as questionable having missed practice time due to a back issue. Glaze led the team in offensive snaps last year, as the one constant on a line that kept changing personnel. Miller is the team’s highest paid offensive player, but has given up a team-high four sacks. The rest of the bench comprises guard Bryce Cabeldue, tackle Charles Grant and third round rookie guard Trey Zuhn III. Grant was a third round pick who had one start as a rookie last season but Cabeldue and Zuhn have played less than 50 offensive snaps between them in regular season action. Zuhn sees some time as a sixth lineman in jumbo packages, though. Running Backs Last year’s top pick Ashton Jeanty continues to see a lot of the ball and rack up production by volume even though he hasn’t been all that effective with a 3.1 yards per carry average. Having come within 25 yards of a thousand-yard season as a rookie, he’s ramped up his passing game production this year and has accounted for 640 yards from scrimmage with four total touchdowns. Jeanty made headlines during the week when he suggested that unnamed Jets players didn’t like to tackle. That was ironic given that he is 25th out of 26 qualifying backs in terms of forced missed tackles so far this season according to Pro Football Focus. Fourth round rookie Mike Washington Jr. has shown some early promise in a reserve role, though, as he is averaging almost five yards per carry. Dylan Laube is the number three back and Connor Heyward is listed as the fullback, although he will also line up at tight end. Pass catchers The Raiders’ best pass catching weapon is pro bowler Brock Bowers. The tight end missed two games but is still tied with Jeanty for the team lead in receptions on 31, for 455 yards and three scores. His fellow tight end Michael Mayer also has 31 catches. Leading the team in receiving yards and touchdown receptions, though, is Tre Tucker with 474 yards and four scores. No other Raiders wideout has double figures in catches, although Cody White has made his eight catches count, with three of them being touchdowns. Jalen Nailor is the other starter along with Tucker, but has just 75 yards on eight catches for the season. Last year’s second round pick, Jack Bech, would presumably be playing a significant role if he weren’t on injured reserve, though, and he has been practicing this week so he may be about to return. His official game status is questionable. Dont’e Thornton, Malik Benson and Dareke Young are also on the roster at wideout and Ian Thomas is the number three tight end. Benson was drafted in the sixth round in April. Defensive Line As ever, the Raiders’ biggest threat on either side of the ball is all-pro defensive end Maxx Crosby. However, it’s the other two edges in the Raiders’ three man rotation – Malcolm Koonce and Kwity Paye – who are tied for the team lead on three sacks each. Crosby certainly hasn’t been slacking, though. His 16 quarterback hits are more than twice as many as any other player on the team. At defensive tackle, Adam Butler and Tonka Hemingway are listed as the starters. However, ex-Jet Folorunso Fatukasi has actually started all seven games. With third round pick Keyron Crawford on injured reserve, depth on the edge comes from Patrick Johnson, although he’s out of Sunday’s game with a stinger. Thomas Booker and JJ Pegues provide further depth inside. Linebackers The Raiders signed linebacker Nakobe Dean to a $12 million per year contract in the offseason and he’s been a settling influence on the defense in the same way Linderbaum was supposed to be for the offense. Dean is tied for the league lead with three forced fumbles and has 68 tackles, 1.5 sacks and an interception. The other starter at linebacker is former first round pick Quay Walker, who has a team-high five tackles for loss, while Tommy Eichenberg sees action in base packages. Cody Lindenberg and Segun Olubi provide depth off the bench. Olubi started two games for the Colts back in 2023. Defensive Backs The Raiders’ 3-0 start was significantly influenced by fifth round rookie Hezekiah Masses, who intercepted three passes in the first three games. However, since that time, Masses has found himself back in a reserve role as he has given up four touchdowns and five defensive penalties with the defense now statistically one of the league’s worst. Eric Stokes, who signed a three-year, $30 million extension during the offseason and Darien Porter are now starting on the outside after Porter had previously seen his starting role taken away by Masses. In addition, Taron Johnson is one of the most reliable slot specialists in the league. At safety, the Raiders drafted Treydan Stukes in the second round and he’s been starting alongside veteran Jeremy Chinn. Isaiah Pola-Mao sees time in three-safety sets. The Raiders also drafted Jermod McCoy and Dalton Johnson in the middle rounds to add some depth at…

title: Saquon Barkley trade rumors: Eagles running back to remain in Philly
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles will NOT be trading Saquon Barkley ahead of the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, November 10, according to reporting from ESPN. Still, Howie Roseman and the Eagles believe they still have plenty of talent on the roster to compete in 2027 and beyond. That’s why, according to sources, they’ve made it clear […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Saquon Barkley #26 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs the ball during the third quarter against the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles will NOT be trading Saquon Barkley ahead of the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, November 10, according to reporting from ESPN . Still, Howie Roseman and the Eagles believe they still have plenty of talent on the roster to compete in 2027 and beyond. That’s why, according to sources, they’ve made it clear to teams they’re not considering trading Barkley. It’s a bit ironic that there’s talk about the Eagles’ long-term vision for Barkley on the same day that they’re counting on him to play through significant injury in a risky attempt to salvage a sinking 2026 season. Some more thoughts to unpack from this report: I think everyone can agree the Eagles shouldn’t be interested in unloading Barkley regardless of the price. This isn’t the same situation that some of their others players are in as impending free agents (see: Moro Ojomo, Riq Woolen). You’re only trading Barkley if the price is too good to refuse, such as it was in the Cam Jurgens trade . Not just because you decided you’re sellers so you’ll take whatever you can get. It seems like Roseman has already gauged the market and sensed there isn’t a no-brainer offer to be had for Barkley, hence this reporting come to light. Perhaps the intent of this report is to set reasonable expectations for the public. But perhaps it’s also a message that teams interested in Barkley must significantly increase their offers if they want him. Barring a no-trade clause, most players don’t have a say in whether they’re traded or not. There’s a case to be made that Barkley deserves more of a voice in these conversations than the average player due to his championship contributions to this franchise. Again, it’s not like you’re turning down a no-brainer haul because of his preferences. But it would be bad form to trade him somewhere against his will, especially if the price isn’t even all that great. The feeling here is that the Eagles could eventually regret not moving Barkley — who turns 30 in February — if they’re passing on some really strong offers. But we don’t know if those are even on the table for him, especially while he’s hampered by injury. It’ll be worth be paying attention to what the Indianapolis Colts can fetch in return for Jonathan Taylor as a potential comparison.

title: Eagles roster news: 2 moves announced ahead of Commanders game
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced two roster moves ahead of the team’s Week 8 Sunday night game against the Washington Commanders. Here’s an overview: Note: teams are permitted to temporarily elevate up to two practice squad players per game. A player can be elevated up to three times in the regular season and an unlimited […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Elijah Mitchell #49 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs the ball during an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced two roster moves ahead of the team’s Week 8 Sunday night game against the Washington Commanders. Here’s an overview: RB Elijah Mitchell and EDGE Mason Reiger were temporarily elevated from the practice squad. Note: teams are permitted to temporarily elevate up to two practice squad players per game . A player can be elevated up to three times in the regular season and an unlimited number of times in the postseason. Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. ELIJAH MITCHELL Saquon Barkley will play against the Commanders despite being listed under “did not participate” on Wednesday and Thursday before being upgraded to limited on Friday. It remains to be seen how much of a workload he can handle; Barkley was clearly playing through discomfort from his hamstring and back injuries in Week 7. He was ultimately limited to 10 snaps on Monday night. Jaydon Blue, who was promoted from the practice squad earlier this week, is the only other Eagles running back on the roster. The Eagles previously had him active for Week 6 but did not play him at all despite injuries knocking them down to Dameon Pierce (who is now on injured reserve) as the only backfield option in that game. By elevating Mitchell, the Eagles now have three running backs for Sunday’s game. He could also factor in as a kick returner with Britan Covey out. This is Mitchell’s second temporary elevation this season. He only has one more remaining. MASON REIGER Reiger is set to make his Eagles debut after originally joining Philadelphia’s practice squad on August 31. The Eagles are currently banged up at edge rusher, sort of. It’s not to the point where their edge rushers won’t suit up for Sunday’s game. But it is to the point where Jalyx Hunt and Jonathan Greenard saw way fewer snaps than normal in Week 7. Nolan Smith is also coming off a concussion while Arnold Ebiketie has been playing a lot due to the other injuries at his position. Reiger likely won’t play much, if at all, on defense but he’s around for depth purposes in addition to contributing on special teams. NON-MOVES For the third game in a row, Zach Ertz will sit out while being on the practice squad. The Eagles already used up his three temporary elevations, so, he can only play if he’s on the roster. And the Eagles have instead opted to go with Dallas Goedert, Johnny Mundt, Eli Stowers, and Grant Calcaterra as their top four tight ends. Maybe the plan is to bring Ertz up if/when the Eagles deal Goedert ahead of the NFL trade deadline? We’ll see. In the meantime, Ertz continues to be seven receptions away from tying the Eagles’ all-time franchise record in that category. The Eagles notably did NOT activate Jakorian Bennett from injured reserve, despite the fact that top backup cornerback Jonathan Jones has been ruled out of Sunday’s game. With the Eagles opening Bennett’s 21-day practice window to return from IR on October 14, the time to activate him is running out. In the meantime, Kelee Ringo and/or Mac McWilliams could see snaps on defense if the Eagles’ corner depth is tested. Interesting to see that the Eagles went with temporarily elevating Reiger instead of 2026 rookie Keyshawn James-Newby. KJN previously got the nod the last two weeks and has one elevation remaining. The Eagles are entering Sunday’s game with just three healthy off-ball linebackers: Zack Baun, Jeremiah Trotter Jr. (starting in place of an injured Jihaad Campbell), and Smael Mondon. The team did not opt to temporarily elevate Anfernee Orji from the practice squad to have a fourth player at this position.

summary: The eighth weekend of the 2026 NFL season is here! Let’s run through a Philadelphia Eagles-focused rooting guide for all of the Week 8 games. They have the second-longest odds (+1100 on FanDuel) […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Quinyon Mitchell #27 of the Philadelphia Eagles tackles Chig Okonkwo #85 of the Washington Commanders during the second quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The eighth weekend of the 2026 NFL season is here! Let’s run through a Philadelphia Eagles-focused rooting guide for all of the Week 8 games. EAGLES GAME PHILADELPHIA EAGLES at WASHINGTON COMMANDERS: The Eagles currently have a 3.7% chance of making the playoffs, according to FTN Fantasy . They have the second-longest odds (+1100 on FanDuel) among NFC teams to qualify for the postseason, only ahead of the Arizona Cardinals (+3500). With this in mind, I don’t think it’s unfair to be interested in the Eagles maximizing their positioning in the 2027 NFL Draft. At the same time, I don’t begrudge any Eagles fans who think that’s loser talk and want to see the team win until they’re officially eliminated (and perhaps even past that point). With a victory, the Eagles will be 3-5 with a chance to reach 4-5 ahead of their Week 10 bye. With a loss, the Eagles can potentially move as high as No. 2 overall in the draft order. Current 2027 NFL Draft order via Tankathon : Vote for your rooting interest in the poll below: NFC EAST ARIZONA CARDINALS at DALLAS COWBOYS: If you want the Eagles to stay alive in the division, you want to see the Cowboys lose. But even if you prefer the draft positioning angle, it’s good to see the Cardinals win to keep Arizona below Philly in the draft order. Root for the Cardinals. NFL DRAFT CONSIDERATIONS BALTIMORE RAVENS at BUFFALO BILLS: The Eagles own the Ravens’ fifth-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft via the Cam Jurgens trade. Might as well root for it to be as favorable as possible. Root for the Bills. TENNESSEE TITANS at CINCINNATI BENGALS: The Titans are ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. The Eagles need Tennessee to win to have a chance to move ahead of them. Root for the Titans. LAS VEGAS RAIDERS at NEW YORK JETS: The 2-5 Jets are currently a bigger threat than the 3-4 Raiders to move ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. Root for the Jets. CLEVELAND BROWNS at PITTSBURGH STEELERS: With both of these teams currently 5-2, they don’t appear to be threatening to move ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. But the angle here is that the Eagles don’t want to see the Ravens win the AFC North since Philly owns Baltimore’s fifth-round pick. With a win, the Browns will be 6-2 overall and 3-0 in division games, making it more difficult for the Ravens to catch up. Root for the Browns. ATLANTA FALCONS at TAMPA BAY BUCCANEERS: The 2-5 Bucs are currently a bigger threat than the 3-4 Falcons to move ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. Root for the Buccaneers. INDIANAPOLIS COLTS at JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS: The Colts are having a fire sale. Due to last year’s Sauce Gardner trade (lol), they don’t own their own first-round pick in this year’s draft. The Jets do. Indy’s continued losing threatens to put that owed pick to the Jets ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. Root for the Colts. LOS ANGELES CHARGERS at LOS ANGELES RAMS: Not sure if the Eagles can actually catch the winless Bolts in the draft order but you can root for it to happen. The Rams losing also helps the Eagles’ wild card chances, if you’re into that angle. Root for the Chargers. KANSAS CITY CHIEFS at DENVER BRONCOS: Of these two teams, the Broncos seem like the bigger threat to fall off and threaten the Eagles’ draft positioning. Root for the Broncos. NEW ENGLAND PATRIOTS at MIAMI DOLPHINS: The Eagles need the Dolphins to win some more to have a chance at moving ahead of them in the draft order. Also, the Eagles own the more favorable of either New England’s or Chicago’s 2027 fifth-round pick due to the A.J. Brown trade. Might as well root for the Pats to lose. Root for the Dolphins. CHICAGO BEARS at SEATTLE SEAHAWKS: Again, the Eagles own the more favorable of either New England’s or Chicago’s 2027 fifth-round pick due to the A.J. Brown trade. Root for the Seahawks. WHAT’S LEFT MINNESOTA VIKINGS at DETROIT LIONS: The Eagles’ chances of earning a wild card spot are very slim; FTN Fantasy puts those odds at 0.3%. But if you’re holding out hope for it to happen, you want to see the Lions lose since they’re closer to losing their grasp on postseason qualification. Root for the Vikings. The injury occurred during a team drill on a day that is considered a light practice. He’ll undergo more tests Saturday, but initial X-rays showed significant damage, a team source told ESPN. Depending on what the additional tests reveal, it’s possible Payne, who’s in the final year of his contract, will be done for the season. It’s yet another blow for the Commanders, who are 1-4-1 in a pivotal third season for coach Dan Quinn. Eagles at Commanders Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 8 enemy – BGN The Philadelphia Eagles are riding a five-game losing streak entering Sunday Night Football against the Washington Commanders, a team they beat in the season opener. Can the Birds win a game for the first time since September 20? In order to preview this Week 8 NFC East battle, I reached out to our enemies over at Hogs Haven. The amicable Andrew Y kindly kindly took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let’s take a look at the answers. NFC East Mixtape VOL. 202: Can Dallas build? | PHI/WAS | Giants Outlook – NFC East Mixtape It feels like the NFC East has been whittled down to two teams, and only one of them is playing this week in the Dallas Cowboys. Meanwhile… the Philadelphia Eagles and Washington Commanders are about to play one of the least exciting Sunday Night Football games we have ever seen. Who wants it more? Who wants it least? And while the New York Giants are off this week times are very exciting for them. Big Blue View’s Ed Valentine joins RJ Ochoa and Brandon Lee Gowton for an update on how things are going with the G-Men. You can see that we have a BRAND NEW NFC East Mixtape YouTube Channel so make sure to subscribe as the show will live here exclusively in video format. AND you can also listen to the show! On Blogging The Boys and/or Bleeding Green Nation podcast feeds as well as the SB Nation NFL Show feed! Washington Commanders vs Philadelphia Eagles Week 8: Five Questions with Bleeding Green Nation – Hogs Haven On defense, the Eagles are healthier, primarily dealing with injury to LB Jihaad Campbell, who has been ruled out of week 8. Despite their health, the Eagles defense has declined precipitously in 2026 to be the 5th-worst pass defense by yards allowed and the 6th-worst rush defense by yards allowed, as well as ranking poorly in advanced stats. One theory behind the defense’s decline is that they are getting beat up from being on the field all the time due to the collapse of the offense. Through Week 7, the Eagles defense has been on the field for 67.3 plays/game, 4th-most in the NFL. Certain players have had a harder time than others, with slot CB Cooper DeJean suffering from a high missed-tackle rate and notable drop in coverage quality. I asked Brandon Lee Gowton of Bleeding Green Nation five questions to better understand the state of the Eagles and what to look for in this game. Why the NFL didn’t flex the Eagles vs. Commanders out of ‘Sunday Night Football’ – SB Nation For 20 years, the NFL has made Sunday Night Football on NBC the marquee prime-time game of the weekend. Flexible scheduling was one of the selling points of SNF on NBC, with the league having the ability to swap out lackluster games for higher quality matchups. For several years, SNF has had its flex scheduling window opened in Week 5 instead of the back-end of the season. And yet, the 2-5 Philadelphia Eagles and 1-4-1 Washington Commanders were not flexed out this weekend, even though there are far more compelling and flex-worthy games on the Week 8 Sunday schedule. Is this just another case of NFC East bias? Well, it’s a little more complicated than that, and it’s largely the NFL’s own doing. Eagles-Commanders Preview: Will Saquon Barkley Tough It Out? SHOULD He? – PHLY Eagles Podcast Saquon Barkley returned the practice field just in time to put his status in play for the Eagles’ road matchup against the Washington Commanders on Sunday night. EJ Smith is joined by Deniz Selman and Brandon Lee Gowton to discuss whether the star running back should push through the hamstring and back injury he entered the week dealing with, whether Jeremiah Trotter Jr. should take over for Jihaad Campbell, and how this year’s team compares to previous lost Eagles seasons. As it stands now the Eagles would have the sixth pick in next year’s draft, and they’ve only drafted that high twice in the last 25 years, taking Lane Johnson fourth in 2013 and Carson Wentz second in 2016. Before that you go back to Corey Simon sixth in 2000 and Donovan McNabb second in 1999. Before that? Kenny Jackson fourth in 1984. So four top-6 picks in the last 42 years. What direction would Howie Roseman go if the Eagles draft that high? We can rule out receiver, running back, tight end, linebacker, corner or safety, which leaves trenches and quarterback. Edge or o-line never surprises you with Howie, but you don’t get many opportunities to draft top-10 quarterbacks, and if the Eagles are concerned with Jalen Hurts’ long-term health, and it’s something they won’t talk about, quarterback makes a lot of sense. You probably wouldn’t get Oklahoma State’s Drew Mestemaker at 6, but C.J. Carr of Notre Dame and Darian Mensah of Miami are in play if there is concern about Hurts being healthy enough to play in 2027 and beyond. Howie has drafted three quarterbacks in the first three rounds as a GM, and all three played a key role on a Super Bowl championship. Nick Foles and Jalen Hurts were Super Bowl MVPs and Carson Wentz went 11-2 before getting hurt in 2017. There is no No. 1 seed without him. It’s hard to imagine having to move on from a Super Bowl-MVP quarterback at 28 years old, but there are so many unknowns with his condition and treatment that it’s possible. Hurts’ contract status only complicates matters because with limited guarantees beyond this year it’s hard to imagine him playing for the Eagles in 2027 without a new or re-worked contract. summary: The Eagles are a mess. The Eagles sit in third place in the hapless NFC East, not that it is any great distinction, one […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Jayden Daniels #5 of the Washington Commanders carries the ball during a game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles are a mess. They are the unproud owners of a five-game losing skid, the longest losing streak in the NFC and currently the second-longest streak in the NFL behind the winless Los Angeles Chargers. The Eagles sit in third place in the hapless NFC East, not that it is any great distinction, one game up on their next opponent, the one-win Washington Commanders, this Sunday night on national TV. If you’re wondering how low the Eagles can go, they are 5.5-point underdogs against the one-win Commanders, who even with one victory hold a larger upside this season than the sinking, listless Eagles. The Eagles are currently ranked 31st in offense, averaging 264.9 yards a game, and 29th in scoring, averaging an NFC-low 18.1 points a game. Defensively, the Eagles are not much better, ranked No. 27 in the NFL, giving up an average of 371.3 yards a game, and 25 points a game. The Eagles are coming off their worst performance of the season, giving up a season-high 416 total yards that translated into a season-high 38 points in the 38-21 to the Dallas Cowboys on Monday night. One weapon the Commanders have that the Eagles do not have is Jayden Daniels, despite the fact that he is 0-7-1 in his last eight starts and will be without Eagle killer Terry McLaurin, out for the season after surgery on Friday to repair the torn patellar tendon in his left knee. Even without McLaurin, the Commanders will be the better team. Defensive tackles Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis were awful against Dallas. They were nowhere to be found. They had no quarterback pressures and were knocked off the ball the whole night. The Cowboys ran 65 plays and the vaunted Eagles’ defense had zero tackles for a loss. Carter, the highest paid defensive tackle in the NFL, ran from adversity and declined to talk to the media after the game and continued with his denial of putting out a maximum effort against Dallas this week leading into the Washington game. At least Eagles’ defensive coordinator Vic Fangio was accountable—as he should have been. When asked about a lack of effort, Fangio denied seeing any lack of effort, although he did say, “I didn’t do a good enough job coaching. We didn’t play the run, obviously, well enough. When you do that, it kind of affects everything. I didn’t have them ready to do that the way we need to. We just didn’t play it well.” Numerous sources in and around the Eagles have told Bleeding Green Nation recently that they still trust and believe in Nick Sirianni and Fangio. That the pair still have the locker room. They still somehow believe that Sirianni and Fangio can turn around this disaster, because they have done it before. That they still have faith the Eagles will be playing in vital November and December games. But where there was once unbending support for learning-on-the-job offensive coordinator Sean Mannion and offensive line coach Chris Kuper may be bending. It has changed to doubt as the Eagles keep sinking.

On Georgia loaded defense, I am most interested to see how Chris Cole goes to battle with the Florida run game. The Gators have a star back in Jadan Baugh and will really want to move the ball on the ground. Chris Cole is the next great Georgia linebacker and can put on a clinic in this game. Griffin Wilde, Wide Receiver, Northwestern v. Oregon (3:30 PM on Peacock): Okay so hear me out… Griffin Wilde is a 6’2” senior pass catcher for Northwestern who has 38% of their receiving yards this season. To put that into perspective, all-world freshman Jesse Legree has 39% of his team’s passing yards this season. Wilde is a big, reliable, athletic target in the Wildcat passing game. While Oregon is down on their luck this season, they will still be a tough match for Chip Kelly’s offense. Wilde will likely be seeing the ball quite a bit. Ahmad Hardy, Running Back, Missouri v. Arkansas (7:45 PM on SECN): Ahmad Hardy was one of the best players in all of college football last year. After starring as a freshman at ULM, Hardy transferred to Missouri and was immediately a game changing running back. He rushed for over 1,600 yards and scored 16 times on the ground. In the spring, Hardy suffered a gunshot wound that has held him out of playing until this week. While Hardy is expected to get limited touches, I am curious to see how he looks. College football is better with Ahmad Hardy healthy, so here’s hoping he feels good and can get back on track to having a great career.

full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s safe to say that DK Metcalf’s first season in a Pittsburgh Steelers uniform was far from a success. The receiver posted just 850 yards after being suspended for the team’s final two regular-season games, and struggled to find consistency with quarterback Aaron Rodgers all season. Many believed the additions of Michael Pittman Jr. and rookie Germie Bernard, coupled with the continued development of Roman Wilson, would alleviate some of the pressure and focus put on Metcalf by opposing defenses. However, it has been a modest at best start to the season for the receiver, as he has posted just 374 yards through the team’s first seven games. Appearing on ESPN’s NFL Live, former Steelers wide receiver Adam Thielen addressed why he believes the connection between Rodgers and Metcalf still has yet to hit its full stride. “What Aaron likes is he likes to have guys just line up and play football,” Thielen said. “We’re not going to move him around. We’re not going to put him in the slot. We’re not going to motion him. We just want to line up and go win.DK is not that guy. He’s not a guy you just put out there at the X, and it’s third and five, and you go win, right? And you’re seeing that on the tape. You’re seeing that it’s he’s looking for him. He wants him, but he’s not open. And that’s okay. Some guys just aren’t that guy. You got to be able to move them around. You got to be able to put them in stacks. You got to be able to motion them. But he’s not that guy right now in this offense.” Thielen appeared in five games for the Steelers last season, recording 11 receptions for 117 yards. Coming from someone who played with the duo last season, this observation holds more weight than your normal sports talking head. The receiver struggled with drops early in the season, but has found some consistency by going over 90 receiving yards in two of his last four games. Something still feels off with the connection between the Steelers quarterback and their top wideout. One former receiver believes it’s due to Metcalf’s lack of versatility overall. Metcalf’s only game of over 100 yards this season happened to come against Cleveland. Metcalf and Rodgers will have to be in sync to help the Steelers win this game and earn sole possession of first place in the AFC North, but it may not be that simple. summary: Pittsburgh Steelers edge rusher Alex Highsmith is garnering trade interest from several NFL teams, Tom Pelissero of The Ringer. “Other teams have inquired about trading for Highsmith since last year, and the Steelers’ answer has always been no,” Pelissero writes, via Noah Strackbein of Sports Illustrated. “But they currently have a logjam at edge rusher, with […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Pittsburgh Steelers edge rusher Alex Highsmith is garnering trade interest from several NFL teams, Tom Pelissero of The Ringer. “Other teams have inquired about trading for Highsmith since last year, and the Steelers’ answer has always been no,” Pelissero writes, via Noah Strackbein of Sports Illustrated. “But they currently have a logjam at edge rusher, with T.J. Watt turning back the clock with a stellar performance this season at age 32, while younger players Nick Herbig and Jackn Sawyer have part-time roles. Highsmith is still in his prime at age 29 and figures to be the subject of more calls leading up to the deadline.” The Steelers extended Nick Herbig in the offseason on a $100 million deal, which makes it all but certain he will take one of the starting edge roles in 2027. In doing so, one of Highsmith or T.J. Watt will have to be gone. Considering Highsmith will be in the final year of his deal in 2027 and has no guaranteed money remaining on his deal, he becomes a prime trade candidate next offseason. However, with the Steelers trying to make one more run with Aaron Rodgers, trading Highsmith during the season seems highly unlikely – next March is a different story. title: NFL predictions: Steelers will ride offense to win over Browns
summary: The one game standing between the 5-2 Pittsburgh Steelers and their bye week is their most consequential yet, as they are set to take on the 5-2 Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh. When the ball is kicked, it will be exactly a month to the day since Cleveland took the first game between […]
full_text: (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The one game standing between the 5-2 Pittsburgh Steelers and their bye week is their most consequential yet, as they are set to take on the 5-2 Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh. When the ball is kicked, it will be exactly a month to the day since Cleveland took the first game between the teams on Thursday Night Football. However, the Steelers have rattled off three straight wins since then. The winner of this game will be in sole possession of first place in the AFC North heading into the second half of the regular season. With both teams coming off wins and identical records, FanDuel Sportsbook gives the Pittsburgh Steelers the slight edge as a 3.5-point favorite over Cleveland. This is as close to a “must-win” game in the middle of the season for the Steelers as we will ever see. With all of that being said, here are some predictions based around my favorite prop bets of the weekend. Germie Bernard over 43.5 receiving yards This number is ridiculously low because the rookie receiver will be one of, if not the most targeted pass catchers on the entire team on Sunday. Last time these two teams met, Bernard got barely any playing time, but that gives him the chance to take advantage of a group that hasn’t seen what he can do yet. In their first matchup, Pittsburgh had two receivers go over this total. I’m not letting last game scare me, as the Steelers controlled the clock running the football, leading to limited opportunities for any receiver. It would be a shock to see no receiver have more than three catches for the second week in a row. Bernard is a volume receiver that the Steelers will need to rely on to get open and break some tackles against their tough man defense. Rico Dowdle gets over 70 scrimmage yards Ever since running back Rico Dowdle has returned to the lineup from his toe injury, he has looked significantly more efficient with the ball in his hands. Sure, the improved offensive line helps, but Dowdle is going to continue to earn more runs in the offense with his numbers improving. Last week, the veteran back averaged a season-high 4.6 yards per carry. Dowdle also hauled in six passes, good for the most on the team, for 45 yards. It was a more even share of the opportunities for the Steelers running backs, as Dowdle had 16 touches compared to Jaylen Warren’s 21. Dowdle is the change of pace back in the Steelers offense, but is one that they will continue to use quite a bit as he gets healthier. Warren’s breakout doesn’t mean that Dowdle won’t be involved in the offense. In fact, I think what we saw against New Orleans is what we can expect from Dowdle for the rest of the season. With the browns struggles to defend the run, both backs could be in for a big day on Sunday. Darnell Washington continues dominance with a touchdown The Steelers’ six-foot-seven tight end has already set career highs in total touchdowns this season. His increased usage in the red zone is something Steelers fans have been begging to see for years now. Last week, Washington dunked on Saints defensive back Kool-Aid McKinstry as he snatched the ball out of the air from four yards out for the Steelers’ only touchdown in Paris. The tight end has caught a touchdown pass in two consecutive games, and I have a hard time seeing that trend stopping against Cleveland given his continued usage in the red zone. Washington also scored against the Browns in their first matchup a month ago. It almost makes too much sense to see Washington in the end zone again on Sunday. title: Steelers keys to victory vs. Browns
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are looking to even their season series with the Cleveland Browns on Sunday. Pittsburgh hasn’t been swept by the Browns since 1988, and the winner will hold sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Here are this week’s keys to victory. Dominate the short passing game The Steelers faced similar […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are looking to even their season series with the Cleveland Browns on Sunday. Pittsburgh hasn’t been swept by the Browns since 1988, and the winner will hold sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Here are this week’s keys to victory. Dominate the short passing game The Steelers faced similar coverage against the Saints that Cleveland will deploy. Entering Week 7, the Saints were No. 2 in single-high defensive looks, trailing only the Browns. Aaron Rodgers was, statistically, the worst quarterback in football against single-high looks this season. However, Rodgers and the Steelers found success against the Saints, finishing 21-of-24 for 178 yards while facing single-high looks. While throwing short passes (0-9 yards downfield) Rodgers went 11-of-14 for 107 yards and finished ninth among all quarterbacks overall when facing single-high looks. The Browns are going to look to pressure Rodgers like they did in the first matchup. If Pittsburgh is able to have a high success rate in the quick and short passing game, Cleveland will have to unpin its ears, which will open up everything else. On the other side, the Steelers’ defense has to be able to stop that very same attack by the Browns. Deshaun Watson had 27 short passing attempts in Week 7 and led all quarterbacks with 255 yards on those attempts. For reference, Tyler Shough had the most short pass attempts last week against Pittsburgh with 33, and the Saints were able to consistently convert on third down. The Steelers can’t allow Watson to dink-and-dunk on their defense all afternoon. Continue to stop the run The Steelers haven’t allowed a running back to top 50 yards since facing the Browns in Week 4. From Weeks 4-7, Cleveland ranks ninth in the NFL in yards per carry, and their six rushing scores are tied for second in the league. The Steelers have been the league’s best rush defense over the last three weeks. If they hone in on Quinshon Judkins and make Deshaun Watson beat them, their odds of winning will increase exponentially. Deploy heavy Cover Three looks The Steelers’ defense has the second-best total EPA against the pass in the league while in Cover Three. To compare, the Browns’ offense is 25th in EPA per play while facing Cover Three. Show looks the Browns struggle against, take away the run, and make Watson beat you with his arm. If the Steelers can do that, they should go into their bye week 6-2. Let us know what you think in the comments . summary: First place in the AFC North is up for grabs as the Pittsburgh Steelers host the Cleveland Browns. full_text: (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images First place in the AFC North is up for grabs as the Pittsburgh Steelers host the Cleveland Browns. Both teams enter the day at 5-2, with Cleveland holding a 1-0 head-to-head advantage over Pittsburgh. Will they beat the Steelers on the road in a regular season game for the first time since 2003? Our staff weighs in. Mike Nicastro : The Steelers haven’t lost to the Browns twice in a season in almost three decades, but this year presents a unique challenge. Teams traveling internationally over the last two seasons are just 1-7 when returning to face a team that did not travel overseas the prior week. That one win was the Broncos last season, when they scored 33 4th quarter points against the Giants to win by 1 point. Fatigue will play a factor, but having home field will help significantly. This is still a Browns team that lost to the Jets on the road, and just went to the wire with the Titans. Won’t be surprised if its ugly, but Pittsburgh rides the run game again into their bye. Steelers 20 Browns 17. Jason Aponte: This will be a dogfight between the division rivals. The Steelers have shown improvement offensively lately and will need to beat Cleveland’s plan of man coverage. Rodgers and the offense does enough and the defense holds up to give Pittsburgh the division lead. Steelers 21, Browns 17. Ryan Parish : The Steelers were the better team in 3 out of 4 quarters the last time these teams met a few weeks ago. Both teams have found a groove since, and they enter the contest at 5-2. Winner leaves the game atop the AFC North. I’ve had a running bit in these predictions that will not change until it stops working. Browns 24-Steelers 23. Austin Bechtold: The Steelers haven’t lost to the Browns at home in the regular season since I was two. I can’t fathom it happening with how the Steelers defense is playing right now. I’ve been wrong about Patrick Graham and doubted his scheme to a degree early in the season, but if he calls a great gameplan Sunday I’m sold. Aaron Rodgers is playing his best football since 2021. The Browns aren’t the old Browns and I think are better than people are giving credit for. The Steelers do what it takes, and will be in sole possession of first place in the AFC North on Sunday. Steelers 24-18. Ryland Bickley : This is a series that has been defined by home teams winning as of late, and with the Steelers on a hot streak and playing in Acrisure this Sunday, I don’t expect that to change. Cleveland’s man coverage scheme should once again prove a challenge for the Pittsburgh offense, but the Steelers defense has taken some strides since the last matchup. Steelers 27, Browns 20 . Joey Bray : When these teams take the field on Sunday, the Pittsburgh Steelers will be exactly one month removed from suffering another loss to the Browns in Cleveland on Thursday Night Football. Since that game, the Steelers have won three straight. I can’t say for certain how much the team has grown since then, as they still have concerns in the secondary on defense and struggles in the red zone as an offense. Unlike last time where the browns jumped out to a big lead early, I think this game will be a close one throughout. The Browns are a much better football team that anyone anticipated entering the season. Todd Monken deserves a ton of credit for the way he has continued to put Deshaun Watson and the offense in positions to win. However, all five of their wins have come on game winning drives, a trend that is unlikely to continue. I’ll take Pittsburgh to get their revenge on Cleveland and go into the bye week with sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Steelers 21, Browns 20 . Jarrett Bailey: I said ahead of the Saints game that I don’t know if the Steelers are a team I’d bank on winning four games in a row, yet here we are after a three-game win streak. The whole “Cleveland hasn’t won in Pittsburgh since 2003” doesn’t necessarily mean much to me in terms of results. Although it does seem to matter when these two teams play in Cleveland that the Steelers turn into the worst versions of themselves. I do think the Steelers win, but I’m not going to take this Browns team lightly. Steelers 20, Browns 16. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Seahawks Uchenna Nwosu fined for horse-collar tackle on Patrick Mahomes
summary: The Seattle Seahawks played their most complete game of the season last Sunday, routing the Kansas City Chiefs 20-3 behind efficient offense and a masterful defensive performance. They did not, however, come away unscathed in the NFL’s fine book. Unsurprisingly, edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu was docked some money after he was penalized for a horse-collar […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks played their most complete game of the season last Sunday, routing the Kansas City Chiefs 20-3 behind efficient offense and a masterful defensive performance. They did not, however, come away unscathed in the NFL’s fine book. Unsurprisingly, edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu was docked some money after he was penalized for a horse-collar tackle on Patrick Mahomes. Nwosu was held on the same play, so there were offsetting penalties called and a replayed down. On the next snap, Derick Hall had a crunching strip-sack on the Chiefs quarterback, but neither Nwosu nor Jarran Reed could recover the loose ball, and Mahomes somehow recovered his own fumble to preserve Kansas City’s eventual field goal. Rumor has it that Mike Tirico is still saying, “STILL OUT!” to this day. Seahawks edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu was fined $17,911 for his horse-collar tackle of Patrick Mahomes. It was the only fine on either team. pic.twitter.com/fWWiJaTxVg — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) October 31, 2026 Horse-collar tackles are among the offenses that the NFL has deemed suspension worthy for repeat offenders. If Nwosu commits two more horse-collar penalties this year, he will serve an automatic one-game ban. No other Seahawks were fined. The immediate greater worry for Nwosu is his availability for Monday night against the Chicago Bears, as he’s listed as doubtful for the game.

title: Seahawks vs. Bears game preview: Another big primetime showdown at Lumen Field
summary: Mike Macdonald’s defense has just completed an impressive two-week stretch. First, the Seattle Seahawks held Sean Payton’s Denver Broncos to 17 points. Then, one week later, it limited Andy Reid’s Kansas City Chiefs to just three. Those are two of the most accomplished offensive minds in the NFL, and the Seahawks found ways to disrupt […]
full_text: Mike Macdonald’s defense has just completed an impressive two-week stretch. First, the Seattle Seahawks held Sean Payton’s Denver Broncos to 17 points. Then, one week later, it limited Andy Reid’s Kansas City Chiefs to just three. Those are two of the most accomplished offensive minds in the NFL, and the Seahawks found ways to disrupt both systems. Now comes a different kind of challenge. The Chicago Bears arrive in Seattle with a 5–2 record and an offense led by Ben Johnson, one of the most promising young offensive minds in football. Johnson does not have the résumé of Reid or Payton yet, but he has already shown the creativity and adaptability that make him one of the most intriguing play-callers of his generation. That is what makes this matchup so compelling. Macdonald has just gone through two consecutive tests against established offensive masterminds. Now he gets a chance to measure his defense against a younger coach who is building something of his own in Chicago. Johnson’s offense uses motion, formation variation, play-action and a balanced rushing attack to create favorable matchups. Macdonald’s defense is built to disguise its intentions, change the picture after the snap and make quarterbacks hesitate. It is a clash between a defensive mind who has found answers against two elite offensive coaches and an emerging play-caller who wants to make Seattle solve a different set of problems. Keeping Caleb Williams in the pocket The first priority for Seattle is clear: keep Caleb Williams inside the pocket. It has been one of the defining strengths of Macdonald’s defense. Seattle has done a good job keeping quarterbacks such as Brock Purdy and Bo Nix from turning pressure into extended plays. The defensive line has maintained its rush lanes, while the coverage has forced quarterbacks to work through their progressions instead of relying on improvisation. The results have been impressive. The Seahawks held Patrick Mahomes to only 165 passing yards. Against the Chiefs, Seattle compressed the pocket, disrupted the timing of the passing game and prevented Kansas City from finding its usual rhythm. Still, the performance against Mahomes also offered a few reminders that Seattle is not flawless. There were moments when the rush lost some of its discipline and the quarterback had opportunities to move outside the structure of the play. Mahomes was unable to turn those moments into consistent production, but a more balanced and healthier Chicago offense could be better equipped to exploit them. Williams presents a different challenge. He has the athleticism to escape pressure, extend plays and give his receivers extra time to uncover. He has also shown that he can attack downfield when the protection holds. Johnson can make that even more dangerous by designing plays that move the launch point through bootlegs and play-action, giving Williams simpler reads while forcing the defense to account for his mobility. Seattle cannot become so aggressive in its pursuit that it opens escape lanes. The edge defenders must maintain their leverage, the interior rush needs to compress the pocket without losing control, and the linebackers must be ready to react when Williams leaves the original launch point. The goal is not necessarily to sack him on every passing down. It is to make him play quarterback from the pocket, where Seattle can use its coverage structure and pass rush together. If Williams is allowed to turn broken plays into second chances, Chicago has the weapons to make those opportunities hurt. Defending the tight ends The tight end matchup could be one of the most important parts of the game, particularly because Seattle has shown some vulnerability in this area. Ernest Jones has had difficult moments when asked to handle tight ends one-on-one. That is a matchup Chicago can look to exploit with Colston Loveland, who has become a meaningful part of the Bears’ passing offense. Loveland has 26 receptions for 244 yards and two touchdowns through seven games, and he gives Williams a reliable option between the numbers. The Seahawks just faced a reminder of how tight ends can become a quarterback’s most dependable answers against their defense. Against Kansas City, Travis Kelce and Noah Gray were the Chiefs’ most productive receiving targets. Both finished with 44 yards, but the difference in how they got there is worth noting: Kelce needed eight targets to reach that total, while Gray caught all three of his targets. No Kansas City wide receiver finished with more than 18 receiving yards. That should get Seattle’s attention. The defense did an excellent job limiting the Chiefs’ outside receivers, but the tight ends still found ways to make plays in the middle of the field. Chicago can try to reproduce that approach with Loveland, especially if the Bears can create favorable matchups against the linebackers. This is where Jones and the rest of Seattle’s second level will have to be disciplined. If the linebackers step too aggressively toward the line of scrimmage to help against the run, Loveland can work behind them. If they sit too deep to protect the passing lanes, Chicago can use the space underneath and make the defense tackle. Johnson can also use formations and motion to make the defense declare its coverage responsibilities. Loveland can line up attached to the offensive line, split out wide or move into the slot. Those changes can create mismatches and force Seattle to adjust its personnel and communication before the snap. Seattle needs to avoid giving Williams easy answers. The linebackers must understand their leverage, the safeties need to recognize when Loveland is entering the seam, and the defensive line must prevent the quarterback from having all day to wait for the route to develop. The ground game: patience on both sides Chicago’s rushing attack is another major concern. The Bears have a productive combination in D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai, although Monangai has just been ruled out for Monday. Swift has 476 yards on 116 carries, averaging 4.1 yards per attempt, with seven touchdowns. Monangai has added 324 yards on 60 carries, averaging 5.4 yards, with three scores. The combination gives Johnson two backs with different usage profiles and allows Chicago to keep its ground game involved throughout the game. The Bears do not need to break off a huge run early to make their rushing attack effective. They can work through four- and five-yard gains, stay ahead of the chains and gradually force the defense to respect the run. That is particularly important against a defense like Seattle’s, which wants to dictate passing situations and unleash its pass rush. The Seahawks need to win the line of scrimmage without allowing the Bears to dictate the tempo. The defensive front must stay disciplined with its gaps, while the linebackers need to read their keys and avoid getting caught between the run and the passing game. Williams’ mobility adds another element, since the quarterback can become part of the rushing threat when the defense overcommits to the running back. On the other side of the ball, Seattle should have a similar commitment to patience. The Seahawks cannot abandon the run just because the first few carries do not produce explosive gains. The objective should be to keep moving the chains, even if the progress comes in small increments. Two or three yards on an early-down carry are not necessarily a failure if the offense avoids negative plays and stays in manageable situations. That approach was visible against Kansas City. Emanuel Wilson finished with 100 yards on 24 attempts, and his production became particularly important late in the game. Wilson generated more than 50 yards across Seattle’s final three drives, helping the offense keep moving and close out the win. That is the kind of patience Seattle needs again. The Seahawks should not feel compelled to force a big play on every possession. Keep handing the ball off,…

title: NFL predictions: 4 game picks for critical Bears-Seahawks matchup
summary: Monday Night Football brings the Chicago Bears to Seattle for a Week 8 matchup, featuring two new shiny trade acquisitions; Quenton Nelson for the Seahawks, and Jeffery Simmons for the Bears. If you’re looking for player props and game-day value, check out the latest lines at FanDuel Sportsbook before kickoff. The Seattle Seahawks are coming […]
full_text: Monday Night Football brings the Chicago Bears to Seattle for a Week 8 matchup, featuring two new shiny trade acquisitions; Quenton Nelson for the Seahawks, and Jeffery Simmons for the Bears. If you’re looking for player props and game-day value, check out the latest lines at FanDuel Sportsbook before kickoff. The Seattle Seahawks are coming off of a huge momentum swing this past week. After losing two straight, the Seahawks dismantled the Chiefs and pulled off a huge trade for a future Hall of Hame offensive guard, Quenton Nelson . The Bears are feeling good about themselves too after a big win over the New England Patriots last week, and now with Jeffery Simmons leading the defensive line room . Let’s look at some game picks ahead of this matchup Sunday Night. Over/Under 46.5 (-110) Whenever Ben Johnson is involved in a game, many people assume that there will be lots of points scored. That is a fair assumption to make as Johnson is an offensive mastermind, even against Mike Macdonald and the Seahawks. Just look at the last time Johnson played Mike Macdonald and the Seahawks: Week 4 of 2024 when he put up 42 points against them. That alone would nearly hit the over on this upcoming week’s money line. However, that 2024 matchup also did not have many of the key defensive pieces that Macdonald and the Seahawks will be deploying this week against the Bears (DeMarcus Lawrence, Leonard Williams, Byron Murphy II, Nick Emmanwori, Ernest Jones, the list can go on.) This is all to say, do not assume Johnson will be able to put up points as easily as he did last time he played against Mike Macdonald’s defense. The other thing to consider with this money line is the amount of possessions each time will have. Both offenses love running the ball. The Bears are the number one team in rush attempts per game in 2026 , averaging over 35 carries a game. The Seahawks are not far behind at fifth most in the league, averaging over 29 carries a game. Seattle now has a new toy to play with in Quenton Nelson. Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet will potentially be making their returns to the field as well. All of this points to two offenses running the ball a lot and churning a lot of clock. This will likely lead to limited possessions by each team, and less opportunities to score. All of this being said, expect a lower scoring game. The pick: Under 46.5 total points (-110) . Jaxon Smith-Njigba over 150 receiving yards (+390) It cannot be a FanDuel Predictions article without talking about Jaxon Smith-Njigba, arguably the favorite for offensive player of the year. Smith-Njigba continued his heater of a 2026 campaign last week against the Kansas City Chiefs, putting up nine receptions, 150 yards, and one touchdown. He has 58 receptions, 867 yards, and 8 touchdowns on the season already. That is an average of 123.9 yards per game. There is no question that Smith-Njigba will have another big game, the question is, how big can it be? The Bears have given up an average of 225.9 passing yards per game this season. That is good for 18th best in the league . That is right around where the Chiefs are, who rank 17th best in the league. You saw what Smith-Njigba did to the Chiefs last week, perhaps he could pull off the same feat this upcoming week. However, one more wrinkle to add to this; Bears starting cornerback Malik Muhammad II has been limited in practice this week. If he can’t suit up, then there is a real chance Smith-Njigba is lining up against a backup cornerback for the Bears. All of this lines up to lean towards another Smith-Njigba huge game. The pick: Smith Njigba over 150 receiving yards (+390). Sam Darnold over 20 rushing yards (+630) A friskier bet will be taking the over on Sam Darnold rushing yards. Between the two quarterbacks in this matchup, Darnold is clearly not the more mobile quarterback. However, last week Darnold carried the ball two times for 17 yards , both times converting for a first down. This willingness to use his feet was a big difference between the Seahawks ability to move the ball on offense against the Chiefs compared to the prior weeks. Because of this, expect Darnold to look for opportunities to use his feet once again. On top of this, with the acquisition of Quenton Nelson, along with the potential returns of Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price, the Seahawks run game may be able to take a big leap this week against the Bears. If the run game can continue to ascend, that will open the playbook for a lot more play actions and bootlegs; all concepts ripe for a running back to move out of the pocket and use his legs. 20 yards is not much for a quarterback to get – Darnold could easily get this all in one play. The pick: Sam Darnold over 20 rushing yards (+630) . First touchdown scorer: Zach Charbonnet (+500) Last week I predicted that Zach Charbonnet will score two or more touchdowns . As he didn’t play ( thanks for the heads up, Ian Rapoport ), that clearly did not happen. However, with one more week of practice under his belt, this may be the week it finally does happen. If Charbonnet does play, him finding the end zone is a good bet. Charbonnet, when healthy, becomes the Seahawks clear number one running back, and strongest between the tackle runner. With Seattle’s struggles in the redzone, expect Charbonnet to get most of his touches when close to the goal line. title: 5Qs, 5As: Strength vs strength as Seahawks defense gets set to test Bears offense
summary: It’s Halloween weekend, but for fans of the Seattle Seahawks it’s a Sunday they get to spend without the stresses of “enjoying” a Seahawks game, as Mike Macdonald and his crew will take to the field against the Chicago Bears on Monday Night Football. Fresh off a dominant primetime win over Andy Reid and the […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - DECEMBER 26: Leonard Williams #99 of the Seattle Seahawks sacks Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears during the second quarter at Soldier Field on December 26, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Quinn Harris/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s Halloween weekend, but for fans of the Seattle Seahawks it’s a Sunday they get to spend without the stresses of “enjoying” a Seahawks game, as Mike Macdonald and his crew will take to the field against the Chicago Bears on Monday Night Football. Fresh off a dominant primetime win over Andy Reid and the Kansas City Chiefs, Seattle will be looking for an encore performance against another playoff contender led by one of the top offensive minds in the league in Ben Johnson. It will be the first time Macdonald and Johnson have gone head to head since the Detroit Lions thumped the Seahawks 42-29 on the back of a day that saw Jared Goff go 18-18 for 292 yards and a pair of touchdowns while also adding a seven yard touchdown reception from Amon-Ra St. Brown. In any case, it should be a fantastic primetime showdown, and nobody clicked to read a bunch of fluff at the top of the post. Thus, without wasting any time, here are the questions posed to Bill Zimmerman of Windy City Gridiron, along with the answers provided. 1. So many offensive coaches break into the NFL with a splash, but then fizzle over time. Ben Johnson, in contrast, has remained one of the best playcallers in the NFL over the past four and a half seasons and has the Bears poised to compete in a tough NFC North. What has allowed his continued success, while so many other former hot name offensive coordinators, like Bobby Slowik and Mike McDaniel, have seen their success fade over the past couple of years? Well, it helps that Ben Johnson is a psycho, and I mean that in the most complimentary way. He has a drive to be the best and to win like very few others I’ve seen pass through Chicago (probably since Mike Ditka). He’s also constantly looking to evolve his offense every season. Whether it be his run-blocking schemes, his passing concepts, and everything in between, he doesn’t run Sean McVay’s offense or Kyle Shanahan’s offense; he takes aspects of great offenses and tries to merge them into Ben Johnson’s offense. Ben has an understanding that what worked in 2025 may not work in 2026 as defensive coordinators adjust. Heck, he understands that what works in week 1 of 2026 may not work in week 10 of 2026. He’s a very smart guy, and he uses that to keep defenses on their toes. I think what makes Ben a tick above just about everyone else is he’s truly a brilliant playcaller. He’s playing chess every Sunday. He uses plays that he runs throughout the first half and early in the second half to get tendencies and open up plays for big gains in the fourth quarter. That was a big part of the late-game success last year. Yes, Caleb Williams had some magician moments, but those plays worked thanks to some Rembrandt-like work from Ben Johnson all game long, setting those up. Ben has worked his way into the McVay/Shanahan realm of offensive minds and we are confident he’s going to stay on that level. 2. For the second time in recent history the Bears have swung big in adding an All-Pro to the defensive front. What changes with the addition of Jeffery Simmons, and how much does this move change the Chicago defense? It’s not too often a team can add an actual game wrecker in arguably their biggest need midseason, but that’s what the Bears pulled off here. I can’t overstate how big this is for the Chicago defense. I know I sound like a homer right now, but let me not for a second, prior to this trade, I had the stance that this Bears team could never reach or win a Super Bowl because their defensive line was too deficient. You guys know this in Seattle: if you are going to beat great QBs, you need to get pressure with four. The Bears simply could not do that. Dennis Allen was a wizard with his pressure packages, but that’s always a bit of smoke and mirrors. Sure, it works in the regular season against Michael Penix, but that’s not what you want to do in the playoffs against Matthew Stafford or Josh Allen. Simmons isn’t just a great player. He’s a multiplier. He’s going to make the rest of the DL around him better because of the attention he will draw. He will still make several impact plays a game despite that attention. And because he elevates the entire DL, the DL will elevate the back seven. The Khalil Mack trade was awesome (that you were referring to in the question), but that didn’t work out as well because Ryan Pace bet that Mitch Trubisky was the guy, and well, he wasn’t. This time, there is far more confidence in Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams than Trubisky and Matt Nagy. 3. Most Seattle fans are familiar with the big names on the Bears roster, but who is a player on each side of the ball whose name fans may not recognize, but could have an outsized impact on the outcome of the game? This is always a fun question but a tough one to answer from the Bears on the offensive side of the ball because they don’t have a lot of under-the-radar players. I think most NFL fans are well aware of who Caleb Williams, Colston Loveland, Luther Burden, Rome Odunze, and D’Andre Swift are. I’d love to give you Sam Roush, the Bears rookie who is going to get more snaps with Cole Kmet injured, but Roush has had a lot of rough moments as a rookie. The best one is Kalif Raymond. Raymond was with Ben Johnson in Detroit and is one of those Swiss Army Knife-type wide receivers that can do a lot of different things. He runs clean routes, is a great blocker, knows where he is supposed to be on the field at all times, and if he gets the chance to move with the ball in space, he does have some speed. Raymond hasn’t been involved in the offense as much the last few weeks, but he was quite important the first 3 or 4 games of the season. It would not surprise me if he saw an uptick in targets this Monday against Seattle’s defense. On the defensive side of the ball, I’m going to give you the edge opposite Montez Sweat, Austin Booker. Booker was a 5th-round pick for the Bears in 2024 and had 6 sacks combined in his first two seasons. This year through 7 games, he already has 4 sacks, 5 TFLs (tying his career high already), and 2 forced fumbles. He’s playing solid football on a unit that desperately needed someone to step up. Now with Simmons in the mix, he should see even less attention and could have a chance to make a splash play or two. 4. Mike Macdonald’s defenses have been particularly troublesome for younger, less experienced quarterbacks. How has Caleb Williams looked so far in 2026, and what should Seahawks fans expect from the young signal caller as he faces off against a defensive group that just got done shutting down Patrick Mahomes? I would never suggest that Caleb Williams is going to cook a Mike Macdonald defense, because it’s an awesome defense and it gives plenty of QBs trouble. But I don’t think Caleb Williams should be considered a less-experienced QB at this point. Caleb has started over 40 games at this point and has 25 starts in Ben Johnson’s scheme. He’s grown a lot this year as a QB. Caleb will always be a QB who wants to take a shot down the field because he trusts his arm and his playmaking ability, but he has definitely learned to take the easy yards when they are there, and we’ve seen a big change. Last year, every Williams critic wanted to complain about his completion percentage. Well, this year, Caleb is sitting at 71%, good for 2 nd in the NFL behind Joe Burrow. He rarely turns the ball over as well. If I’m Seattle, I think you get Caleb Williams moving as much as possible and see how much he trusts his hamstring at this point. He’s had a nice break from Thursday Night Football, and the hamstring should be okay, but we haven’t seen him run since he returned from injury. He has 21 rushing yards in the last two games after having 107 in his…

title: Seahawks Reacts Survey results: Fans confident Seattle comes out on top over Bears
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Each week we ask questions of the most plugged-in Seattle Seahawks fans and fans across the country. Coming off a dominant 20-3 victory over the previously undefeated Kansas City Chiefs—where both the offense as well as the defense appeared to be near the […]
full_text: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Each week we ask questions of the most plugged-in Seattle Seahawks fans and fans across the country. Coming off a dominant 20-3 victory over the previously undefeated Kansas City Chiefs—where both the offense as well as the defense appeared to be near the top of their game, the Seattle Seahawks are within two games of taking over first place in the NFC West. With the division leader San Francisco 49ers on a bye week, they have a chance to inch one step closer. But, it won’t come easy when they host the high-powered Chicago Bears, who have won four of their last five games. Despite another tough matchup, there remains a high level of confidence Seattle can deliver a second consecutive win. While fans are seemingly certain the Seahawks will collect another primetime win (94% of votes), the margin of victory has conflicting opinions. In a tight poll, the majority believes Seattle will produce a convincing victory by a 9-16 point margin, with 46% of votes trending in that direction. However, 42% of voters think they’ll still come out on top, but by less than a possession. In addition, six percent of participants view a Seahawks victory by two or more possessions, whereas five percent believe the Bears will haul out a close win and one percent pessimistically think Chicago will prevail by 9+ points. Given the recent success of Chicago and quarterback Caleb Williams, a Seahawks victory by more than one possession appears to be wishful thinking, but it’d be foolish to rule it out after their defense—nicknamed the ‘Dark Side’ sacked Patrick Mahomes once, picked him off and forced a fumble while holding one of the NFL’s most prolific offenses to just three points last week. As an added bonus, they held superstar running back Kenneth Walker III to just 36 yards on the ground and spoiled his return to Seattle. It’s also worth noting quarterback Sam Darnold had arguably his best game of the season and although it may not have looked that way on paper, his confidence, composure and ability to find open receivers was a noticeable step up compared to where it was just a week before against the Denver Broncos. On top of the Seahawks issues running the ball, Chicago’s allowing the third least amount of rushing yards per game (87.6), meaning Darnold is poised to be heavily relied upon to deliver through the air. With wide receiver Rashid Shaheed’s (knee) status in question after he failed to participate in either of the team’s first two practices of the week, Seattle’s receiving core appears likely to be shorthanded on Monday night. Luckily for Seattle’s signal caller, general manager John Schneider acquired eight-time Pro Bowler Quenton Nelson—one of the league’s best guards on Tuesday to significantly boost their offensive line, one who’s allowed 16 sacks through seven games. As for Nelson, he’s only allowed one quarterback hit this year. While he’s a significant upgrade over Anthony Bradford, Nelson and the rest of Seattle’s offensive line will be faced with stopping an impactful defensive line who just added All-Pro tackle Jeffrey Simmons via a trade with the Tennessee Titans. Although they’re set to receive an addition in the trenches, the Seahawks pass could be in trouble if Shaheed is ultimately ruled out. Chicago ranks third in offensive yards per game (390.7), with playmakers all over the field. Williams and emerging star wideout Luther Burden III have connected on all targets so far this season, and Rome Odunze as well as Colston Loveland also profile as dangerous receiving option. As for their ground attack, running back D’Andre Swift has been consistent, having totalled 476 yards and seven touchdowns. He’ll likely command the backfield once again with fellow back Kyle Monangai (toe, thumb) having logged two consecutive missed practices to open the week. Williams has also proven to be a rushing threat, but hasn’t eclipsed 20+ yards since returning from a hamstring injury that sidelined him from Weeks 2-6. Whether Mike Macdonald and Seattle’s defense can apply enough pressure to prevent the dual-threat quarterback from utlizing his legs will likely impact the momentum and possibly, the final outcome. Regardless, they’re one of the best offenses in the league, and if the Seahawks is forced to play from behind, it would hurt having Shaheed sidelined and potentially running back Zach Charbonnet (knee) as well—who was downgraded to a limited participant at Friday’s practice. Outside of Shaheed and Charbonnet, linebacker Uchenna Nwosu (ankle), offensive tackle Charles Cross (ankle), running back Velus Jones Jr. (hamstring), and offensive guard Anthony Bradford (knee) were all non-participants in Friday’s practice. Cross’ absence isn’t surprising considering he was diagnosed with a high ankle sprain on Monday and is expected to miss time but it appears Seattle could possibly be without additional reinforcements against Chicago. A staple on Macdonald’s defense, it’ll be worth monitoring whether Nwosu is assigned an injury designation on Sunday. Linebacker Tyrice Knight (hip), quarterback Drew Lock (right elbow) and Byron Murphy II (back) practiced in a limited capacity on Friday, so it’ll be worth monitoring their status’ leading up to kickoff as well. Considering the Bears have won both of their primetime matchups this season and the Seahawks are likely to be without numerous starters, a multi-possession victory for the home side appears unlikely—even though it generated 52% of votes. However, given the nature of Seattle’s win over Kansas City, it’d be a disservice to count them out in any capacity. The Seahawks are currently 3-point favorites on FanDuel and with questions hovering over both teams, a narrow, one-possession victory appears to be the most plausible heading into the weekend—although Seattle’s injury designations will likely provide a clearer picture. By the way, confidence is high among the fanbase once again. Check out FanDuel , the official sportsbook partner of SB Nation.
